definition_zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；人物描绘
definition_en: a painting, drawing or photograph of a person, especially of the face, or a description that captures someone's character
core_image: 一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，眼神却继续朝外看
scene: 摄影棚里，摄影师请她略微转头，让光落在颧骨上。 The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
sceneCN: 这里 portrait 指「人像照片」（第 2 个义项：以相机拍摄的人物肖像）；句意为摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；文字描绘；（纸张的）竖幅

derivatives.zh: portray + -al（名词后缀）→ 描绘出的形象；从「再现动作」转到「产出的形象」
portrait + -ist（从业者）→ 肖像画家；从「作品」转到「作者」
portrait + -ure（行为或结果）→ 肖像画艺术；从「单件」转到「整个实践」
self- + portrait → 自画像；从「他人肖像」转到「自我再现」

senses.title: A painted or drawn image of a person
senses.definition: a painting or drawing representing a person, especially the face
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人、尤以面部为主的绘画或素描
senses.example: The portrait shows a merchant holding a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像画着一位手持信件的商人。
senses.why: Portrait began as a noun from the verb 'to draw forth'; the drawn likeness of a person is the core that all other senses extend.
senses.whyCN: portrait 最初是动词「拉出、描绘」的名词化；一个人的被描绘形象是其余义项所扩展的核心。

senses.title: A photographic likeness
senses.definition: a photograph of a person, usually posed and framed
senses.definitionCN: 通常经过摆拍与取景的人物照片
senses.example: The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光。
senses.why: When photography arrived, the old word for a drawn likeness transferred to the camera: the medium changed, the social function did not.
senses.whyCN: 摄影出现后，旧有的「绘制形象」一词转到相机上：媒介变了，社会功能没变。

senses.title: A description in words
senses.definition: a literary description that captures a person's appearance and character
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中捕捉一个人外貌与性格的描写
senses.example: The novel opens with a portrait of the aunt at her piano.
senses.exampleCN: 小说开篇是姑妈坐在钢琴前的一幅文字肖像。
senses.why: The metaphor 'portrait in words' treats language as a surface that can hold a likeness, an extension recorded in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 「文字中的肖像」这一隐喻把语言当作能承载形象的表面，这一扩展在 18 世纪有记录。

senses.title: A filmic depiction of a place or group
senses.titleCN: 影视对地点或群体的描绘
senses.definition: a film or television work that depicts a place, community or period in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入描绘一个地点、群体或时期的电影或电视作品
senses.example: The documentary is a portrait of a fishing town in decline.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片是一个衰落渔港的肖像。
senses.why: The sense widens from a person to any subject treated as a character: a place can be given a face by a film.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人扩展到任何被当作角色处理的对象：一部影片可以给一个地方一张脸。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.titleCN: 艺术史中的肖像画门类
senses.definition: the genre of portraiture as classified in art history
senses.definitionCN: 艺术史分类中的肖像画门类
senses.example: Portrait was ranked below history painting in the academy.
senses.exampleCN: 在学院体系里，肖像画的等级低于历史画。
senses.why: A kind of work becomes a genre, so the noun can name the category rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 一类作品会变成一个门类，因此这个名词能命名类别，而非单件作品。

senses.title: A likeness in any medium
senses.titleCN: 任何媒介中的相似形象
senses.definition: a representation of a person's appearance in any medium
senses.definitionCN: 在任何媒介中对一个人外貌的再现
senses.example: The coin bears a portrait in low relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚钱币上有浅浮雕肖像。
senses.why: Once the word means 'likeness', the material is free: paint, stone, metal and pixels can all carry a portrait.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词义是「相似形象」，材料就不受限制：颜料、石头、金属与像素都能承载肖像。

senses.title: Vertical page or screen format
senses.definition: the upright orientation of a page, photograph or screen
senses.definitionCN: 页面、照片或屏幕的竖直方向
senses.example: Switch the page to portrait before printing.
senses.exampleCN: 打印前把页面改成竖幅。
senses.why: A portrait painting is typically taller than it is wide, so the format inherited the name of its usual subject.
senses.whyCN: 肖像画通常高大于宽，因此这种版式继承了其常见题材的名称。

senses.title: A sculpted head or bust
senses.definition: a sculpted head or bust representing a person
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人的雕塑头部或胸像
senses.example: A marble portrait of the founder stands in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一尊创始人的大理石胸像立在大厅里。
senses.why: Sculpture adopts the word because the aim is still a recognisable person, even when the medium is stone rather than paint.
senses.whyCN: 雕塑采用这个词，因为目标仍是可辨认的个人，即使媒介是石头而非颜料。

intro.en: Portrait came into English in the sixteenth century from French, ultimately from Latin protrahere 'to draw forth'; it is a doublet of portray. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portrait 于 16 世纪从法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」；它与 portray 是同源双重词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere meant 'to draw forth, drag out, reveal'; it joined pro- 'forth' to trahere 'to draw, drag'.
items.cn: protrahere 意为「拉出、拖出、显露」，由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉、拖」组合。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray', literally 'to trace forth'; medieval Latin also used protrahere for painting.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」，字面是「向前描出」；中世纪拉丁也用 protrahere 指绘画。

items.en: Old French portret, the past participle of portraire used as a noun, named a drawn or painted figure.
items.cn: 古法语 portret 是 portraire 的过去分词名词化，指被绘制的人物形象。

items.en: English portrait is recorded in the 1560s as 'a figure drawn or painted', a back-formation from portraiture or a direct borrowing from French.
items.cn: 英语 portrait 于 16 世纪 60 年代有记录，指「被绘制的人物形象」，或由 portraiture 逆构，或直接借自法语。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the head and face represented from life, which became the central everyday meaning.
items.cn: 词义收窄到写生表现的头部与面部，这成为日常核心义。

items.en: Photography, film and printing extended the word to camera likenesses, depictions of places and vertical page formats.
items.cn: 摄影、电影与印刷把这个词扩展到相机拍摄的肖像、地点描绘与竖幅版式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are constantly confused with portrait; group two holds nouns for likenesses that differ in medium or scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常与 portrait 混淆的词；第二组是不同媒介或范围的人物再现名词。

entries.definition: The art of making portraits, or portraits collectively; portrait is one work.
entries.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术，或肖像总称；portrait 是一件作品。

entries.definition: To depict in a picture or words; portrait is the resulting noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在图画或文字中描绘；portrait 是结果名词。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer who specialises in portraits; the word names the person, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；这个名词指人，而非作品。

entries.definition: A portrait in which the artist depicts himself or herself; it is a compound of portrait with self.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家描绘自己的肖像；是 portrait 与 self 的复合词。

entries.definition: The quality of looking like someone, or an image that resembles them; it need not be a formal portrait.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人的性质，或相似的形象；不一定是正式肖像。

entries.definition: A general visual representation; portrait specifies that the subject is a person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指视觉再现；portrait 限定对象是人。

entries.definition: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders; portrait includes painted, photographed and full-figure works.
entries.definitionCN: 人物头肩部的雕塑；portrait 还包括绘画、摄影与全身作品。

entries.definition: A side view of a face, or a short biographical sketch; a portrait may be frontal or in profile.
entries.definitionCN: 脸的侧面，或简短生平；肖像可以是正面或侧面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin protrahere 'draw forth' gives both portrait and portray.
normal.cn: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」同时给出 portrait 与 portray。

normal.en: The noun is a past participle turned into a thing: 'the drawn-out likeness'.
normal.cn: 这个名词是过去分词变成的物件：「被拉出的形象」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: portrait painter, family portrait, portrait mode.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：肖像画家、全家福、竖屏模式。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraiture, portraitist, portray and self-portrait.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraiture、portraitist、portray 与 self-portrait。

normal.en: A page taller than wide is in portrait format because portraits usually are.
normal.cn: 高大于宽的页面叫竖幅，因为肖像通常如此。

abstract.en: Picture a face held still while its look continues to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被固定住的脸，目光却仍在移动。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that can be paper, canvas, stone or a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一种可以是纸、画布、石头或屏幕的表面。

abstract.en: Picture a likeness that survives the person it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比被描绘者活得更久的形象。

examples.en: The portrait was cleaned and the varnish removed.
examples.cn: 这幅肖像经过清洗，清漆被去掉。

examples.en: He wrote a portrait of his father that avoided sentiment.
examples.cn: 他写下一篇避免感伤的父亲肖像。

examples.en: The stamp carries a portrait engraved from a photograph.
examples.cn: 这枚邮票上有一幅依据照片雕刻的肖像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「por（向前）+ trait（拉）」——把人的样子拉出来 → 肖像

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」（pro- 向前 + trahere 拉）经古法语 portraire、过去分词 portret，16 世纪 60 年代进入英语为 portrait；与 portray 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the drawn face to the photograph, the verbal description, the filmic place, the genre, any likeness, the vertical format and the sculpted bust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从绘制的脸出发，转到照片、文字描写、影视地点、艺术门类、任何媒介的相似形象、竖幅版式与雕塑胸像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face is fixed in a pose while its gaze keeps looking outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，目光却继续朝外看。

branches.en: THE LIKENESS IN MATTER: painted or sculpted, both aim at a recognisable person.
branches.cn: 材料中的形象：绘画或雕塑，目标都是可辨认的个人。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the drawn likeness becomes a photographic one.
branches.cn: 相机：被绘制的形象变成照片。

branches.en: IN WORDS AND ON FILM: a person described, then a place given a face.
branches.cn: 文字与影片：先描写一个人，再给一个地方一张脸。

branches.en: CATEGORY AND MEDIUM: the genre, then any material that can carry it.
branches.cn: 类别与媒介：先是门类，再是任何能承载它的材料。

branches.en: FORMAT: the upright page inherits the shape of its usual subject.
branches.cn: 版式：竖幅页面继承了其常见题材的形状。

intro.en: Portrait is a Latin participle form borrowed through French; its family includes the verb of depicting and the name of the practice.
intro.cn: portrait 是经法语借入的拉丁分词形式；其词族包括描绘动词与指称这门实践的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere supply the root; the -trait ending is the French past-participle shape, not a living English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 提供词根；-trait 词尾是法语过去分词形态，不是能产的英语后缀。

items.example: The prefix contributes the sense of drawing out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀贡献「拉出」之义。

items.example: Trahere also gives tractor and trace.
items.exampleCN: trahere 还给出 tractor 与 trace。

items.example: The verb passed into English as portray.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入英语成为 portray。

items.structure: French portrait, past participle of portraire
items.example: The portrait was hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 这幅肖像挂在壁炉上方。

items.example: The novel portrays the city in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描绘冬天的城市。

items.example: Portraiture flourished at the court.
items.exampleCN: 肖像艺术在宫廷兴盛。

items.example: The portraitist worked only in pastel.
items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家只用色粉。

items.example: The self-portrait shows the artist at work.
items.exampleCN: 这幅自画像表现正在作画的艺术家。

definition_zh: 反方论点；针对某一主张提出的反对论证；文章或辩论中先摆出的对立观点
definition_en: an argument that opposes or challenges another argument, often presented before it is answered
core_image: 两个人对坐，桌上一张纸写着主张，另一张纸从对面推过来，写着相反的推论
scene: 论文写到第三段，作者先把可能反对自己的一方意见完整摆出来，再准备逐条回应。 The essay admits a strong counterargument before defending its thesis.
sceneCN: 这里指先摆出来的对立观点（第 1 个义项：反对某一主张的论证）；句意为这篇文章在为自己的论点辩护之前，先承认一个强有力的反方论点。

pos.zh: 反方论点；反对论证

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「使清楚、证明」而来的名词，义为「论证；论点」
同源动词，义为「论证；争辩」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「好争辩的；论证性的」
由拉丁语「反对」而来的前缀，义为「反；对应」
由同一前缀加「主张」构成，义为「反诉；相反主张」

senses.title: An argument that opposes a thesis
senses.definition: a set of reasons put forward to show that another argument or claim is wrong or weak
senses.definitionCN: 为表明另一论证或主张有误或站不住而提出的一组理由
senses.example: The strongest counterargument is that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 最强的反方论点是样本太小。
senses.why: Counter- adds opposition to argument, so the word names the other side of a contested claim.
senses.whyCN: 前缀给「论证」加上对立，因此这个词指有争议主张的另一面。

senses.title: The opposing case in a debate
senses.definition: the body of argument that the opposing team or speaker presents
senses.definitionCN: 对方队伍或发言人提出的整套论证
senses.example: The negative team built its counterargument around cost.
senses.exampleCN: 反方队伍围绕成本构建了它的对立论证。
senses.why: Debate is organised into sides, and each side's case is literally an argument set against the other.
senses.whyCN: 辩论分成正反两方，每一方的立论就是对着另一方摆出的论证。

senses.title: The fairness paragraph of an essay
senses.titleCN: 文章中体现公允的段落
senses.definition: the part of an essay that states the opposing view before answering it
senses.definitionCN: 文章在回应之前先陈述对立观点的部分
senses.example: A short counterargument paragraph makes the paper look fair.
senses.exampleCN: 一段简短的反方论点使文章显得公允。
senses.why: Academic writing treats the opposing view as a required move, so the word also names that paragraph.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把对立观点当作必要的一步，因此这个词也指那一段。

senses.title: A rival explanation in research
senses.definition: an alternative explanation that could account for the same observations
senses.definitionCN: 能对同一批观察给出解释的另一种说法
senses.example: The authors tested a counterargument based on weather rather than policy.
senses.exampleCN: 作者检验了一个基于天气而非政策提出的竞争性解释。
senses.why: In science the opponent is not a person but another explanation, and it must be ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 在科学里，对手不是人而是另一种解释，它必须被排除。

senses.title: A hypothetical objection used as a test
senses.titleCN: 用作检验的假想反对意见
senses.definition: an objection thought up to stress-test a claim before it is published
senses.definitionCN: 在发表之前用来压力测试某一主张而想出的反对意见
senses.example: She wrote the strongest counterargument she could imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 她写下了自己能想到的最强反方论点。
senses.why: Imagining the opposition is a method, since a claim that survives a hard objection is stronger.
senses.whyCN: 想象反对意见是一种方法，经得住严厉质疑的主张更稳固。

senses.title: The opposing legal case
senses.definition: the version of facts and law that the opposing party argues in a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 争议中对方当事人所主张的事实与法律版本
senses.example: Counsel spent the morning preparing a counterargument on jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 律师整个上午都在准备关于管辖权的反方论证。
senses.why: Litigation is an argument with consequences, and each party's case is a counterargument to the other's.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼是带后果的论证，每一方的主张都是对另一方主张的反论。

senses.title: A challenge to a policy
senses.definition: a reasoned objection to a proposed measure or official plan
senses.definitionCN: 对拟议措施或官方计划提出的有理有据的反对
senses.example: The committee heard a counterargument from the small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会听取了小企业提出的反方论证。
senses.why: Policy debate reproduces the academic form, with objections stated before decisions are taken.
senses.whyCN: 政策辩论复制了学术的形式：在作出决定前先陈述反对意见。

senses.title: A move that shows balance
senses.definition: the rhetorical act of presenting the other view so that one's own case appears measured
senses.definitionCN: 先呈现对方观点、使自己的立场显得持中的修辞动作
senses.example: The speaker opened with a counterargument to win the audience's trust.
senses.exampleCN: 发言者先抛出一个反方论点来赢得听众信任。
senses.why: Stating the other side first is a way of borrowing its credibility, which is why the move is taught explicitly.
senses.whyCN: 先讲对方一面是借取其公信力的办法，所以这一招被明确写进写作教材。

intro.en: Counterargument is a transparent compound: a Latin prefix meaning against joined to a Latin word for a reasoned argument. The word names the opposing case itself, not the answer to it.
intro.cn: 这是一个构词透明的组合：表示「反对」的拉丁前缀，加上表示「有理据的论证」的拉丁词。它指对立方的主张本身，而不是对它的回应。

items.en: Contra meant against or opposite, and it survives in English prefixes and in words such as contradict.
items.cn: 这个词意为「反对、相对」，至今保存在英语前缀以及「反驳」一类词里。

items.en: Arguere meant to make clear, to prove, and also to accuse; the proving sense fed the modern word for argument.
items.cn: 这个词意为「使清楚、证明」，也指指控；其中「证明」义喂养了现代的「论证」一词。

items.en: Argumentum named the content of a proof, and English took argument through French with the same core.
items.cn: 这个词指证明的内容，英语经法语引入「论证」，核心义相同。

items.en: Old French used contre- for opposition in compounds, and English borrowed the pattern.
items.cn: 古法语用这一前缀表示复合词中的对立，英语借用了这种构词方式。

items.en: The compound appeared in English in the nineteenth century; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十九世纪的英语中出现；确切的最早记录不确定。

items.en: Composition teaching fixed counterargument as the paragraph that states the other view, making it a classroom term.
items.cn: 写作教学把「反方论点」固定为陈述对方观点的那一段，使它成为课堂术语。

note.en: The first group shares the argument root or the opposition prefix; the second group names the answer rather than the opposing case.
note.cn: 第一组共享「论证」词根或「反对」前缀；第二组指回应，而不是对立方的主张。

entries.definition: A set of reasons offered in support of a position.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某一立场提供的一组理由。

entries.definition: To give reasons for or against something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为或反对某事给出理由。

entries.definition: A claim set against another claim, often in law.
entries.definitionCN: 指对着另一主张提出的主张，常用于法律。

entries.definition: A contrasting element; its root is a point, not an argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指形成对照的要素；词根是「点」，不是「论证」。

entries.definition: A case that disproves a general statement.
entries.definitionCN: 指推翻一般性陈述的反例。

entries.definition: To meet unexpectedly; it looks like counter but comes from a meeting prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指意外相遇；形似却来自表示相遇的前缀。

entries.definition: The answer that tries to disprove the opposing argument, not the opposing argument itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指试图驳倒对方论证的回应，而不是对方论证本身。

entries.definition: A stated reason for opposing something, often shorter than a full argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指反对某事的理由，通常比完整论证短。

entries.definition: The act of proving an argument false.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明某论证为假的行为。

entries.definition: The position held by those who disagree, stated without the full reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同意者的立场，未必带完整推理。

entries.definition: A call to justify a claim, weaker than a worked-out argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求为某主张给出理由，比完整论证弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two papers facing each other, the essay paragraph and the debate side.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两张对推的纸、作文里的那一段与辩论中的一方。

normal.en: Counter means against and argument means reasons, so the word is simply the reasons against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「反对」，后一半意为「理由」，所以这个词就是「反对的理由」。

normal.en: The essay phrase is «acknowledge the counterargument», a standard move in composition.
normal.cn: 作文里的固定说法是「承认反方论点」，是写作中的标准动作。

normal.en: A counterargument is not a rebuttal: one is the punch, the other is the block.
normal.cn: 反方论点不是反驳：一个是打出的拳，一个是挡回的格。

normal.en: A counterexample is a single case; a counterargument is a whole case against you.
normal.cn: 反例是一个事例，反方论点则是整套反对你的理由。

normal.en: In debate the negative team's whole case can be called the counterargument.
normal.cn: 在辩论中，反方队伍的整体立论可称为反方论点。

abstract.en: A counterargument is the shadow that proves the light exists, since a claim with no opposition is not yet a claim.
abstract.cn: 反方论点是证明光存在的影子，因为无人反对的主张还称不上主张。

abstract.en: Arguing against yourself is the cheapest way to find out what you actually believe.
abstract.cn: 与自己争辩，是弄清自己真正相信什么的最省力的办法。

abstract.en: Every strong case carries its opponent inside it from the beginning.
abstract.cn: 每个强立论从一开始就把对手装在自己体内。

examples.en: The paper addresses the main counterargument in a single paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇论文用一段回应了主要的反方论点。

examples.en: Ignoring a counterargument makes a proposal look weak.
examples.cn: 忽视反方论点会让提案显得薄弱。

examples.en: She offered a counterargument based on the cost of the scheme.
examples.cn: 她基于该方案的成本提出了一个反方论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「反」加「论证」：对着你的主张推回来的那套理由，就是反方论点

root: 前缀来自拉丁语 contra「反对、相对」；后一半来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明的内容」，其动词 arguere 意为「使清楚、证明」。古法语用对立前缀构词，英语借用；复合词在十九世纪出现，写作教学在二十世纪把它固定为「陈述对方观点的那一段」。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the claim to the classroom: an opposing argument, a debate side, the fairness paragraph, a rival explanation, a hypothetical test, the legal case, a policy challenge, and a balancing move.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从主张延伸到课堂：反对论证、辩论一方、公允段落、竞争性解释、假想检验、法律主张、政策质疑、平衡姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sheets of paper travel toward each other across a table, each carrying reasons against the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张纸在桌面上相互推近，各自写着反对对方的理由。

branches.en: THE OPPOSING CASE: reasons set against a claim, whether in writing or in debate.
branches.cn: 对立的主张：对着某一论点摆出的理由，无论书面还是辩论。

branches.en: THE FAIRNESS MOVE: stating the other view first so one's own case looks measured.
branches.cn: 公允之举：先讲对方观点，使自己的立场显得持中。

branches.en: THE RIVAL EXPLANATION: another account of the same facts, waiting to be ruled out.
branches.cn: 竞争性解释：对同一批事实的另一说法，等着被排除。

branches.en: THE SELF-TEST: an objection invented to try to break one's own claim.
branches.cn: 自我检验：为击破自身主张而想出的反对意见。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE ARENA: the legal case and the policy objection.
branches.cn: 外部场域：法律上的对方主张与政策质疑。

intro.en: Counterargument is a compound of a Latin opposition prefix and a Latin argument word, and neither half has changed meaning.
intro.cn: 这个词组由拉丁语的对立前缀与论证词构成，两半的含义都没有改变。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies contra and argumentum; English supplies the combining habit that made them one word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「反对」与「论证」，英语提供了把它们合成一个词的构词习惯。

senses.title: A confident statement of fact
senses.definition: a firm statement that something is true, made without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 毫不迟疑地断定某事为真的陈述
senses.example: Her assertion that the test had failed was later confirmed.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于测试失败的那句断言后来得到证实。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to claim as one's own, and a claim made firmly becomes a statement of fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「认作自己的」，坚定地认领就成了一种事实陈述。

senses.title: A claim open to challenge
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true that others may reasonably dispute
senses.definitionCN: 被提出为真、但他人可以合理反驳的陈述
senses.example: The report's central assertion has no data behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的核心主张背后没有数据。
senses.why: Anything asserted invites a counter-statement, so the word often marks a claim still awaiting proof.
senses.whyCN: 凡是断言都会招来反陈述，因此这个词常标出尚待证明的主张。

senses.title: A declaration of rights
senses.definition: the act of stating or defending a right, title or claim
senses.definitionCN: 声明或维护某项权利、名分或主张的行为
senses.example: The march was an assertion of the right to assemble.
senses.exampleCN: 那场游行是对集会权利的一次声明。
senses.why: Rights are claimed before they are used, and the word covers that public claiming.
senses.whyCN: 权利在被使用之前先被主张，这个词覆盖这种公开主张。

senses.title: A proposition affirmed in logic
senses.definition: a proposition that is put forward as true and from which inferences may follow
senses.definitionCN: 被提出为真、并可据以推出结论的命题
senses.example: In the proof, each assertion must follow from the one before.
senses.exampleCN: 在证明中，每个命题都必须由前一个推出。
senses.why: Logic treats an assertion as a statement with a truth value, which is a formal version of claiming.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把断言看作有真值的陈述，这是「主张」的形式化版本。

senses.title: An assertion in a program
senses.definition: a statement in code that declares a condition which must be true at that point
senses.definitionCN: 代码中声明某条件在该处必须为真的语句
senses.example: The developer added an assertion to catch empty input.
senses.exampleCN: 开发者在代码里加了一个断言，用来捕获空输入。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the word because a check asserts that a condition holds, and fails loudly if it does not.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用这个词，因为检查是在断言某条件成立，不成立就大声报错。

senses.title: A forceful expression of opinion
senses.definition: a confident way of saying what one thinks, often in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以自信的方式说出自己的想法，常见于口头表达
senses.example: His assertion that the plan was hopeless silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句计划毫无希望的说法让全场安静下来。
senses.why: Tone matters here: the noun can name the force of a statement as much as its content.
senses.whyCN: 语气在这里很关键：这个名词既指内容，也指说话的力度。

senses.title: An assertion of authority
senses.definition: the act of showing or enforcing one's power or control
senses.definitionCN: 展示或强行施加自身权力与控制的行为
senses.example: The new manager's first meeting was an assertion of control.
senses.exampleCN: 新任经理的第一次会议是一次掌控权的宣示。
senses.why: Power is often claimed before it is obeyed, and the word names that claim.
senses.whyCN: 权力常在被服从之前先被主张，这个词就指那种主张。

senses.title: A statement made without proof
senses.definition: a statement offered as true although no evidence has been supplied
senses.definitionCN: 虽无证据却作为真实提出的陈述
senses.example: The essay opens with an assertion rather than a finding.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以一个断言而不是发现开头。
senses.why: Because the word does not itself guarantee proof, it can politely name something unproven.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本身不保证有证明，它可以客气地指称未经证实的东西。

intro.en: Assertion comes from Latin asserere, to claim or maintain, literally to join something to oneself. The noun entered English through French and kept both the sense of a firm statement and the sense of defending a right.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 asserere「主张、维护」，字面意为「把某物接到自己身上」。名词经法语进入英语，既保留「坚定陈述」的意思，也保留「维护权利」的意思。

items.en: Serere meant to join or arrange in a row, and it also gave the words for series and insert.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「连接、排成行」，也表示「系列」与「插入」的词也出自它。

items.en: With the prefix ad-, the verb meant to join to oneself, hence to claim a thing as one's own and defend it.
items.cn: 加上表示「朝向」的前缀后，动词意为「接到自己身上」，因而指把某物认作自己的并加以维护。

items.en: Roman law used the verb for asserting freedom or a right, and English kept that public, declarative force.
items.cn: 罗马法用这个动词表示主张自由或权利，英语保留了这种公开宣告的力量。

items.en: The noun assertion appeared in English writing on logic and law; its exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词「断言」在十五世纪的逻辑与法律写作中出现；确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: Grammar calls a positive statement an assertive sentence, and logic treats assertions as propositions with truth values.
items.cn: 语法学把肯定陈述称为断言句，逻辑学把断言当作有真值的命题。

items.en: Programming languages adopted assertion for a condition the program declares must hold at a given point.
items.cn: 编程语言采用这个词，指程序声明在某处必须成立的条件。

note.en: The first group shares the joining root or looks similar; the second group names statements and claims of other strengths.
note.cn: 第一组共享「连接」词根或形近；第二组指力度不同的陈述与主张。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to state firmly or to defend a right.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚定陈述或维护权利的动词。

entries.definition: Confident and direct in stating one's views.
entries.definitionCN: 指陈述观点时自信直接的。

entries.definition: The quality of standing up for oneself calmly and directly.
entries.definitionCN: 指平静而直接地维护自身立场的品质。

entries.definition: To put something inside; same joining root, inward prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物放入；与断言共享「连接」词根，前缀向内。

entries.definition: To abandon; the prefix means apart, so the joining is undone.
entries.definitionCN: 指抛弃；前缀意为「分开」，即把连接解开。

entries.definition: Capable of being asserted as true.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以被断言为真的。

entries.definition: A statement that something is true, often one not yet proved.
entries.definitionCN: 指声称某事为真，常指尚未证明的说法。

entries.definition: A formal public statement, stronger in official weight than in proof.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式的公开声明，官方分量重于证明。

entries.definition: The neutral word for something said or written.
entries.definitionCN: 指说出或写下的内容，是中性的说法。

entries.definition: A point argued in a debate or essay.
entries.definitionCN: 指辩论或文章中提出的论点。

entries.definition: A positive statement that something is true, often in law or religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指肯定某事为真的陈述，常用于法律或宗教。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the stamp picture, the legal claim of a right and the programming statement.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用盖章的画面、对权利的法律主张以及程序中的断言语句。

normal.en: To assert is to claim something as one's own, which is why the word can mean both saying and defending.
normal.cn: 断言就是把某物认作自己的，所以这个词既能指说出，也能指维护。

normal.en: An assertion is a stamp pressed down: the mark is made before anyone can argue with it.
normal.cn: 断言是按下的一枚印章：印痕在别人反驳之前就已经留下。

normal.en: Assertive speech is confident speech, and assertiveness training teaches people to state needs plainly.
normal.cn: 断言式说话就是自信的说话，「自信训练」教人把需求讲清楚。

normal.en: In code, an assertion is a promise that a condition holds, and a failed assertion stops the program.
normal.cn: 在代码里，断言是「某条件成立」的承诺，断言失败会中止程序。

normal.en: Assertion of rights is a fixed legal phrase, showing that the word kept its declarative legal force.
normal.cn: 「权利的主张」是固定法律说法，说明这个词保留了宣告式的法律力量。

abstract.en: An assertion is a claim wearing the clothes of a fact, and the clothes are what listeners must see through.
abstract.cn: 断言是一个穿着事实外衣的主张，而听众要做的正是看穿这件外衣。

abstract.en: Every field has its own way of stamping: logic stamps truth values, law stamps rights, code stamps conditions.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都有自己的盖章方式：逻辑盖真值，法律盖权利，代码盖条件。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that before evidence arrives, all we have is someone standing behind a sentence.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们，在证据到来之前，我们只有某个人站在一句话后面。

examples.en: The author's assertion about rising costs is supported by three surveys.
examples.cn: 作者关于成本上升的断言得到三项调查的支持。

examples.en: No one could disprove his assertion that the method was safe.
examples.cn: 没有人能反驳他关于该方法安全的断言。

examples.en: The code contains an assertion that the list is never empty.
examples.cn: 这段代码里有一个断言，声明该列表永不为空。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从言语行为延伸到代码：自信陈述、可质疑的主张、权利声明、逻辑命题、程序断言、有力的意见、权威的彰显、无证明的陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal is pressed hard onto paper, and the mark stays after the hand lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章重重压上纸面，手抬起后印痕仍在。

branches.en: THE STAMPED SENTENCE: a firm statement that may or may not have proof behind it.
branches.cn: 盖章的句子：坚定的陈述，背后未必有证明。

branches.en: THE OPEN CLAIM: a statement that invites others to dispute it.
branches.cn: 敞开的主张：招来他人反驳的陈述。

branches.en: THE CLAIMED RIGHT: a right declared in public, and power shown by assertion.
branches.cn: 被主张的权利：公开宣告的权利，以及以断言彰显的权力。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL PROPOSITION: a statement carrying a truth value.
branches.cn: 逻辑命题：带有真值的陈述。

branches.en: THE CODE CHECK AND THE FORCEFUL TONE: a condition declared in code, and the weight of confident speech.
branches.cn: 代码检查与有力语气：在代码中声明的条件，以及自信说话的重量。

senses.definition: connected with the making or applying of rules that govern an activity
senses.definitionCN: 与制定或适用管理某项活动的规则有关
senses.example: The regulatory system for food additives is complex.
senses.exampleCN: 食品添加剂的规章体系很复杂。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ory to regulator, so it describes whatever belongs to the work of ruling by rules.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由 regulator 加 -ory 构成，描述属于「依规则治理」工作的事物。

senses.title: Of an oversight body
senses.titleCN: 监管机构的：指负责监督的机关
senses.definition: describing an official body whose job is to supervise and enforce rules in a sector
senses.definitionCN: 形容负责监督并执行某行业规则的官方机构
senses.example: The regulatory agency approved the drug after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构经两年审查后批准了该药物。
senses.why: Institutions need a label for themselves: an agency that regulates is regulatory, and the adjective becomes part of its name.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要给自身一个标签：负责监管的机关就是 regulatory，形容词成了机构名称的一部分。

senses.title: Compliance with rules
senses.definition: describing the state of meeting the rules set by authorities
senses.definitionCN: 形容满足主管机关所设规则的状态
senses.example: Regulatory compliance costs the firm about a million dollars a year.
senses.exampleCN: 监管合规每年花掉这家公司约一百万美元。
senses.why: The adjective marks the boundary between permitted and forbidden conduct, and compliance is living inside that boundary.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记允许与禁止行为之间的边界，而合规就是生活在这条边界之内。

senses.title: Framework and approval
senses.titleCN: 框架与审批：规则体系及放行程序
senses.definition: describing the structure of rules and the formal permissions required before an activity may proceed
senses.definitionCN: 形容规则的整体结构，以及活动开始前所需的正式许可
senses.example: No product reaches the market without regulatory approval.
senses.exampleCN: 没有产品能在未获监管审批的情况下进入市场。
senses.why: A framework is the architecture of rules; approval is the gate, and the same adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 框架是规则的建筑结构，审批是闸门，同一个形容词涵盖两者。

senses.title: The cost of oversight
senses.titleCN: 监管负担：合规带来的成本
senses.definition: describing the time, money and staff that rules impose on those they govern
senses.definitionCN: 形容规则对被监管者施加的时间、金钱与人力成本
senses.example: Small firms complain about the regulatory burden.
senses.exampleCN: 小公司抱怨监管负担。
senses.why: The adjective can turn critical: what began as protection is also measured as a weight carried by business.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以转为批评：原本的保护措施也被计为企业的负担。

senses.title: Biological control elements
senses.titleCN: 生物调控元件：控制基因开关的片段
senses.definition: in genetics, describing DNA sequences or molecules that control when a gene is expressed
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学中形容控制基因何时表达的 DNA 序列或分子
senses.example: A regulatory sequence upstream of the gene binds a repressor.
senses.exampleCN: 基因上游的调控序列会结合阻遏蛋白。
senses.why: Biology uses the same adjective for the parts that regulate: the controlling function, not the rule-making institution.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用同一个形容词指执行调控的部件：是控制功能，而非制定规则的机构。

senses.title: Regulatory capture
senses.titleCN: 监管俘获：监管者被被监管者影响
senses.definition: describing the situation in which an agency comes to serve the industry it is meant to oversee
senses.definitionCN: 形容监管机构转而服务于本应被其监督的行业的情形
senses.example: Regulatory capture can turn a watchdog into a partner.
senses.exampleCN: 监管俘获可能把看门狗变成伙伴。
senses.why: The phrase names a failure of the adjective's purpose: the regulator still regulates, but in the industry's interest.
senses.whyCN: 该短语命名形容词所指目的的失败：监管者仍在监管，却是按行业利益监管。

senses.title: Cross-border coordination
senses.titleCN: 跨境监管协调：不同辖区规则对接
senses.definition: describing cooperation among countries or jurisdictions to align their rules and standards
senses.definitionCN: 形容国家或辖区之间为统一规则与标准而进行的合作
senses.example: Regulatory cooperation reduced duplicate inspections.
senses.exampleCN: 监管合作减少了重复检查。
senses.why: As trade crosses borders, the adjective extends from one agency to the relations among many.
senses.whyCN: 当贸易跨越国界，形容词便从单一机构扩展到许多机构之间的关系。

intro.en: Regulatory is an English adjective: regulator plus the ending -ory, which comes from Latin -orius. Regulator itself is regulare 'to rule' plus -or 'one who'.
intro.cn: regulatory 是英语形容词：regulator 加词尾 -ory，后者出自拉丁 -orius。regulator 本身则是 regulare「管理」加 -or「做某事的人」。

items.en: Regula 'rule, straight stick' is the base. It is generally connected with regere 'to guide straight'.
items.cn: 词基是 regula「规则、直木条」，一般认为与 regere「引直、治理」相关。

items.en: Regulare meant 'to rule, regulate'; adding -or produced regulator, 'one who regulates', used for officials and later for devices.
items.cn: regulare 意为「管理、调节」；加 -or 构成 regulator「调节者」，先用于官员，后用于装置。

items.en: The adjective suffix -orius formed words meaning 'belonging to or serving' a person or function; English -ory descends from it.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -orius 构成意为「属于或服务于某人/某功能」的词；英语 -ory 由此而来。

items.en: Regulatory appears in English in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, first in legal and administrative writing.
items.cn: regulatory 于 18 至 19 世纪出现在英语中，最早见于法律与行政文本。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it to independent agencies, compliance departments, and gene regulatory sequences.
items.cn: 20 世纪把它扩展到独立监管机构、合规部门与基因调控序列。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the relationship of regula to regere is accepted rather than fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（派生路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；regula 与 regere 的关系属于「一般认为」，并非完全有文献可证。

note.en: The first group separates the regulate family; the second gives near-synonyms for rule-making and for control.
note.cn: 第一组区分 regulate 词族；第二组给出关于规则制定与控制的近义词。

entries.definition: The rule or the act. Regulatory is the adjective placed before agency, framework or compliance.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则或动作；regulatory 是放在 agency、framework、compliance 前的形容词。

entries.definition: The institution or mechanism that regulates. Regulatory describes such a body's character.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行监管的机构或装置；regulatory 描述这类机构的性质。

entries.definition: To make or apply rules. Regulatory never functions as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指制定或适用规则；regulatory 从不用作动词。

entries.definition: Organized with rigid discipline. It is critical and has nothing to do with formal agencies.
entries.definitionCN: 指以严格纪律组织起来，带批评意味，与正式监管机构无关。

entries.definition: Relating to the running of an organization. Regulatory work is one kind of administration, focused on rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指与组织运作有关；监管工作是行政管理的一种，聚焦于规则。

entries.definition: Created or required by a formal law. Regulatory bodies are often statutory, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 指由正式法律创设或要求；监管机构常为法定机构，但两词回答的问题不同。

entries.definition: Relating to oversight of people or work. Supervision may be internal, while regulatory usually implies public authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指对人员或工作的监督；监督可以是内部的，而 regulatory 通常暗示公共权威。

entries.definition: Having power over something. It is broader and more forceful than regulatory, which works through rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物拥有控制权，范围更广、语气更强；regulatory 则通过规则运作。

entries.definition: The activity of enforcing order. It stresses detection and enforcement more than rule design.
entries.definitionCN: 指维持秩序的执法活动，更强调发现与执行，而非规则设计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: regulator + -ory: belonging to the work of ruling by rules.
normal.cn: regulator + -ory：属于「依规则治理」的工作。

normal.en: The family runs regulate, regulation, regulator, deregulation, self-regulatory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 regulate、regulation、regulator、deregulation、self-regulatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: regulatory agency, regulatory framework, regulatory compliance, regulatory burden.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：监管机构、监管框架、监管合规、监管负担。

normal.en: regulatory capture names the watchdog that ends up serving the industry.
normal.cn: 监管俘获指看门狗最终反过来服务行业。

normal.en: In genetics, a regulatory sequence switches a gene on or off.
normal.cn: 遗传学中，调控序列开关基因。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with a clipboard beside it, where every truck must show its papers.
abstract.cn: 想象一道大门旁放着记录板，每辆卡车都要出示文件。

abstract.en: Picture a switch upstream of a lamp, deciding whether the lamp can light at all.
abstract.cn: 想象灯的上游有个开关，决定灯能否亮起。

abstract.en: Picture a watchdog slowly being fed by the same hand it was meant to guard against.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看门狗慢慢被它本该防着的那只手喂养。

examples.en: Regulatory approval for the new aircraft took four years.
examples.cn: 新飞机的监管审批用了四年。

examples.en: The company hired a regulatory affairs team before launch.
examples.cn: 公司在上市前组建了监管事务团队。

examples.en: A regulatory sequence can silence a gene without changing its code.
examples.cn: 调控序列可以在不改变基因编码的情况下使其沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「regulator（监管者）+ y」——带着规章来管 → regulatory 监管的

root: 拉丁 regula「规则」→ regulare「管理」→ regulator「监管者」+ -ory（形容词后缀）→ regulatory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show the adjective spreading from a rule, to an agency, to compliance, approval, cost, genes, capture and cross-border cooperation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展示该形容词的扩展：从一条规则，到机构、合规、审批、成本、基因、俘获与跨境合作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clipboard gate where every truck must show papers.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录板旁的大门，每辆卡车都要出示文件。

branches.en: RULES AND BODIES: the rule system itself, and the agency that administers it.
branches.cn: 规则与机构：规则体系本身，以及执行它的机构。

branches.en: THE GATE: compliance inside the boundary, and approval before entry.
branches.cn: 闸门：边界之内的合规，以及进入之前的审批。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: the same protection is also a cost carried by the regulated.
branches.cn: 负担：同一保护措施也成为被监管者承担的成本。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: the controlling part of a gene, not a controlling institution.
branches.cn: 生物学：基因的调控部件，而非监管机构。

branches.en: FAILURE AND SCALE: the watchdog may be captured, and rules must meet across borders.
branches.cn: 失败与尺度：看门狗可能被俘获，规则还须跨境对接。

intro.en: Regulatory stacks an agent noun and an adjective ending: regulate, regulator, then -ory, from Latin -orius.
intro.cn: regulatory 叠加了施动名词与形容词词尾：regulate、regulator，再加出自拉丁 -orius 的 -ory。

latinIntro.en: The regula family supplies rule, regular, regulate, regulator, regulation, regime and regiment; each keeps the image of a straight line or a fixed order.
latinIntro.cn: regula 词族提供 rule、regular、regulate、regulator、regulation、regime、regiment，每个词都保留直线或固定秩序的意象。

items.meaningCN: 属于规则制定或控制的
items.example: Regulatory oversight increased after the accident.
items.exampleCN: 事故之后监管监督加强了。

items.example: The state regulates the sale of alcohol.
items.exampleCN: 国家监管酒类销售。

items.meaning: a rule; the act of regulating
items.example: The regulation limits sulfur in fuel.
items.exampleCN: 该规章限制燃料中的硫含量。

items.meaning: an official body or device that regulates
items.meaningCN: 进行监管的机构或装置
items.example: The regulator published its findings.
items.exampleCN: 监管机构公布了调查结果。

items.example: Regular inspections keep the plant safe.
items.exampleCN: 定期检查保障工厂安全。

items.example: The press adopted a self-regulatory code.
items.exampleCN: 新闻界通过了自我监管守则。

items.example: The deregulatory package passed easily.
items.exampleCN: 放松监管方案轻松通过。

items.example: The tax regime favours small firms.
items.exampleCN: 该税制偏向小公司。

definition_zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平
definition_en: the variety of living organisms and the ecological systems they form, measured at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels
core_image: 同一片森林里，每一层都长着不同的生命
scene: 这座岛与大陆隔开千万年，物种因此自成一套。 The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity, with species found nowhere else on Earth.
sceneCN: 这里 biodiversity 是「生物多样性」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的物种多样性）；句意：这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性，有些物种在地球上别处都找不到。场景要点：海岛、多层的热带植被、不同种类的鸟与昆虫、记录表、望远镜。

pos.zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平

collocations.zh: 生物多样性补偿（生态补偿机制）

derivatives.zh: 生物多样的
农业生物多样性
生物多样性极高的（用于 megadiverse countries）

senses.title: Species diversity in a place
senses.titleCN: 物种多样性：一个地区有多少种生物
senses.definition: the variety and number of species living in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区内物种的多样程度和数量
senses.example: The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性。
senses.why: bio- supplies 'life' and diversity supplies 'turned different ways'. The first sense counts how many kinds of living thing share a place: difference among organisms is the core of the word, and species are the easiest differences to see.
senses.whyCN: bio- 提供“生命”，diversity 提供“转向各方”。第一个义项数的是一个地方共享着多少种生物：生物之间的差异是这个词的核心，而物种是最容易看见的差异。

senses.title: Genetic diversity within a species
senses.titleCN: 遗传多样性：同一物种内部的基因差异
senses.definition: the variation in genes among individuals of the same species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的基因差异
senses.example: Small populations lose biodiversity at the genetic level even before species disappear.
senses.exampleCN: 小种群在物种消失之前，就已经在遗传层面失去生物多样性。
senses.why: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity defined the term at three levels, and the first extension went inward: variety does not stop between species, it continues among individuals and their genes. A species is itself a pool of differences.
senses.whyCN: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》把该词定义为三个层次，第一次延伸是向内走：多样性并不止于物种之间，它继续存在于个体及其基因之间。一个物种本身就是一池差异。

senses.title: Ecosystem and habitat diversity
senses.titleCN: 生态系统与生境多样性
senses.definition: the variety of ecosystems, habitats, and ecological communities in a region
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区内生态系统、生境与生态群落的多样程度
senses.example: Wetlands, forest and coral reef add ecosystem biodiversity to the same region.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地、森林与珊瑚礁为同一地区增加了生态系统多样性。
senses.why: The third level steps outward: not the organisms but the kinds of place and the communities they form. Difference now applies to habitats, so the same word covers a forest, a marsh and a reef.
senses.whyCN: 第三个层次向外走：不是生物本身，而是地方的类型以及它们形成的群落。差异这时适用于生境，于是同一个词覆盖森林、沼泽与珊瑚礁。

senses.title: The measured level: high or low
senses.titleCN: 多样性水平：可高可低的量
senses.definition: the measured degree of variety in a place, which can be high, low, or declining
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方多样性的可测程度，可高、可低或正在下降
senses.example: The survey recorded low biodiversity in the polluted stretch of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到河流受污染河段的生物多样性很低。
senses.why: Once a quantity can be counted, it can be compared. Diversity stops being a bare fact and becomes a scale — high, low, rich, poor — which is what field surveys actually report.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可以计数，就可以比较。多样性不再是单纯的事实，而变成一把刻度——高、低、丰富、贫乏——这正是野外调查实际报告的内容。

senses.title: Loss of biodiversity
senses.definition: the decline or disappearance of biological variety, usually through human pressure
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性程度的下降或消失，通常由人类压力造成
senses.example: Habitat clearance is the leading cause of biodiversity loss worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 栖息地清除是世界范围内生物多样性丧失的首要原因。
senses.why: A scale that can fall invites the noun 'loss'. The word now names a public problem, not only a property of a place; conservation supplies the negative frame, and loss becomes the standard collocation.
senses.whyCN: 一个会下跌的刻度自然引出“丧失”这个名词。这个词现在命名的是一种公共问题，而不只是某地的属性；保护话语提供了负面框架，loss 于是成为标准搭配。

senses.title: Conservation hotspot
senses.titleCN: 保护热点：多样性极高又受威胁的地区
senses.definition: a region with exceptionally high biodiversity that is under serious threat
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性异常高、同时面临严重威胁的地区
senses.example: The mountain range is recognised as a global biodiversity hotspot.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉被认定为全球生物多样性热点地区。
senses.why: Where diversity is high and threatened, attention concentrates. Hotspot is the spatial form of that concentration: a place worth naming, mapping and funding, so the word becomes an argument for protection.
senses.whyCN: 在多样性高又受威胁的地方，注意力会集中。hotspot 就是这种集中的空间形态：一个值得命名、绘图和投入资金的地方，于是这个词本身成了一种保护理由。

senses.title: Agricultural biodiversity
senses.titleCN: 农业生物多样性：作物与家畜品种的多样
senses.definition: the variety of crops, livestock breeds, and associated organisms used in farming
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的作物、家畜品种及相关生物的多样性
senses.example: Traditional farms preserve agricultural biodiversity that monocultures lose.
senses.exampleCN: 传统农场保存着单一种植所丧失的农业生物多样性。
senses.why: Humans select plants and animals, so variety also exists among breeds and crop varieties. The compound widens 'life' from wild organisms to cultivated ones, and the word becomes a measure of food-system resilience.
senses.whyCN: 人类对动植物进行选择，所以品种与作物之间也存在多样性。这个复合词把“生命”从野生生物扩展到栽培生物，于是该词成为衡量食物系统韧性的一项指标。

senses.title: Biodiversity as a global commons
senses.titleCN: 作为全球公共资源的生物多样性
senses.definition: biodiversity treated as a shared resource and a subject of international law and policy
senses.definitionCN: 被当作共享资源、并成为国际法与政策对象的生物多样性
senses.example: The treaty treats biodiversity as a common concern of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约把生物多样性视为人类的共同关切。
senses.why: Because genes, species and habitats cross borders, the noun was lifted from ecology into international law. The 1992 Convention made it the name of a shared resource, and the word acquired a political subject as well as an ecological one.
senses.whyCN: 由于基因、物种与生境都跨越国界，这个名词从生态学被提升到国际法。1992 年公约使它成为一种共享资源的名称，这个词于是既有生态学主体，也有政治主体。

senses.title: Diversity in managed or urban land
senses.titleCN: 城市与人工生境中的生物多样性
senses.definition: biological variety measured in cities, restored land, and other human-managed landscapes
senses.definitionCN: 在城市、修复地及其他人类管理景观中测得的生物多样性
senses.example: Green roofs and city parks can raise urban biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色屋顶与城市公园可以提升城市生物多样性。
senses.why: The last extension drops the wilderness assumption: diversity is measured wherever life persists, including cities and restored land. The word becomes a planning target rather than a description of untouched nature.
senses.whyCN: 最后一次延伸丢掉了“荒野”预设：凡有生命存续之处都可测多样性，包括城市与修复地。这个词于是从“未受触及的自然之描述”变成一项规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is not an inherited word. It is a 20th-century scientific compound, clipped from the phrase biological diversity: bio- is Greek, diversity is Latin, and the two were joined in modern English. The earliest written record is disputed.
intro.cn: biodiversity 不是承袭来的词，而是 20 世纪的科学复合词，由短语 biological diversity 截短而成：bio- 是希腊语，diversity 是拉丁语，两者在现代英语里被拼在一起。最早的书面记录存疑。

items.en: bios means 'one's life, course or way of living, lifetime', as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. It comes from PIE *gwei- 'to live'. In English bio- has been used in scientific compounds since about 1800 for 'organic life', though biography keeps the older 'life-story' sense.
items.cn: bios 意为“一个人的生命、生活历程、寿命”，与 zoē“动物生命”相对，来自原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”。英语自约 1800 年起用 bio- 构成科学复合词，表示“有机生命”，但 biography 仍保留更古老的“生平故事”义。

items.en: divertere 'to turn apart' is dis- 'apart' + vertere 'to turn'. Its past participle diversus means 'turned different ways', and diversitas gives 'difference, variety'. English diversity (mid-14c) came through Old French diversete.
items.cn: divertere“转开”是 dis-“分开”+ vertere“转”。其过去分词 diversus 意为“转向各方的”，名词 diversitas 表示“差异、多样”。英语 diversity（14 世纪中）经由古法语 diversete 而来。

items.en: The full phrase was used in ecology and conservation from the 1970s–80s for variety at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. It is a descriptive phrase built from existing words, not a classical term with an ancient pedigree.
items.cn: 完整短语 biological diversity 在 20 世纪 70—80 年代的生态学与保护生物学中用来指基因、物种、生态系统三个层次的多样性。它是由现有词构成的描述性短语，不是有古老传承的经典术语。

items.en: Etymonline dates biodiversity 'by 1988'. The clipped form is often credited to W. G. Rosen in conference material around 1985–86, later printed in 1988; the exact first written use and the first coiner are disputed, and sources differ. Treat the date as approximate.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 biodiversity 记作“by 1988”。这个截短形式常被归到 W. G. Rosen 在 1985—86 年前后的会议材料，后来于 1988 年付印；最早的书面使用与首创者都有争议，各家资料不一。年代只能作大致估计。

items.era: WHY IT IS NOT AN OLD WORD
items.en: There is no Latin biodiversitas and no Greek compound of this shape. The word was built from a living prefix and a living noun to fill a gap in ecology, so its structure stays transparent in a way inherited words are not.
items.cn: 并不存在拉丁语 biodiversitas，也没有这种形状的希腊语复合词。这个词是用活的前缀加活的名词造出来填补生态学的空缺，因此它的结构保持着承袭词所没有的透明性。

items.en: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity fixed the three-level definition and turned the word into a legal and policy term. Later compounds — hotspot, offset, agrobiodiversity — extend it outward from ecology into planning, finance and agriculture.
items.cn: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》确定了三层定义，把这个词变成法律与政策术语。后来的复合词——hotspot、offset、agrobiodiversity——又把它从生态学向外扩展到规划、金融与农业。

note.en: The first group contains the words and phrases most often mistaken for biodiversity itself; the second contains measures of living variety that differ in what they actually count.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误当成 biodiversity 本身的词与短语；第二组是衡量生命多样性的指标，但各自实际计数的对象不同。

entries.definition: Variety or difference in general. It can describe people, ideas, or tastes; only the bio- prefix makes it about living organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指多样或差异，可指人、想法、口味；只有加上 bio- 才专指生物。

entries.definition: The longer, formal phrase from which biodiversity was clipped. It is the safer term in legal and scientific writing and covers the same three levels.
entries.definitionCN: biodiversity 由之截短而来的较长正式短语。在法律与科学写作中更稳妥，涵盖同样的三个层次。

entries.definition: The total mass of living matter. It shares bio- but measures amount, while biodiversity measures difference.
entries.definitionCN: 活物质的总质量。它共享 bio-，但衡量的是数量，而 biodiversity 衡量的是差异。

entries.definition: A written life of a person, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. It looks like a bio- word but has nothing to do with ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 人物传记，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。它看起来像 bio- 词，却与生态学无关。

entries.definition: The quality of differing in form or type. Everyday and unmeasured, with no ecological definition behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 形式或类型上存在差异的性质。日常用语，不可量化，背后没有生态学定义。

entries.definition: The number of species in a place. It counts only species, whereas biodiversity also includes genetic and ecosystem variety.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的物种数目。它只数物种，而 biodiversity 还包括遗传与生态系统层面的多样。

entries.definition: The number of individuals of a species. More individuals is not more diversity; a field of one crop can have high abundance and low biodiversity.
entries.definitionCN: 某一物种的个体数量。个体多并不等于多样性高；一块单一种植的田可以个体数量很高而生物多样性很低。

entries.definition: Unevenness in composition or structure across space. It is a measurement of pattern, not the variety of life itself.
entries.definitionCN: 组成或结构在空间上的不均匀。它是格局的度量，而不是生命本身的多样。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek prefix, the real Latin noun, and the real three-level definition.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊前缀、真实的拉丁名词，以及真实的三层定义。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + diversity 'turned apart': life turned into many different forms.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ diversity“转向各方”：生命被分成许多不同的形态。

normal.en: Three levels: genes → species → ecosystems. The word covers all three, and most exam questions test only the first.
normal.cn: 三个层次：基因 → 物种 → 生态系统。这个词覆盖三层，而多数考题只考第一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. The second half of each word tells you what is measured.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量的是数量，biodiversity 量的是多样。两个词的后半部分告诉你衡量的对象。

normal.en: bio- means 'life story' in biography and 'life science' in biology; biodiversity belongs to the science side.
normal.cn: bio- 在 biography 里是“生平故事”，在 biology 里是“生命科学”；biodiversity 属于科学这一侧。

normal.en: The word usually travels with loss, hotspot and conservation, because it names something that can be measured, threatened and protected.
normal.cn: 这个词常与 loss、hotspot、conservation 同行，因为它命名的东西可以被测量、被威胁、被保护。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf with many different books; abundance would be many copies of one book, diversity is many different titles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架摆着许多不同的书；abundance 是同一本书有很多本，diversity 是有很多不同的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a forest where canopy, understory and soil each hold a different community of life.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林，树冠层、林下层与土壤各自住着不同的生命群落。

abstract.en: Picture three nested circles: genes inside species, species inside ecosystems. Biodiversity is the whole set of circles, not just the middle one.
abstract.cn: 想象三个同心圆：基因在物种之内，物种在生态系统之内。biodiversity 是整套圆，而不只是中间那一圈。

examples.en: The rainforest supports biodiversity that no plantation can replace.
examples.cn: 雨林所支撑的生物多样性是任何单一林场都无法替代的。

examples.en: Scientists measure biodiversity at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels.
examples.cn: 科学家在遗传、物种和生态系统三个层次上测量生物多样性。

examples.en: The report links biodiversity loss to the draining of local wetlands.
examples.cn: 报告把生物多样性丧失与当地湿地被排干联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命所赐，大（dai）家各有伟（ver）色，提（ti）供多样 → biodiversity 生物多样性

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 diversus“转向各方”构成的 diversity“多样性”；20 世纪仿 biological diversity 截短而成的新造复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one core: difference among living things. The word then widens inward to genes, outward to ecosystems, sideways to measurement and loss, and finally into law and city planning.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个核心：生物之间的差异。这个词随后向内扩展到基因，向外扩展到生态系统，再横向扩展到测量与丧失，最后进入法律与城市规划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life turned into many different forms in one place.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一片土地上的生命分成许多不同的形态。

branches.en: LEVELS OF VARIETY: species differ from one another, and individuals differ genetically inside a species.
branches.cn: 多样的层次：物种之间彼此不同，个体在同一物种内部也有基因差异。

branches.en: PLACES AND CULTIVATION: habitats differ from one another, and farming adds human-selected varieties.
branches.cn: 生境与栽培：生境彼此不同，农业又加入人类选育的品种。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT AND DECLINE: variety becomes a scale with high and low values, and a falling scale becomes loss.
branches.cn: 测量与下降：多样性变成有高低值的刻度，而刻度下跌就成了丧失。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND LAW: threatened richness concentrates attention, and cross-border variety becomes a global commons.
branches.cn: 保护与法律：受威胁的丰富度集中注意力，跨国界的多样性成为全球公共资源。

branches.en: BEYOND WILDNESS: managed and urban land also count, so the word becomes a planning target.
branches.cn: 超越荒野：人工管理与城市土地也计入，于是这个词成为规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is a transparent modern compound: bio- + diversity. Both parts are free-standing or semi-free in English, which is why the word feels self-explaining even to a reader who knows no Latin or Greek.
intro.cn: biodiversity 是一个透明的现代复合词：bio- + diversity。两部分在英语中都能独立或半独立使用，所以即使不懂拉丁语或希腊语，读者也觉得它自我解释。

latinIntro.en: There is no single Latin word behind biodiversity. The prefix is Greek bios; the noun is Latin diversitas, from diversus, past participle of divertere. The compound itself is modern, so its 'etymology' is a join, not an inheritance.
latinIntro.cn: biodiversity 背后没有单个拉丁词。前缀是希腊语 bios；名词是拉丁语 diversitas，出自 divertere 的过去分词 diversus。复合词本身是现代造物，所以它的“词源”是一次拼接，而不是承袭。

items.meaning: the science of life and living things
items.example: She studied biology before turning to ecology.
items.exampleCN: 她在转向生态学之前学的是生物学。

items.meaning: the variety of life at several levels
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性（bio-“生命”+ diversity“多样”）
items.example: The survey mapped biodiversity across the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查绘制了山谷各处的生物多样性。

items.meaning: having a high variety of living things
items.meaningCN: 生物多样的；生物种类丰富的
items.example: The delta is one of the most biodiverse regions in Asia.
items.exampleCN: 这片三角洲是亚洲生物多样性最丰富的地区之一。

items.meaning: the diversity of crops and livestock
items.meaningCN: 农业生物多样性（agro-“农田”+ biodiversity）
items.example: Seed banks protect agrobiodiversity.
items.exampleCN: 种子库保护农业生物多样性。

items.meaning: a place of intense activity or concentration
items.meaningCN: 热点（活动或集中程度极高的地点）
items.example: The region is a biodiversity hotspot.
items.exampleCN: 该地区是一个生物多样性热点。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.example: Carbon moves through the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 碳在生物圈中循环。

items.meaning: a large ecological community shaped by climate
items.example: Tundra is a cold biome.
items.exampleCN: 苔原是寒冷的生物群系。

items.meaningCN: 多样性；差异（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The region is known for its cultural diversity.
items.exampleCN: 该地区以文化多样性著称。

items.meaning: to make or become more varied
items.meaningCN: 使多样化；分散（-ify 表示“使……化”）
items.example: Farmers diversified their crops.
items.exampleCN: 农民使作物多样化。

items.meaning: compensation for damage to habitats, usually by restoring or protecting an equivalent area
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性补偿：通过修复或保护等面积生境来弥补损害
items.example: The company funded a biodiversity offset near the mine.
items.exampleCN: 公司出资在矿区附近实施生物多样性补偿。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向各方的；各种各样的

definition_zh: 全球市场；世界市场；某一产品的全球需求与交易体系
definition_en: the worldwide system in which goods, services and capital are bought and sold across national borders
core_image: 一颗地球仪上密布着连线，每一条线两端各是一处港口或交易所，货物与资金沿线来回
scene: 跨国公司的会议室里，墙上挂着一幅世界地图，负责人指着几处港口说，产品要在所有国家同时销售。 The directors studied how the product would compete in the global market.
sceneCN: 这里指「全球范围的市场体系」，对应第 1 个义项：跨越各国边界的买卖与竞争场所；句意为董事们研究该产品将如何在全球市场中竞争。画面要点：世界地图、港口标记、会议桌、销售图表。

pos.zh: 全球市场；世界市场（可数，常用单数指整体体系，复数指多个区域市场）

collocations.phrase: a player in the global market

derivatives.zh: 使全球化（global 加动词后缀，语义从「整体」转为「扩展到全球」）
全球化（globalize 加名词后缀，指跨国整合的过程）
在全球范围内（global 加副词后缀，指作用范围）
市场场所（market 加 place 构成的复合词，指交易发生的具体场所）
营销（market 加动名词后缀，语义从「市场」转为「开拓市场的行为」）

senses.title: The worldwide trading arena
senses.definition: the worldwide system in which goods, services and capital are exchanged across borders
senses.definitionCN: 货物、服务与资本跨国交换的世界性体系
senses.example: The directors studied how the product would compete in the global market.
senses.exampleCN: 董事们研究该产品将如何在全球市场上竞争。
senses.why: Global extends Latin globus 'sphere' to the whole earth, and market names a place of trade, so the phrase is the trading place of the whole sphere.
senses.whyCN: global 把拉丁 globus「球体」扩展到整个地球，market 指交易之所，合起来就是整个球面上的交易场所。

senses.title: Combined demand from all countries
senses.titleCN: 所有国家买方的合计需求
senses.definition: the total demand for a category of goods from buyers in every country
senses.definitionCN: 各国买方对某一类货物的需求总和
senses.example: Demand for the device grew across the global market.
senses.exampleCN: 全球市场对该设备的需求增长了。
senses.why: A market can mean the buyers themselves, so a global market is the sum of buyers everywhere rather than a physical place.
senses.whyCN: 市场也可以指买方本身，因此全球市场就是各地买方的总和，而不是一个实体场所。

senses.title: The worldwide market for one product
senses.definition: the worldwide supply and demand for a single product or service
senses.definitionCN: 单一产品或服务在世界范围内的供给与需求
senses.example: The global market for memory chips is highly concentrated.
senses.exampleCN: 存储芯片的全球市场高度集中。
senses.why: Naming the product narrows the sphere to one trade, as in the steel market or the car market.
senses.whyCN: 点明产品就把整个球面收窄到一桩生意，如钢铁市场或汽车市场。

senses.title: The international capital market
senses.definition: the cross-border system in which money, securities and credit are traded
senses.definitionCN: 资金、证券与信贷跨境交易的世界性体系
senses.example: Pension funds move capital through the global market every day.
senses.exampleCN: 养老基金每天都在全球市场中调度资本。
senses.why: Finance uses the same arena image, but the cargo is money and the ports are exchanges.
senses.whyCN: 金融沿用同一个场所意象，只是货物变成金钱，港口变成交易所。

senses.title: Access to customers outside one's country
senses.titleCN: 进入本国之外客户群的通道
senses.definition: the opportunity for a firm to sell to customers in other countries
senses.definitionCN: 企业向他国客户销售的机会
senses.example: Small firms struggle to reach the global market without partners.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业若没有伙伴，很难进入全球市场。
senses.why: From a company's viewpoint the phrase names an opening rather than a place, and entry becomes the key verb.
senses.whyCN: 从企业视角看，这个短语指一扇打开的门而不是一个地点，因此「进入」成了常用动词。

senses.title: Worldwide competitive position
senses.definition: the rank or share that a firm holds in worldwide sales of a product
senses.definitionCN: 企业在某产品的世界销售额中所占的排名或份额
senses.example: The company holds a third of the global market in turbines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司占全球涡轮机市场的三分之一。
senses.why: Share language turns the arena into a pie to be divided, so the phrase measures position rather than describes trade.
senses.whyCN: 份额的说法把竞技场变成一块待分的饼，于是这个短语衡量的是地位，而不是描述贸易。

senses.title: The price level set worldwide
senses.titleCN: 由全球供求形成的价格水平
senses.definition: the price of a commodity determined by worldwide supply and demand rather than local conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由世界范围供求而非本地情况决定的商品价格
senses.example: Wheat prices now follow the global market, not the village harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦价格如今跟着全球市场走，而不是看村里收成。
senses.why: When buyers and sellers are everywhere, no single locality sets the price, so the phrase denotes a price formed collectively.
senses.whyCN: 当买卖双方遍布各地，任何单一场地都无法定价，因此这个短语指集体形成的价格。

senses.title: Worldwide competition as an arena
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把全球竞争视作一个竞技场
senses.definition: the abstract arena in which firms, cities or ideas compete for worldwide attention and sales
senses.definitionCN: 企业、城市或观念争夺全球关注与销售份额的抽象竞技场
senses.example: Universities now compete in a global market for students.
senses.exampleCN: 大学如今在学生这一全球市场中相互竞争。
senses.why: The metaphor widens once more: anything that can attract people or money can be said to have a global market.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻再度扩展：凡能吸引人或钱的东西，都可以说拥有一个全球市场。

intro.en: Global market joins two separate Latin lines: global from globus 'sphere', market from mercatus 'trade'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: global market 联结了两条独立的拉丁语线索：global 出自 globus「球体」，market 出自 mercatus「交易」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Globus meant a ball or sphere, and it was used for the round earth by Roman writers.
items.cn: globus 意为球或球体，罗马作家也用它指圆形的大地。

items.en: French formed global in the sense of taking the whole into one view, and English adopted it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语构成 global，意为把整体纳入一个视野；英语在 17 世纪吸收了它。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise'.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或市场，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「货物」。

items.en: Old English borrowed market through Latin and French, first as a place and then as the demand found there.
items.cn: 古英语经拉丁语与法语借入 market，最初指地点，随后指那里出现的需求。

items.en: Global market became common in the late twentieth century as transport and finance knit national markets together.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，随着运输与金融把各国市场织在一起，global market 成为常用说法。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two roots and looks close; the second group names markets that differ by scope.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词根之一且外形相近；第二组是按范围区分的不同市场。

entries.definition: A sphere or a model of the earth; it is the object from which the adjective global was made, not a trading place.
entries.definitionCN: 球体或地球模型；它是 global 这个形容词的来源物，不是交易场所。

entries.definition: The process of knitting economies and cultures together; a global market is one result of that process, not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把经济与文化织在一起的过程；全球市场是该过程的一个结果，而不是过程本身。

entries.definition: A concrete place or platform where buying and selling happen; global market stresses scope rather than location.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖发生的具体地点或平台；global market 强调的是范围而不是位置。

entries.definition: A trading place, shortened from market but influenced by Dutch; it names a local venue, not a worldwide system.
entries.definitionCN: 交易场所，由 market 缩略并受荷兰语影响；它指本地场地，而非世界体系。

entries.definition: Nearly interchangeable with global market; world is native English and global is the Latin-derived formal variant.
entries.definitionCN: 与 global market 几乎可互换；world 是英语本族词，global 是拉丁来源的正式变体。

entries.definition: Trade between countries; it stresses relations across borders, while global market stresses the whole as one arena.
entries.definitionCN: 国家之间的贸易；它强调跨国关系，而 global market 强调整体是一个竞技场。

entries.definition: Markets beyond the sea from the speaker's country; the phrase is relative to a home base, unlike global market.
entries.definitionCN: 从说话者本国看去的海外市场；这个说法相对于本国而言，而 global market 不带立场。

entries.definition: A group of countries treating their economies as one market, such as a customs union; it is regional, not worldwide.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干国家经济体当作一个市场的集团，如关税同盟；它是区域性的，不是全球的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the sphere root, the trade root and real market phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：球体词根、交易词根与真实市场搭配。

normal.en: Global is the whole sphere; market is where trade happens; the phrase is trade on the whole sphere.
normal.cn: global 是整个球面，market 是交易发生之处，短语就是整个球面上的交易。

normal.en: The two halves come from different Latin words: globus for the sphere, mercatus for trade.
normal.cn: 两半来自不同的拉丁词：globus 指球体，mercatus 指交易。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: global market share, global market prices, enter the global market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：全球市场份额、全球市场价格、进入全球市场。

normal.en: Global market is uncountable in its system sense and countable when it means several regional markets.
normal.cn: 指整个体系时不可数，指多个区域市场时可数。

normal.en: The phrase is about scope, so it pairs with verbs of reaching and competing, not with verbs of visiting.
normal.cn: 这个短语讲范围，因此常与「抵达」「竞争」类动词搭配，而不与「到访」类动词搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a globe wrapped in threads, each thread a trade route with a price tag at both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗地球仪被线缠满，每根线是一条商路，两端各挂一个价签。

abstract.en: Picture one enormous auction hall with every country's flag on the wall and one running price board.
abstract.cn: 想象一座巨大的拍卖厅，墙上挂着各国旗帜，只有一块跳动的价目板。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium whose seats are filled by buyers from every continent, all watching the same scoreboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场，座位上坐满各洲来的买方，共同盯着同一块记分牌。

examples.en: The firm sells to the global market rather than to one region.
examples.cn: 这家公司面向全球市场销售，而不是只做一个区域。

examples.en: Cheap freight opened the global market to small producers.
examples.cn: 低廉的运费向小生产者打开了全球市场。

examples.en: Its global market share slipped as rivals expanded.
examples.cn: 随着对手扩张，它的全球市场份额下滑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「整个地球的集市」——球面全算进来，货物在各国之间买卖 → 全球市场

root: global 出自拉丁 globus「球体」，经法语 global 进入英语；market 出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」，源 merx「货物」。两者合成「覆盖整个地球的交易场」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same arena at different scales: the whole system, its combined demand, one product's worldwide trade, capital flows, a firm's access, its share, a world price and finally any competition for worldwide attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一竞技场的不同尺度：整个体系、其合计需求、单一产品的世界贸易、资本流动、企业的进入通道、企业份额、世界价格，最后是任何争夺全球关注的竞争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a globe threaded with trade routes, each ending in a price.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗缠满商路的地球仪，每条路的尽头都标着价格。

branches.en: BASE ARENA: the trading place of the whole sphere.
branches.cn: 基础竞技场：整个球面的交易场所。

branches.en: DEMAND AND PRODUCT: the arena can be summed as buyers, or narrowed to one trade.
branches.cn: 需求与产品：这个竞技场可汇成买方总和，也可收窄到一桩生意。

branches.en: CAPITAL: the cargo becomes money and the ports become exchanges.
branches.cn: 资本：货物变成金钱，港口变成交易所。

branches.en: FIRM VIEW: the arena is an opening to be entered and a share to be held.
branches.cn: 企业视角：竞技场是一扇可进入的门，也是一份可持有的份额。

branches.en: PRICE AND METAPHOR: a world price forms, and any contest can be called a global market.
branches.cn: 价格与比喻：世界价格形成，任何争夺都可被称为全球市场。

intro.en: Global market is a phrase of two free words, each with a Latin root and a productive family.
intro.cn: global market 是由两个自由词构成的短语，各自有拉丁词根与能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin globus 'sphere' gives globe, global, globalization; Latin mercatus 'trade' gives market, marketing, marketplace and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 globus「球体」衍生 globe、global、globalization；拉丁 mercatus「交易」衍生 market、marketing、marketplace 与 merchant。

items.exampleCN: 这个成分构成一批关于圆形与整体的词。

items.exampleCN: 全球化把远方的工厂连在一起。

items.example: The brand is known globally.
items.exampleCN: 这个品牌在全球知名。

items.exampleCN: 市场九点开市。

items.example: A merchant sold silk there.
items.exampleCN: 一位商人在那里卖丝绸。

items.example: They compete in the global market.
items.exampleCN: 他们在全球市场上竞争。

definition_zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少；资源不足以满足需求的状态
definition_en: the state in which something needed exists in a quantity too small to satisfy the demand for it
core_image: 集市收摊时只剩最后一筐苹果，围上来的人却比开市时更多
scene: 集市收摊后，最后一筐苹果前反而围了更多人，摊主悄悄翻过价格牌。 Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
sceneCN: 这里 scarcity 指「物品稀少而需求仍在，因而产生溢价的情形」（第 9 个义项：因稀少而形成的附加价值）；句意为稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。图中可辨识物件：空摊位、最后一筐苹果、围拢的人群、翻面的价牌。

pos.zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少（可数指具体的一次短缺，不可数指普遍状态）

derivatives.zh: 缺乏的；稀少的
几乎不；勉强
