senses.title: A shortage of something needed
senses.definition: the condition in which the supply of a needed thing is smaller than the amount people require
senses.definitionCN: 所需之物的供给小于人们所需数量的状况
senses.example: Scarcity of clean water shaped the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净水的短缺塑造了这座小镇的历史。
senses.why: Scarcity names a relationship, not a count: the same amount can be plentiful in one place and scarce in another because demand differs.
senses.whyCN: scarcity 命名的是关系而非数量：同样的量在一处充裕、在另一处稀缺，因为需求不同。

senses.title: Limited means against unlimited wants
senses.titleCN: 经济学：有限资源面对无限欲望
senses.definition: the founding condition of economics, in which resources are finite while human wants are not
senses.definitionCN: 经济学的出发点：资源有限而人的欲望无限
senses.example: Economics begins with scarcity and asks how to allocate.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学从稀缺出发，追问如何分配。
senses.why: Political economy took the everyday word and made it the reason markets and choices exist at all.
senses.whyCN: 政治经济学把这个日常词提升为市场与选择之所以存在的理由。

senses.title: The rarity of a particular object
senses.definition: the quality of being hard to find or obtain, as of a rare book or a scarce stamp
senses.definitionCN: 难以找到或取得的性质，如稀见书或罕邮票
senses.example: The scarcity of the first edition made it expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 初版书的稀有使它昂贵。
senses.why: Collectors use the word for the object itself, because what matters is how few survive rather than how many are wanted.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者用这个词指物本身，因为要紧的是存世多少，而不是多少人想要。

senses.title: Resource depletion in ecology
senses.definition: the falling availability of a natural resource as it is used up or its habitat shrinks
senses.definitionCN: 自然资源因被耗尽或栖息地缩小而日益不可得
senses.example: Scarcity of nesting sites reduced the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 营巢地的稀缺使这个群落变小。
senses.why: Ecology views scarcity as a limit that shapes behaviour, competition and population size.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把稀缺看作塑造行为、竞争与种群规模的限制。

senses.title: Perceived scarcity and the mindset it creates
senses.titleCN: 感知到的稀缺及其心态
senses.definition: a felt shortage that narrows attention, encourages hoarding and pushes people toward short-term choices
senses.definitionCN: 感到的短缺，它会收窄注意力、促使人囤积并偏向短期选择
senses.example: A scarcity mindset kept the team from sharing information.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺心态让这个团队不愿共享信息。
senses.why: Psychology separated the state from the perception, because people act on what they believe is scarce.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把状态与感知分开，因为人是按自己所相信的稀缺去行动的。

senses.title: Not enough hours in the day
senses.definition: the shortage of time relative to the tasks and commitments one has accepted
senses.definitionCN: 相对于已接受的任务与承诺而言的时间不足
senses.example: Time scarcity, not money, kept her from finishing the course.
senses.exampleCN: 让她没能修完课程的，是时间稀缺而非缺钱。
senses.why: The word extends easily to time, because hours are a fixed supply that cannot be increased by effort.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很容易延伸到时上，因为小时是固定供给，再努力也加不出来。

senses.title: Attention and information scarcity
senses.definition: the shortage of attention available for a flood of information, or of reliable information itself
senses.definitionCN: 面对信息洪流时注意力的不足，或可靠信息本身的不足
senses.example: Information scarcity was replaced by information overload.
senses.exampleCN: 信息稀缺已被信息过载取代。
senses.why: Media economics applied the word to attention, since the scarce thing in an abundant market is the audience's focus.
senses.whyCN: 传媒经济学把这个词用到注意力上，因为在充裕的市场里，稀缺的是受众的专注。

senses.title: Artificial scarcity created on purpose
senses.titleCN: 为获利而人为制造的稀缺
senses.definition: a shortage deliberately maintained by a seller, cartel or platform to keep prices or status high
senses.definitionCN: 卖方、卡特尔或平台为维持高价或地位而有意保持的短缺
senses.example: The limited release was artificial scarcity, not a real shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 限量发售是人为稀缺，并非真的缺货。
senses.why: Once scarcity can be manufactured, the word no longer assumes a natural limit; it can describe a strategy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦稀缺可以被制造，这个词就不再假定自然极限，而可以指一种策略。

senses.title: The premium that rarity adds to value
senses.titleCN: 因稀少而产生的价值溢价
senses.definition: the extra price or prestige an item gains because few like it are available
senses.definitionCN: 物品因同类稀少而获得的额外价格或声望
senses.example: Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。
senses.why: Value can come from the supply side alone: when the same thing is abundant it is cheap, and when it is nearly gone it is dear.
senses.whyCN: 价值可以只来自供给一侧：同样的东西多时便宜，快没有时就贵。

intro.en: Scarcity came into English from Old French in the fourteenth century, but its deeper root is disputed between two accounts that are still taught side by side. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: scarcity 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，但其更深词源在两种说法之间至今仍有争议，两种说法常并列讲授。年代均为约数。

items.en: One account derives scarcitas from parcus 'sparing, frugal'. The deeper origin of parcus is uncertain; the suggestion that it comes from parcere 'to spare' is a hypothesis rather than a proved link.
items.cn: 一种说法把 scarcitas 追溯到 parcus「节省的、俭省的」。parcus 的更深来源不确定；认为它出自 parcere「节省」的说法是假说，而非已证实的联系。

items.en: Scarcitas meant 'scarcity, scantiness'. On this account the noun passed into Old French as scarcete and then into English.
items.cn: scarcitas 意为「短缺、稀少」。按这一说法，该名词进入古法语作 scarcete，再进入英语。

items.en: Old French scarcete meant 'smallness, scantiness, stinginess' and English scarcity first carried that sense of meagre supply before widening to any shortage.
items.cn: 古法语 scarcete 意为「少、不足、吝啬」，英语 scarcity 最初带这种「供给寒酸」的意思，后扩为任何短缺。

items.en: The competing account connects the adjective scarce to Vulgar Latin excarpsus 'plucked out', from ex- 'out' plus carpere 'to pluck'. This account explains the adjective but does not settle the noun.
items.cn: 对立说法把形容词 scarce 连到俗拉丁 excarpsus「被摘出的」，出自 ex-「向外」加 carpere「摘取」。这一说法解释了形容词，却未能定下名词的来源。

items.en: From the nineteenth century classical economics made scarcity the central condition of economic life, and the word acquired its technical sense of finite means against unlimited wants.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，古典经济学把稀缺定为经济生活的核心条件，这个词于是获得「有限手段面对无限欲望」的技术义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the derivation is disputed between parcus and excarpsus, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the modern economic sense, so its first date is approximate; any older Indo-European forms offered for this family are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：词源在 parcus 与 excarpsus 之间存疑，现代经济义也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；凡为这个词族给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to scarcity but differ in part of speech, meaning or root; group two holds other nouns of not having enough, each with a different reason for the shortfall.
note.cn: 第一组是与 scarcity 形近、但词性、含义或词根不同的词；第二组是其他表示「不够」的名词，每一个的短缺原因都不同。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'hard to obtain in quantity'; scarcity is the noun built on it in meaning, even where the derivation is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「数量稀少、难以取得」；scarcity 在语义上是它的名词形式，尽管词源仍有争议。

entries.definition: Means 'barely, hardly', not 'sparsely'; the adverb has drifted away from the idea of quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「几乎不、勉强」，而非「稀少地」；这个副词已偏离数量概念。

entries.definition: Thinly spread, from Latin sparsus 'scattered'; it looks close to scarce but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 分布稀疏的，出自拉丁 sparsus「散开的」；与 scarce 外形相近，但并无共同词根。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym of scarcity formed with -ness; it names the state without the economic overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的较罕用同义词；它只指状态，不带经济学色彩。

entries.definition: A plain word for a supply that is below the amount required, usually temporary or local.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给低于所需数量的普通词，通常是临时或局部的。

entries.definition: An old word for a scarce supply, especially of food; it comes from dear in the sense of costly, not from scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给稀少、尤指食物的旧词；它出自表示「昂贵」的 dear，而非出自 scarcity。

entries.definition: A formal noun for a small number or amount, from Latin paucus 'few'; it stresses fewness rather than unmet demand.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指数量很少，出自拉丁 paucus「少」；它强调数量少，而非需求未被满足。

entries.definition: The quality of being uncommon; a rare thing may be plentiful in absolute terms and still be uncommon in kind.
entries.definitionCN: 不常见的性质；稀见之物在绝对数量上可能很多，只是在种类上少见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun of scarce; the -ity ending turns the adjective into a state.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词，-ity 后缀把形容词变成状态。

normal.en: The economic sense is fixed in one phrase: limited resources against unlimited wants.
normal.cn: 经济义固定在一句话里：有限资源面对无限欲望。

normal.en: The family runs scarce, scarcely, scarceness, scarcity and water-scarce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 scarce、scarcely、scarceness、scarcity 与 water-scarce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: water scarcity, food scarcity, resource scarcity, artificial scarcity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：水资源短缺、粮食短缺、资源稀缺、人为稀缺。

normal.en: Sparse looks like scarce but comes from sparsus 'scattered', so the two are false relatives.
normal.cn: sparse 看起来像 scarce，却出自 sparsus「散开的」，两者是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture the last basket on a table and every hand reaching at once.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上最后一筐，所有手同时伸过去。

abstract.en: Picture a day with more tasks than hours, so each choice costs another choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一天里任务多过小时，每个选择都要用另一个选择来换。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf kept almost empty on purpose so that the few items look precious.
abstract.cn: 想象货架故意留得几乎空着，好让剩下的几件显得珍贵。

examples.en: Classical economics treats scarcity as the reason choice is necessary.
examples.cn: 古典经济学把稀缺视为选择之所以必要的原因。

examples.en: The scarcity of rare earths reshaped the electronics supply chain.
examples.cn: 稀土资源的稀缺重塑了电子产业供应链。

examples.en: Artificial scarcity can keep a price high long after demand has fallen.
examples.cn: 人为稀缺可以在需求下降很久之后仍把价格维持在高位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「scarce（稀少）+ ity」——东西少、要的人多 → 稀缺、短缺

root: 古法语 scarcete < 拉丁 scarcitas「短缺」；词根一说为 parcus「俭省的」，另一说与俗拉丁 excarpsus「摘出的」（ex- + carpere）相关，两说并存未定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one relation: a supply is smaller than the demand on it. The word then becomes the foundation of economics, the state of a rare object, an ecological limit, a mindset, a shortage of time, of attention, a shortage made on purpose and finally a premium on price.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个关系展开：供给小于对它的需求。这个词随后成为经济学的基础、稀见物的状态、生态的限制、一种心态、时间与注意力的不足、有意制造的不足，最后是价格上的溢价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one last basket on an emptying table while more hands reach for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：空下去的桌上只剩最后一筐，伸过来的手却更多。

branches.en: THE GAP: the everyday shortfall and the founding condition of economics are the same relation formalised.
branches.cn: 缺口：日常的不足与经济学的出发点，是同一关系被形式化。

branches.en: FEWNESS: a rare object and a depleted habitat are both cases of supply falling.
branches.cn: 稀少：稀见之物与枯竭的栖息地，都是供给下降的情形。

branches.en: MIND: perception can produce the behaviour of scarcity before the shortage arrives.
branches.cn: 心态：感知可以在短缺到来之前就制造出稀缺的行为。

branches.en: NON-MATERIAL: hours and attention are fixed or finite supplies of their own.
branches.cn: 非实物：小时与注意力本身就是固定或有限的供给。

branches.en: MADE AND PRICED: scarcity can be staged, and rarity can be charged for.
branches.cn: 制造与定价：稀缺可以被安排出来，稀少也可以被收费。

intro.en: Scarcity is a noun formed with a Latin state suffix on a stem whose own origin is disputed, so the suffix is certain while the root is not.
intro.cn: scarcity 是用拉丁状态后缀构成的名称，词干本身的来源有争议，因此后缀确定而词根不确定。

latinIntro.en: The state suffix -itas gives English -ity in scarcity, rarity and paucity; the root is variously traced to parcus 'sparing' or to excarpsus 'plucked out'.
latinIntro.cn: 状态后缀 -itas 在 scarcity、rarity 与 paucity 中作英语 -ity；词根则有 parcus「俭省的」与 excarpsus「摘出的」两种追溯。

items.structure: Old French scars / escars (adjective, disputed origin)
items.example: Clean water was scarce after the drought.
items.exampleCN: 旱情之后洁净水很稀缺。

items.example: The suffix turns scarce into a named state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 scarce 变成一个有名称的状态。

items.example: Scarceness is the plainer twin of scarcity.
items.exampleCN: scarceness 是 scarcity 更朴素的双胞胎。

items.meaning: shortage; the state of being scarce
items.example: Scarcity raised the price of grain.
items.exampleCN: 稀缺抬高了谷物价格。

items.example: Good soil is scarce on the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上良田稀少。

items.example: She scarcely had time to eat.
items.exampleCN: 她几乎没时间吃饭。

items.example: The scarceness of fuel closed the mill.
items.exampleCN: 燃料的稀少让磨坊关了门。

items.meaning: charges raised because supply is short

dict_mnemonic.text: elapse ＝ e-（离开，ex- 的变体）＋ lapse（滑动，拉丁 labi／lapsus）＝「滑走」。关键限制：elapse 的主语只能是时间（time, years, minutes, hours），不能说「人 elapse」。同根一家：lapse 名词「小失误；（时间）流逝」，动词「失效」（membership lapses 会员资格失效）；collapse ＝ col-（一起）＋ lapse ＝ 一起滑倒＝倒塌、崩溃；relapse ＝ re-（回）＋ lapse ＝ 滑回去＝复发；elapsed 形容词「已过去的」，elapsed time 已用时间。日常口语说 time passes / time goes by，elapse 偏书面与计时语境。近义 expire 指「到期」（护照、合同），intervene 指「（时间）介于其间」。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（离开）＋ labi（滑动）→ elabi → elapsus（已溜走的）→ elapse（时间消逝）

senses.title: Of little importance
senses.definition: too small or unimportant to affect the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 太小或不重要，影响不到主要问题
senses.example: The delay was trivial compared with the cost of a wrong decision.
senses.exampleCN: 与错误决策的代价相比，这点延误微不足道。
senses.why: The word's history runs from the crossroads to the common, and then to the common that no longer matters.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的历史从「三岔路口」走到「平常」，再走到「平常到不再重要」。

senses.title: An everyday trifle
senses.definition: a small everyday detail hardly worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 不值得关注的小日常细节
senses.example: They argued about whose turn it was to water the plants, a trivial matter in a busy week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争该轮到谁浇花，这在忙碌的一周里只是琐事。
senses.why: A matter is trivial when its size, not its difficulty, is the reason to ignore it.
senses.whyCN: 一件事被称为琐事，是因为它小，而不是因为它难。

senses.title: A cost too small to count
senses.definition: an expense so small that it does not change a decision
senses.definitionCN: 小到不会改变决策的支出
senses.example: The extra licence fee is trivial next to the legal risk.
senses.exampleCN: 与法律风险相比，额外的许可费微不足道。
senses.why: Costs are trivial when the decision would be the same without them.
senses.whyCN: 成本在去掉它决策也不变时，就是微不足道的。

senses.title: The obvious solution in mathematics
senses.definition: the simple solution that satisfies the equation without special work, often zero
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别处理即满足方程的简单解，常为零
senses.example: The equation has a trivial solution at zero and two others that matter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有一个位于零的平凡解，另有两个真正重要的解。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word for the case that gives itself away, which is the technical descendant of commonplace.
senses.whyCN: 数学用它指那个自己送上门的情形，是「平常」这一义的技术后裔。

senses.title: An objection that misses the point
senses.definition: a complaint that does not touch the main question
senses.definitionCN: 没有触及主要问题的抱怨
senses.example: He raised a trivial objection about the font and said nothing about the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他对字体提了个无关紧要的反对，对数据却一言不发。
senses.why: An objection is trivial when it leaves the main claim standing.
senses.whyCN: 反对在主要主张仍然立得住时，就是无关紧要的。

senses.title: Small details used to avoid the issue
senses.definition: minor points brought up to delay or distract
senses.definitionCN: 用细小的点来拖延或转移注意
senses.example: The report drowns in trivial details and never states the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 报告淹没在细枝末节里，始终没说清原因。
senses.why: Details become trivial when they are used to fill the space where the argument should be.
senses.whyCN: 当细节被用来填满本该放论证的位置，它们就成了细枝末节。

senses.title: Shallow talk
senses.definition: conversation without substance or interest
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质或趣味的谈话
senses.example: The party talk was trivial, but it passed the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上的谈话很浅薄，却也把晚上打发了。
senses.why: Talk without substance earns the word because it leaves nothing behind.
senses.whyCN: 没有实质的谈话得到这个词，因为它什么也没留下。

senses.title: A minor fault
senses.definition: an offence treated as slight rather than serious
senses.definitionCN: 被当作轻微而非严重的过错
senses.example: Under the old rules, a late form was a trivial offence with no penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 按旧规，迟交表格属轻微过失，不受处罚。
senses.why: Law calls a fault trivial when the penalty is lighter than the paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当处罚比文书手续还轻时，法律就把该过失称为轻微的。

senses.title: Too simple to need comment
senses.definition: so easy in computing or logic that it is not worth explaining
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机或逻辑上简单到不值得解释
senses.example: The remaining case is trivial, so the proof simply says it follows.
senses.exampleCN: 剩下的情形简单到无需说明，证明里只写一句「由此可得」。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the oldest idea: so common and easy that it needs no remark.
senses.whyCN: 技术义保留了最古老的意思：太寻常、太容易，因而不必再提。

intro.en: Trivial comes from Latin trivialis, belonging to the crossroads, from trivium, a place where three roads meet. Medieval schools called the first three arts the trivium, so the adjective meant belonging to the basic studies, then commonplace, and finally of little importance. The modern sense grew out of that social judgement rather than from the number three.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「属于三岔路的」形容词，出自表示「三条路交汇处」的名词。中世纪学校把最初三门学科称为「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础学科的」，再变成「平常的」，最后成为「不重要的」。现代义从这种社会判断长出来，而不是从数字「三」直接得来。

items.en: A trivium was a place where three roads met, from tri- three and via road.
items.cn: 这个词指三条路交汇之处，由「三」与「道路」构成。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to such a public corner, hence common and ordinary.
items.cn: 该形容词指属于这种人流交汇的公共角落，因此有「平常、普通」之意。

items.en: The first three liberal arts were called the trivium, and trivialis came to mean belonging to basic instruction.
items.cn: 最初三门博雅学科合称「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础教学的」。

items.en: English took the word for things common and therefore slight.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用于平常因而轻贱的事物。

items.en: The sense of unimportant hardened, and mathematics adopted it for the obvious case.
items.cn: 「不重要」义渐趋固定，数学又用它指显然的情形。

items.en: Quiz games and computing gave the word new phrases; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 问答游戏与计算机给出新的说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the crossroads root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of smallness. The note also ties trivial to its noun triviality.
note.cn: 第一组共享「三岔路」词根或形近；第二组指其他「小」的说法。这里也把形容词与其名词形式「琐碎」连起来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the crossroads, the basic school subjects, the meeting that argues about wording, and the obvious equation case.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用三岔路口、基础学科、为一个用词争吵的会议，以及显然的方程情形。

normal.en: A crossroads is public and common, and common things soon look small.
normal.cn: 三岔路是公共而平常的，而平常的东西很快就显得微小。

normal.en: The three basic arts were the trivium, so trivial once meant elementary, not worthless.
normal.cn: 三门基础学科合称三艺，所以这个词曾经意为「基础的」，而不是「无价值的」。

normal.en: A trivial solution is the one that offers itself without effort.
normal.cn: 平凡解就是那个不用费力自己送上门的解。

normal.en: A trivial objection changes the font, not the argument.
normal.cn: 无关紧要的反对改的是字体，不是论证。

normal.en: Triviality is what happens when a serious subject is discussed only in small details.
normal.cn: 琐碎化，就是严肃话题只剩细枝末节时发生的事。

abstract.en: Calling something trivial is a way of deciding what will not be looked at.
abstract.cn: 把某事称为微不足道，是在决定什么不必再看。

abstract.en: The crossroads made a word for the common, and the common became a verdict on worth.
abstract.cn: 「三岔路」造出了一个表示「平常」的词，而「平常」又变成了对价值的判决。

abstract.en: Every field keeps a set of trivial cases, and they are the ones that teach the shape of the rest.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都留着一批平凡情形，而正是它们教人看清其余部分的形状。

examples.en: The difference in price is trivial compared with the difference in quality.
examples.cn: 与质量差距相比，价格差距微不足道。

examples.en: Do not waste the meeting on trivial details that the report already covers.
examples.cn: 别把会议浪费在报告里已经写到的细枝末节上。

examples.en: The first case is trivial, so the proof moves straight to the second.
examples.cn: 第一种情形简单到无需说明，所以证明直接转向第二种。

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「三岔路口」的名词，由「三」与「道路」构成，派生形容词义为「属于三岔路的、平常的」。中世纪把三门基础学科合称三艺，于是又指「基础学科的」，再演变为「平常的」，最后成为「微不足道的」。数学「平凡解」义为十九世纪后的技术引申；各短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the crossroads to the equation: unimportant, an everyday trifle, a negligible cost, the obvious mathematical case, a pointless objection, distracting details, shallow talk, a slight fault, and the simple case that needs no comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从三岔路走到方程：不重要、日常琐事、可忽略的成本、数学的显然情形、无的放矢的反对、转移注意的细节、浅薄的闲谈、轻微过失，以及无需说明的简单情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one end of the table is covered with notes about wording, while the budget sheet stays shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌子一端堆满改词的纸条，另一端的预算表始终没有翻开。

branches.en: THE SMALL AMOUNT: importance and cost measured and found tiny.
branches.cn: 微小的分量：重要性与成本一量就小。

branches.en: THE TRIFLE AND THE DISTRACTION: small items, and small items used to avoid the point.
branches.cn: 琐事与分神：小东西，以及被用来回避要点的小东西。

branches.en: THE EASY CASE: the solution or case that offers itself.
branches.cn: 轻易的情形：自己送上门的解或情形。

branches.en: THE LIGHT COMPLAINT: an objection or fault too slight to matter.
branches.cn: 轻微的抱怨：轻到不必计较的反对或过失。

branches.en: THE SHALLOW TALK: conversation without substance.
branches.cn: 浅薄的谈话：没有实质的闲聊。

intro.en: Trivial is a crossroads noun with an adjective ending; the family covers trivia, the three basic arts, and the act of making something seem small.
intro.cn: 这个词是「三岔路」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖冷知识、三门基础学科，以及「把某事说得微不足道」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin tri- and via build trivium, and the derived adjective trivialis supplies the English word and its whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「三」与「道路」构成表示「三岔路」的名词，派生形容词给出英语词及其整个词族。

items.example: It marks the meeting of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它标出三条路的交汇。

items.example: It is also the source of English via.
items.exampleCN: 它也是英语「经由」的来源。

items.example: The noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把该词标为形容词。

items.example: It forms triviality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「琐碎」。

items.example: It forms trivialize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「使显得琐碎」。

items.example: The plural keeps the idea of many small things.
items.exampleCN: 复数保留了「许多小东西」的意思。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「琐碎；琐事」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使显得琐碎」
由「使显得琐碎」加名词尾构成，义为「淡化；琐碎化」
由拉丁语「三岔路」构成，义为中世纪三门基础学科

definition_zh: 时间的；时间先后上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的；（解剖）颞的
definition_en: relating to time or to the order of events, and, in another line of the same spelling, relating to temples of the head or to worldly affairs
core_image: 档案柜的抽屉按年份一层层往下排，同一件事的三份记录落在三个不同的格子里
scene: 档案室里，三份记录同一事件的文件夹按年份排成一列，谁在前谁在后一眼可见。 Researchers tracked the temporal order of the three events rather than the distance between them.
sceneCN: 这里指事件在时间上的先后（第 2 个义项：时间先后次序）；句意为研究者追踪三个事件的时间先后，而不是它们之间的空间距离。图中可辨识物件：按年份排列的档案夹、三份记录、年份标签、档案柜。

pos.zh: 时间的；时间上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的
（解剖）颞的；太阳穴部位的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上；按时间」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性；暂时性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
解剖学中由同一部位名词构成的名称，指颞肌
由表示「在上」的前缀加该解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

senses.title: Relating to time
senses.definition: concerned with time as a dimension
senses.definitionCN: 涉及时间这一维度的
senses.example: The study measures temporal change rather than differences between places.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究测量的是随时间发生的变化，而不是地方之间的差异。
senses.why: The Latin word for time gives this adjective its broadest frame, and most other senses narrow it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「时间」的词给出最宽的框架，其余义项大多是在此之上收窄。

senses.title: Order of events in time
senses.definition: the sequence in which events happen
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生的先后顺序
senses.example: The notes record the temporal order of the symptoms, not their severity.
senses.exampleCN: 记录写的是症状出现的时间先后，而不是轻重。
senses.why: Order needs an axis, and time supplies one; this sense is the everyday core.
senses.whyCN: 次序需要一个轴，时间提供了这个轴，这是最日常的核心义。

senses.title: Time resolution
senses.definition: how finely an instrument or dataset divides time
senses.definitionCN: 仪器或数据集把时间切分的精细程度
senses.example: The camera's temporal resolution is one frame every ten milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机的时间分辨率是每十毫秒一帧。
senses.why: Here time is measured as a grid, so the word marks the fineness of that grid.
senses.whyCN: 这里时间被当成一张网格来量，词于是标出网格的细密程度。

senses.title: The temporal lobe of the brain
senses.definition: the lobe at the side of the head, named from the temples
senses.definitionCN: 位于头侧、因太阳穴部位得名的脑叶
senses.example: The temporal lobe handles much of what we hear and remember.
senses.exampleCN: 颞叶负责我们所听到与记住的很大一部分内容。
senses.why: This sense belongs to a different Latin word, the plural name for the temples of the head.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项属于另一个拉丁词，即「头部太阳穴」的复数形式。

senses.title: Worldly power
senses.definition: authority over worldly affairs as opposed to spiritual authority
senses.definitionCN: 对世俗事务的管辖权，与属灵权力相对
senses.example: The dispute was over temporal power, not over doctrine.
senses.exampleCN: 争论针对的是世俗权力，而不是教义。
senses.why: The church set the authority of this world against the authority of the next, and the word carried the contrast.
senses.whyCN: 教会把此世的权力与彼世的权力对立起来，这个词就承载了这组对照。

senses.title: Earthly and passing
senses.definition: belonging to this world and therefore not lasting
senses.definitionCN: 属于此世、因而不能长久的
senses.example: Monks renounced temporal goods but kept their books.
senses.exampleCN: 修士舍弃尘世的财物，却留下了书。
senses.why: The same axis of time carries a judgement: what is in time will pass.
senses.whyCN: 同一条时间轴带上了判断：凡在时间之中的都会过去。

senses.title: A clause of time
senses.definition: a subordinate clause saying when something happens
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事何时发生的从属分句
senses.example: The sentence opens with a temporal clause introduced by after.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子以表示「之后」的连接词引导的时间从句开头。
senses.why: Grammar names by function, so any clause marking time takes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 语法按功能命名，凡标出时间的分句都用这个形容词。

senses.title: Temporal scale
senses.definition: the length of time over which something is observed
senses.definitionCN: 观察某事所跨的时间长度
senses.example: Climate and soil form on very different temporal scales.
senses.exampleCN: 气候与土壤在以极为不同的时间尺度形成。
senses.why: Scale is the length of the ruler, and on the time axis the ruler is a span of years.
senses.whyCN: 尺度就是尺子的长度；放在时间轴上，这把尺子就是一段年份。

intro.en: Temporal is two words wearing one shape. The time sense comes from Latin tempus, time, and its adjective temporalis, which also supplied the church's word for worldly affairs. The anatomy sense comes from Latin tempora, the temples of the head, a different word. English merged them in spelling, not in origin.
intro.cn: 这个词其实是两个词穿了同一件外衣。时间义来自拉丁语 tempus「时间」及其形容词，教会又用它指世俗事务。解剖义来自拉丁语 tempora「头部太阳穴」，是另一个词。英语只是在拼写上把它们合在一起，来源并不相同。

items.en: Tempus meant time, with the stem tempor- appearing in all other cases.
items.cn: 这个词意为「时间」，其余各格都用表示「时间」的词干。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to time, and the church used it for what belongs to this world.
items.cn: 该形容词意为「属于时间的」，教会用它指属于此世的事物。

items.en: A separate noun, plural of tempus in the sense of the temples of the head, gave the anatomical word.
items.cn: 另一个名词，即「太阳穴」义的复数，给出了解剖学上的这个词。

items.en: French kept the church contrast between the worldly and the spiritual.
items.cn: 法语保留了教会关于「世俗」与「属灵」的对照。

items.en: English took both senses, and later added the grammatical and scientific uses.
items.cn: 英语把两个义项都吸收进来，后来又加上语法与科学用法。

items.en: Measurement and neuroscience gave the word new compounds; the first dates of those compounds are uncertain.
items.cn: 测量与神经科学又给出新的复合说法；这些说法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the time root or looks close; the second group names time, worldliness and related ideas. The note also contrasts temporal with spatial, and separates the time sense from the anatomy sense.
note.cn: 第一组共享「时间」词根或形近；第二组指时间、世俗及相关概念。这里也把「时间的」与「空间的」对照说清，并分开时间义与解剖义。

entries.definition: Lasting only for a time; the same time root with an ending meaning lasting for a period.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续一段时间；同一时间词根加表示「持续一段」的词尾。

entries.definition: For a limited time only.
entries.definitionCN: 指仅在有限时间内。

entries.definition: The speed of music, from the Italian use of the time word.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐的速度，来自意大利语对「时间」一词的使用。

entries.definition: Existing at the same time; the prefix means with.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在的；前缀意为「共同」。

entries.definition: To stall or act evasively in order to gain time.
entries.definitionCN: 指为争取时间而拖延或见风使舵。

entries.definition: Relating to space, the other axis of measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与空间有关，是测量所用的另一条轴。

entries.definition: Arranged by date, with explicit times attached.
entries.definitionCN: 指按日期排列，并明确标出时间。

entries.definition: Concerned with this world rather than with religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指关心此世而非宗教事务。

entries.definition: Concerned with material life and its affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 指关注物质生活及其事务。

entries.definition: Lasting only a short time and then gone.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续很短时间便消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the dated file drawers, the framework of the church, the temple-side lobe and the frame rate of a camera.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用按年份排的档案抽屉、教会与世俗的对照、头侧的脑叶以及相机的帧率。

normal.en: Temporal questions ask when, the mirror of spatial questions asking where.
normal.cn: 时间类问题问「什么时候」，正好映照空间类问题的「在哪里」。

normal.en: A temporal clause is a subordinate sentence that answers when.
normal.cn: 时间从句就是回答「何时」的从属句。

normal.en: The temporal lobe sits beside the temples, which is exactly what its Latin name says.
normal.cn: 颞叶位于太阳穴旁，它的拉丁名称说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Temporal power is the church's word for the authority of this world.
normal.cn: 世俗权力是教会用来指此世权威的说法。

normal.en: Temporal scale decides what looks fast and what looks slow.
normal.cn: 时间尺度决定什么看起来快、什么看起来慢。

abstract.en: Time is the axis that makes order visible, and this adjective is the name of that axis.
abstract.cn: 时间是把次序变可见的那条轴，而这个形容词就是这条轴的名字。

abstract.en: Two unrelated Latin nouns ended up with the same English spelling, and only the context tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 两个互不相干的拉丁名词最后拼成了一个英语单词，只能靠上下文分开。

abstract.en: Anything inside time is already leaving, which is why the worldly sense carries a hint of loss.
abstract.cn: 凡在时间之中的都已开始离去，所以世俗义总带一丝失去的意味。

examples.en: The two records differ in temporal order but agree on content.
examples.cn: 这两份记录在时间先后上不同，内容却一致。

examples.en: Temporal power and spiritual authority were once argued in the same courtroom.
examples.cn: 世俗权力与属灵权威曾在一间法庭上被同时争辩。

examples.en: Fossils and languages change on completely different temporal scales.
examples.cn: 化石与语言以完全不同的时间尺度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦泼若」：先问「时间」什么时候到，再问「尘土」什么时候散，一事一时都记在案上

root: 一支源于拉丁语中表示「时间」的名词及其形容词，教会又引申指「世俗的」；另一支源于拉丁语中表示「头部太阳穴」的复数名词，给出解剖学的「颞的」。两支同形异源，英语只在拼写上合并。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use two roots: time, its order, its resolution and scale; the anatomy of the temples; worldly power and worldly transience; and the grammar of when.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属两个词根：时间本身、时间次序、时间分辨率与时间尺度；太阳穴部位的解剖；世俗权力与尘世短暂；以及表示「何时」的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three folders for one event slide into year-labelled drawers, and the order is visible at a glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一事件的三份档案滑进标着年份的抽屉，先后一眼可见。

branches.en: THE AXIS AND ITS ORDER: time as a dimension, then events placed along it.
branches.cn: 轴与轴上的次序：先是时间这一维度，再是沿它摆放的事件。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SPAN: fine resolution at one end, long scale at the other.
branches.cn: 被丈量的跨度：一端是精细分辨率，一端是长尺度。

branches.en: THE TEMPLES' LOBE: a second Latin root hiding under the same spelling.
branches.cn: 太阳穴的脑叶：同一拼写之下藏着第二个拉丁词根。

branches.en: THE WORLD AND ITS PASSING: authority here, and the fact that it fades.
branches.cn: 此世与其消逝：这里的权力，以及它终将褪去。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE OF WHEN: grammar marking time in a sentence.
branches.cn: 「何时」从句：语法在句中标出时间。

intro.en: Temporal is a Latin time noun with an adjective ending; its family covers lasting for a time, the musical tempo, and the anatomy of the temples.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「时间」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖「暂时的」、音乐的速度，以及太阳穴的解剖。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus and its stem tempor- supply the time line, while the plural tempora supplies the anatomy line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「时间」及其词干提供时间这一线，而复数形式「太阳穴」提供解剖这一线。

items.example: The source of the time sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是时间义的来源。

items.example: The stem seen in temporal and temporary.
items.exampleCN: 见于「时间的」与「暂时的」两词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: A separate word behind the anatomy sense.
items.exampleCN: 解剖义背后是另一个词。

items.example: It marks both senses as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 它把两个义项都标为形容词。

items.example: It forms temporary, lasting for a time.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「暂时的」。

items.example: It forms temporality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「时间性」。

items.example: It forms temporally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「在时间上」。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
由表示「在上」的前缀加解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

definition_zh: 削弱；暗中破坏；逐渐损毁根基；动摇（信心、权威）
definition_en: to weaken something gradually from below, often secretly, by taking away what supports it
core_image: 老墙脚下，水从砖缝里一点点掏空泥沙，墙面看上去完好，根基却已经空了
scene: 老墙脚下，水从砖缝里一点点掏空泥沙，墙面看着完好，根基却已经空了。 Constant leaks had begun to undermine the old wall.
sceneCN: 这里指从根基上逐渐削弱、掏空（第 1 个义项：损毁实物的基础）；句意为持续的渗漏已经开始逐渐损毁那面老墙。

pos.zh: 削弱；暗中破坏；逐渐损毁根基；动摇

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「暗中破坏；起削弱作用的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「暗中破坏者」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被削弱的；根基受损的」

senses.title: Hollow out a physical base
senses.definition: of water, digging or decay, to remove the material under a wall, road or building
senses.definitionCN: 指水、挖掘或腐朽移除墙、路或建筑底下的材料
senses.example: Salt water can undermine the foundation of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 盐水会逐渐掏空桥基。
senses.why: The word is literally under plus mine, so the first sense is the mining sense: taking the ground out from beneath a structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在下」加「挖掘」，所以第一个义项就是采矿义：把结构底下的地基取走。

senses.title: Secretly damage a plan or effort
senses.definition: to weaken a plan, campaign or effort by quiet action rather than open opposition
senses.definitionCN: 以暗中行动而非公开反对来削弱计划、行动或努力
senses.example: A few leaks were enough to undermine the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 几次泄密就足以破坏那项计划。
senses.why: A tunnel dug under a defence does its work unseen, and the word kept that secrecy when it moved from walls to plans.
senses.whyCN: 在防线底下挖的坑道在看不见处做工，这个词从墙转到计划时保留了那份隐秘。

senses.title: Weaken a person's confidence
senses.definition: to make someone steadily less sure of themselves or of a decision
senses.definitionCN: 使某人对自己或某个决定逐渐失去把握
senses.example: Constant criticism undermined her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的批评削弱了她的信心。
senses.why: Confidence stands on supports, and enough small attacks from below can make it sag without ever being hit directly.
senses.whyCN: 信心立在支撑上，足够多来自下方的小攻击能让它下沉，却从未被直接击中。

senses.title: Shake an authority or position
senses.definition: to make a leader, office or institution less respected and less able to act
senses.definitionCN: 使领导者、职位或机构受到的尊重减少、行动能力下降
senses.example: The scandal undermined the minister's authority.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻动摇了那位部长的权威。
senses.why: Authority is a structure that stands on accepted ground, and removing that ground is the word's exact work.
senses.whyCN: 权威是立在公认地基上的结构，而抽走那层地基正是这个词的确切工作。

senses.title: Damage a reputation
senses.definition: to lower the trust that others place in a person, company or brand
senses.definitionCN: 降低他人对个人、公司或品牌的信任
senses.example: Rumours undermined the company's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言损害了公司的声誉。
senses.why: A reputation is built from many small confirmations, so it can be undone from below without any single open attack.
senses.whyCN: 声誉由许多小确认堆成，因此可以被下方一点点拆掉，而无需任何一次公开攻击。

senses.title: Weaken an argument
senses.definition: to make a case less convincing by removing the support under one of its claims
senses.definitionCN: 抽掉某个主张底下的支撑，使论证不那么令人信服
senses.example: One weak example undermined the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一个薄弱的例证削弱了整个论证。
senses.why: An argument is a building of reasons, and the word is used for taking a load-bearing stone out of it.
senses.whyCN: 论证是由理由搭起的建筑，这个词就用来形容从中抽走一块承重的石头。

senses.title: Dig beneath a seam or deposit
senses.definition: in mining, to cut a tunnel under a body of coal or ore so that it can be removed
senses.definitionCN: 采矿中指在煤层或矿体下方开掘巷道以便采出
senses.example: Miners undermined the seam from a lower tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工从下方的巷道掏挖那层煤层。
senses.why: This is the technical sense that keeps the two halves of the word visible: under, and mine.
senses.whyCN: 这是让词的两个半截都保持可见的技术义：在下，以及挖掘。

senses.title: Sap physical strength
senses.definition: of illness, hunger or overwork, to wear down a person's strength slowly
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、饥饿或过劳缓慢损耗一个人的体力
senses.example: Illness had undermined his strength over the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病在冬天里一点点损耗了他的体力。
senses.why: The body also has foundations, and slow removal from below describes a decline that no single event explains.
senses.whyCN: 身体也有根基，而从下方缓慢抽走，描述的是一种无法归因于单一事件的衰退。

senses.title: Break the ground under trust
senses.definition: to make the trust between people or groups collapse through repeated small betrayals
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复的小背叛使人或群体之间的信任崩塌
senses.example: Broken promises undermined the trust between them.
senses.exampleCN: 屡次食言破坏了他们之间的信任。
senses.why: Trust rests on a floor of kept promises, and this word describes the floor being taken away one tile at a time.
senses.whyCN: 信任铺在守诺的地板上，而这个词描述的就是地板被一块块抽走。

intro.en: Undermine is an English compound of under and mine. The first half is native Old English; the second came through Old French and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语由「在下」与「矿、挖掘」构成的复合词。前半是本土古英语，后半经古法语而来，其更深来源不明。

items.en: Under is a native preposition and prefix meaning below, and it has shaped hundreds of English compounds.
items.cn: under 是本土介词与副词，意为在下方，它参与构成了数以百计的英语复合词。

items.en: The noun meant a mine, an ore bed or a subterranean passage, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个名词意为矿、矿层或地下通道，英语在中世纪借入。

items.en: The written source is mina, but its own origin is uncertain; it may have come from a Celtic word for ore.
items.cn: 有记载的来源是 mina，但它自身的来源不明，可能来自某支凯尔特语中表示矿石的词。

items.en: The verb first meant to dig under a wall or a fort so that it would fall; the military sense is the oldest recorded one.
items.cn: 这个动词最初意为在墙或堡垒底下挖掘使之倒塌；军事义是最早有记载的义项。

items.en: From digging under defences the word moved to weakening confidence, authority and trust; the date of each shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 从在防线底下挖掘，这个词转向削弱信心、权威与信任；每次转变的年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine uses it for slow declines of strength and immunity that no single cause can explain.
items.cn: 医学用它形容无法归因于单一原因的体力与免疫力缓慢衰退。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like undermine; the second group names neighbouring ways of weakening something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 undermine 相近；第二组是与「削弱、破坏」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of weakening something from below or in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 指从下方或暗中削弱某物的行为。

entries.definition: A person who quietly damages a plan or an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指暗中破坏计划或权威的人。

entries.definition: An excavation for ore, or the act of digging one; the second half of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿坑，或挖掘矿坑的行为；是本词的后半部分。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the earth; it shares the prefix but not the mining verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指地面之下；共享前缀，但不含那个挖掘动词。

entries.definition: To take on a task; it shares the prefix but has an unrelated second half.
entries.definitionCN: 指承担任务；共享前缀，但后半部分无关。

entries.definition: To make less strong; the broad word, with no image of digging or secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变弱；最宽泛的词，不含挖掘或隐秘的意象。

entries.definition: To wear something away gradually by wind, water or friction; it stresses slow surface loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指风、水或摩擦逐渐磨损；强调表面的缓慢流失。

entries.definition: To damage something deliberately, usually from inside an organisation; it stresses intent.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意破坏，通常从组织内部下手；强调意图。

entries.definition: To overturn an authority or system from within; it stresses turning the order upside down.
entries.definitionCN: 指从内部颠覆权威或制度；强调把秩序翻过来。

entries.definition: To reduce the function of something; it stresses loss of working ability rather than support.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低某物的功能；强调工作能力的损失，而非支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two visible halves, under and mine, and the image of ground removed from beneath.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用两个看得见的半截——「在下」与「挖掘」，以及从底下抽走地面的意象。

normal.en: Say the two halves in order: under, then mine. The word is a tunnel dug beneath a wall.
normal.cn: 按顺序念两个半截：先「在下」，再「挖掘」。这个词就是在墙底下挖的一条坑道。

normal.en: A wall can look perfect from the street while the ground beneath it has already been taken away.
normal.cn: 一面墙从街上看似完好，它底下的土却早已被掏走。

normal.en: A rumour works like water in a brick joint: no hammer, but the joint gets wider.
normal.cn: 谣言像砖缝里的水：没有锤子，缝却越来越宽。

normal.en: The word is always gradual; it never means one clean blow.
normal.cn: 这个词总是渐进的，从不指干净利落的一击。

normal.en: The secret is part of the meaning: the damage is done where no one is looking.
normal.cn: 隐秘是意义的一部分：破坏发生在没人看的地方。

abstract.en: Undermining is the quiet form of opposition, and it is harder to answer than an open attack.
abstract.cn: 暗中破坏是反对的安静形式，比公开攻击更难回应。

abstract.en: Structures fail from below long before they fail from the front.
abstract.cn: 结构从下方失效，远早于它从正面失效。

abstract.en: What is undermined is not destroyed but left standing on nothing.
abstract.cn: 被掏空的东西不是被摧毁，而是被留在虚无之上继续立着。

examples.en: The constant flooding undermined the road's foundations.
examples.cn: 反复的洪水损毁了那条路的地基。

examples.en: His careless remarks undermined the peace talks.
examples.cn: 他轻率的言论破坏了和谈。

examples.en: Low pay undermines the morale of the whole team.
examples.cn: 低薪削弱了整个团队的士气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安德曼」——「安德」是「在下」，在墙「曼」慢地挖，墙就从底下空了：暗中削弱

root: 古英语 under「在下」+ 古法语 mine「矿、挖掘」→ 中古英语 undermine「在墙下挖坑道使之倒塌」→ 现代义「从根基上逐渐削弱、暗中破坏」；其中「矿」的更深来源不明，可能出自凯尔特语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one direction, from below and often unseen: a foundation, a plan, a confidence, an authority, a reputation, an argument, a coal seam, a body and the trust between people.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一个方向——自下而上、常在暗处：地基、计划、信心、权威、声誉、论证、煤层、身体，以及人与人之间的信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water taking sand out of a brick joint until the wall stands on emptiness.
core.cn: 核心意象：水把砖缝里的沙一点点带走，直到墙立在空处。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE BRANCH: water takes a bridge's foundation, and miners cut under a seam.
branches.cn: 实物根基分支：水掏空桥基，矿工在煤层下方开挖。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND ARGUMENT BRANCH: leaks damage a campaign and one weak example damages a case.
branches.cn: 计划与论证分支：泄密破坏行动，一个薄弱例证破坏论证。

branches.en: THE INNER STRENGTH BRANCH: criticism lowers confidence and illness lowers bodily strength.
branches.cn: 内在力量分支：批评压低信心，疾病损耗体力。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY BRANCH: a scandal removes the ground a minister stands on.
branches.cn: 权威分支：丑闻抽走部长脚下的地基。

branches.en: THE REPUTATION AND TRUST BRANCH: rumours spoil a name and broken promises spoil a bond.
branches.cn: 声誉与信任分支：谣言毁掉名声，食言毁掉纽带。

intro.en: Undermine is a native prefix on a borrowed noun, and the join is so old that English speakers no longer feel the two parts separately.
intro.cn: 这是一个本土前缀加在借来的名词上，接合得太久，英语使用者已不再分别感觉这两个部分。

latinIntro.en: The second half reached English through Old French from Medieval Latin mina, a word of uncertain origin that may be Celtic.
latinIntro.cn: 后半部分经古法语、来自中世纪拉丁语 mina，这个词来源不明，可能出自凯尔特语。

items.example: It fixes the direction of the damage from the start.
items.exampleCN: 它从一开始就定下破坏的方向。

items.meaning: a pit for ore, a subterranean passage
items.example: The noun supplies the digging that the verb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供动词所描述的挖掘动作。

items.structure: English verb converted from the noun
items.example: English turned the pit into an action without adding an ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个坑直接变成动作，没有加词尾。

items.example: It forms the noun for the slow work of weakening.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「缓慢削弱」这一工作的名词。

items.example: It names the person who digs from below.
items.exampleCN: 它命名从下方挖掘的人。

items.example: It forms undermined, a position already weakened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 undermined，表示已被削弱的处境。

items.meaning: the act of weakening from below
items.meaningCN: 从下方逐渐削弱的行为
items.example: The constant undermining of trust ruined the talks.
items.exampleCN: 对信任的持续侵蚀毁了会谈。

items.meaning: one who digs from below or weakens in secret
items.meaningCN: 从下方挖掘或暗中削弱的人
items.example: An underminer works out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 暗中破坏者在看不见的地方行事。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「暗中破坏；起削弱作用的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「暗中破坏者」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被削弱的；根基受损的」

definition_zh: 减轻；缓和；缓解；使缓和
definition_en: to make damage, risk or hardship less severe, especially by taking action in advance
core_image: 洪水到来前，人在堤脚铺开一层缓冲石，浪头拍到堤面时被卸掉一半的力
scene: 工程开工前先改设计，把可能出现的沉降控制在可接受范围内。 Careful design can mitigate the risk of settlement.
sceneCN: 这里指提前降低风险程度（第 2 个义项：缓和冲击或风险）；句意为精心设计能缓和沉降风险。图中可辨识物件：堤脚铺开的缓冲石、拍上堤面的浪头、卸力后散开的水花。

pos.zh: 减轻；缓和；缓解

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「减轻；缓解」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「起缓和作用的」，法律中指减轻情节
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「缓解者」（少用）
由否定前缀加已然词构成，义为「未减弱的；彻底的」

senses.title: To reduce harm
senses.definition: to lower the amount of harm that an event or action causes
senses.definitionCN: 降低某一事件或行为造成的损害量
senses.example: Early warning mitigated the damage from the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 提前预警减轻了洪水造成的损害。
senses.why: The root is mild, and making harm mild is the whole idea of the word.
senses.whyCN: 词根是「温和」，把伤害化温和就是这个词的全部意思。

senses.title: To lower a risk
senses.definition: to reduce the probability or severity of a future danger
senses.definitionCN: 降低未来危险发生的可能或严重程度
senses.example: Regular inspection mitigates the risk of failure.
senses.exampleCN: 定期检查降低了失效风险。
senses.why: Risk is a future weight, and mitigation is placed before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 风险是未来的重量，而缓解是在它到来之前先布置。

senses.title: To ease pressure or pain
senses.definition: to make a burden or a sensation less severe for those experiencing it
senses.definitionCN: 让承受者的负担或感受变得不那么严重
senses.example: Respite care mitigated the strain on the family.
senses.exampleCN: 喘息照护缓解了这个家庭的负担。
senses.why: This is the everyday use, where the mild root meets a person's experience.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常用法，温和的词根与人切身的感受相遇。

senses.title: To reduce a penalty
senses.definition: to lower the severity of a punishment or a legal liability
senses.definitionCN: 降低处罚或法律责任的严厉程度
senses.example: The court mitigated the sentence because of his cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 考虑到他的配合，法院减轻了判决。
senses.why: Law treats a penalty as a weight that may be reduced, hence mitigation in sentencing.
senses.whyCN: 法律把处罚当作可以减轻的重量，所以量刑中有「减轻」。

senses.title: To slow climate change
senses.definition: to reduce the rate or scale of a long-term environmental change
senses.definitionCN: 降低长期环境变化的速度或规模
senses.example: Cutting emissions mitigates but does not reverse warming.
senses.exampleCN: 减排能减缓变暖，却不能逆转它。
senses.why: Climate writing uses the verb for slowing a process, not for undoing it.
senses.whyCN: 气候写作把这个动词用于「放慢过程」，而不是「撤回结果」。

senses.title: To cut a loss or cost
senses.definition: to make the financial or material cost of an event smaller
senses.definitionCN: 降低某一事件在金钱或材料上的代价
senses.example: The reserve fund mitigated the loss from the cancelled order.
senses.exampleCN: 储备金减少了订单取消带来的损失。
senses.why: Losses are counted, and to mitigate is to bring the count down.
senses.whyCN: 损失是要计数的，而缓解就是把计数降下来。

senses.title: To soften a conflict
senses.definition: to make a dispute or a disagreement less sharp without settling it
senses.definitionCN: 使争端或分歧不那么尖锐，但不一定解决它
senses.example: A neutral chair mitigated the tension in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一位中立的主持人缓和了会上的紧张。
senses.why: Conflict is heat, and the word lowers it rather than putting it out.
senses.whyCN: 冲突是热度，这个词是降温而非灭火。

senses.title: To relieve symptoms
senses.definition: to make the signs of an illness less troublesome while the cause remains
senses.definitionCN: 在病因仍在的情况下，使疾病表现不那么难受
senses.example: The cream mitigates itching but does not treat the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药膏能减轻瘙痒，却不处理病因。
senses.why: Medicine separates relief from cure, and mitigation sits firmly on the relief side.
senses.whyCN: 医学区分缓解与治愈，而缓解稳稳站在「缓解」这一边。

intro.en: Mitigate comes from Latin mitigare, to soften or make mild, from mitis, mild. The second element is generally taken to be agere, to do, though the exact formation is debated.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 mitigare「使软、使温和」，出自 mitis「温和」；第二部分一般认为是 agere「做」，但确切构词方式有争议。

items.en: Mitis meant mild, soft or ripe, and it described both weather and temperament.
items.cn: 这个词意为温和、柔软或成熟，既形容天气也形容性情。

items.en: The verb meant to soften, soothe or appease, and it was used of anger, pain and harsh measures.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使软、安抚、平息，用于怒气、疼痛与严厉措施。

items.en: The tail of mitigare is generally explained as agere, to do, but the exact formation is debated, so its source is uncertain.
items.cn: 词尾一般解释为 agere「做」，但确切构词有争议，宜标为来源不确定。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century, first for tempering harshness and later for reducing harm.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪采用这个动词，先指使严厉变缓，后指减少损害。

items.en: Sentencing and climate policy both gave the verb fixed objects, penalty and emissions.
items.cn: 量刑与气候政策都给这个动词添了固定宾语：刑罚与排放。

items.en: The verb militate, to have force against, comes from miles, a soldier, and must not be confused with mitigate.
items.cn: militate「产生不利作用」出自 miles「士兵」，不可与这个词混淆。

note.en: The first group shares the mild stem or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of relief.
note.cn: 第一组与「mitigate」共享「温和」词干或只是形近；第二组是与「缓解」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for circumstances that reduce blame.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指减轻责任的（情节）。

entries.definition: Not softened at all, hence complete or absolute.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全未减弱的，引申为彻底的。

entries.definition: To work against something, from miles, a soldier; a classic confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生不利作用，出自「士兵」，是经典的易混词。

entries.definition: To intervene between parties, from medius, middle.
entries.definitionCN: 指居中调停，出自「中间」。

entries.definition: To lighten pain or hardship, often after the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻痛苦或困苦，多在事后。

entries.definition: To bring down an amount, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低数量，是宽泛中性的说法。

entries.definition: To make smaller in degree or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指在程度或数量上变小。

entries.definition: To soften the force of something by mixing or moderating.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过掺和或节制削弱力度。

entries.definition: To make something less difficult or painful.
entries.definitionCN: 指使不那么困难或痛苦。

entries.definition: To make less hard or less severe, the literal root picture.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变软或变缓，正是词根的字面画面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the mild root, the legal phrase mitigating circumstances, and the false twin militate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「温和」词根、法律短语「减轻情节」，以及易混的 militate。

normal.en: Mitis is mild, so mitigate is to take the edge off something harsh.
normal.cn: mitis 是「温和」，所以这个词就是把锋利的地方磨钝。

normal.en: Mitigation is what you do before the flood, not after it.
normal.cn: 缓解是在洪水到来之前做的，不是之后。

normal.en: Law speaks of mitigating circumstances that lower a penalty.
normal.cn: 法律说「减轻情节」，用来降低处罚。

normal.en: Militate looks similar but comes from soldier and means to work against.
normal.cn: militate 形似，却出自「士兵」，意为产生不利作用。

normal.en: Climate policy pairs mitigate with adapt: one slows the change, the other lives with it.
normal.cn: 气候政策把「减缓」与「适应」配对：一个放慢变化，一个与之共存。

abstract.en: To mitigate is to accept that the harm will arrive and decide how much of it to absorb.
abstract.cn: 缓解，就是承认伤害会来，然后决定吸收掉其中多少。

abstract.en: A cushion does not stop the blow; it lengthens the time over which the blow is felt.
abstract.cn: 缓冲垫并不挡住打击，它只是拉长感受这一击的时间。

abstract.en: Whatever cannot be removed can still be made mild, and the word lives in that remaining room.
abstract.cn: 去不掉的东西仍可变得温和，这个词就活在那点剩下的余地。

examples.en: Planting trees along the bank mitigated erosion after the floods.
examples.cn: 沿河岸植树减轻了洪水后的侵蚀。

examples.en: The team mitigated the risk by testing each joint twice.
examples.cn: 团队把每个接缝测了两遍，以降低风险。

examples.en: The ruling mitigated the fine because the firm reported early.
examples.cn: 由于该公司主动报告，裁决减轻了罚款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米提盖特」——堤脚先铺缓冲石，浪头拍到就卸一半：减轻、缓和

root: 拉丁语 mitis「温和」→ mitigare「使软、使缓和」；第二成分一般认为是 agere「做」，但确切构词有争议，构成成分来源不确定。英语十六世纪引入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all take the edge off something: harm, risk, pressure, penalty, warming, loss, conflict and symptoms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在磨钝某个东西的锋边：损害、风险、压力、处罚、变暖、损失、冲突与症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: buffer stones are laid before the flood, and the wave spends half its force on them.
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水到来前先铺缓冲石，浪头把一半的力耗在石上。

branches.en: THE HARM IS CUT: damage or financial loss is counted lower than it would have been.
branches.cn: 损害被削：实际损害或金钱损失比原本更低。

branches.en: THE FUTURE IS CUSHIONED: a danger is made less likely or less severe before it arrives.
branches.cn: 未来被垫住：危险在到来之前就被降低可能或严重度。

branches.en: THE BURDEN IS LIGHTENED: strain and symptoms are made easier to carry.
branches.cn: 负担变轻：压力与症状变得较易承受。

branches.en: THE PENALTY IS SOFTENED: a punishment or liability loses part of its weight.
branches.cn: 处罚被软化：刑罚或责任卸去一部分重量。

branches.en: THE PROCESS IS SLOWED: warming or a dispute loses heat without being extinguished.
branches.cn: 过程被放慢：变暖或争端降了温，却没有被扑灭。

senses.title: An order or agreement to stop shooting
senses.titleCN: 停止射击的命令或约定
senses.definition: an instruction or arrangement by which opposing forces stop firing, usually for a set time or area
senses.definitionCN: 交战双方停止射击的指令或安排，通常限定时间或区域
senses.example: The mediator announced a ceasefire, and the shooting stopped by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 调解人宣布停火，到中午枪声就停了。
senses.why: cease is 'to stop' and fire is 'shooting', so the compound names the stopping of shooting directly.
senses.whyCN: cease 是「停止」，fire 是「射击」，因此这个复合词直接命名「停止射击」。

senses.title: The state of no firing
senses.definition: the condition in which no shots are being fired along a line or in an area
senses.definitionCN: 沿某条战线或某个区域内没有射击的状态
senses.example: A fragile ceasefire held while the negotiators met.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判代表会面期间，一个脆弱的停火得以维持。
senses.why: a command creates a state, and English often lets the same noun name both the order and the condition it produces.
senses.whyCN: 命令造成状态，英语常让同一个名词既指命令，也指它造成的状态。

senses.title: A written or spoken agreement
senses.titleCN: 书面或口头的停火协议
senses.definition: a formal or informal deal that fixes when and where firing will stop
senses.definitionCN: 确定何时何地停止射击的正式或非正式约定
senses.example: The ceasefire agreement set a corridor for aid.
senses.exampleCN: 停火协议划出了一条援助走廊。
senses.why: the word is used for the document as well as the act, as with treaty and armistice.
senses.whyCN: 和 treaty、armistice 一样，这个词既指行为，也指文书。

senses.title: A unilateral declaration
senses.definition: a halt declared by one side without the other's consent, often to gain political advantage
senses.definitionCN: 一方未经对方同意而宣布的停止射击，常为取得政治优势
senses.example: The government offered a unilateral ceasefire at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在午夜单方面提出停火。
senses.why: one party can stop shooting alone; the word does not require reciprocity, though it often implies it.
senses.whyCN: 一方可以独自停止射击；这个词并不要求对等，尽管通常暗示对等。

senses.title: A humanitarian pause
senses.definition: a short, local halt arranged so that aid, evacuation or burial can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 为援助、撤离或掩埋而安排的短时局部停火
senses.example: A humanitarian ceasefire let convoys cross the front.
senses.exampleCN: 人道主义停火让车队穿过前线。
senses.why: when the purpose is saving lives rather than settling the war, the compound takes a humanitarian modifier.
senses.whyCN: 当目的在救命而非解决战争时，这个复合词会带人道主义修饰语。

senses.title: A ceasefire that is broken
senses.definition: a halt that fails, with firing resuming and blame traded by both sides
senses.definitionCN: 未能维持、射击恢复且双方互相指责的停火
senses.example: The ceasefire collapsed after a single mortar round.
senses.exampleCN: 一发迫击炮弹就让停火崩溃。
senses.why: a pause is fragile because it rests on restraint, not on settlement; the word therefore appears with collapse and violation.
senses.whyCN: 暂停是脆弱的，因为它依赖克制而非解决；因此这个词常与「崩溃」「违反」搭配。

senses.title: Figurative halt of intense attacks
senses.definition: by extension, a pause in a fierce non-military campaign such as cyber attacks or hostile publicity
senses.definitionCN: 引申指网络攻击或敌意宣传等非军事激烈行动的暂停
senses.example: The platforms called a ceasefire in the disinformation war.
senses.exampleCN: 各平台在虚假信息战中呼吁停火。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the gunfire image and applies it to any exchange of blows at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留枪火意象，把它用于任何远程交火。

senses.title: Abstraction: a cooling of a conflict system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：冲突系统的冷却
senses.definition: any agreed reduction of intensity in a hostile system, seen as a cooling rather than a cure
senses.definitionCN: 敌对系统中任何约定的强度下降，被视为降温而非治愈
senses.example: A ceasefire lowers the temperature, but the dispute remains.
senses.exampleCN: 停火降低了温度，但争端仍在。
senses.why: the deepest sense is thermodynamic rather than legal: intensity falls, structure stays.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是热力学式的而非法律式的：强度下降，结构不变。

intro.en: Ceasefire joins an Old French verb of stopping to the native English word for fire. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceasefire 把古法语「停止」动词与英语本族词「火」连接起来，属近代复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old French cesser 'to stop, give way' came from Latin cessare, a frequentative of cedere 'to go, yield'.
items.cn: 古法语 cesser「停止、让出」来自拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「行走、让出」的反复动词。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, withdraw, yield'; cessare repeated the action, giving the sense of holding off or stopping.
items.cn: cedere 意为「行走、退去、让出」；cessare 表示反复，产生「退开、停止」之义。

items.en: Fire descends from Old English fȳr and Proto-Germanic *fōr; the Indo-European ancestor is usually reconstructed as *perjos, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: fire 承自英语 fȳr 与原始日耳曼语 *fōr；其印欧祖形通常重构为 *perjos，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The compound cease-fire appeared in military writing in the early twentieth century, when industrialized armies needed a word for a scheduled halt of artillery.
items.cn: cease-fire 这一复合词在二十世纪初的军事写作中出现，当时工业化军队需要一个词来指按计划停止炮击。

items.en: After the First World War the term moved into diplomacy and then into figurative use for any intense campaign.
items.cn: 第一次世界大战之后，这个词进入外交领域，随后引申用于任何激烈行动。

items.en: Source uncertain (coinage date): dictionaries differ on the first printed use, and the Indo-European roots of both fire and cedere are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（造词年代）：辞书对最早印刷用例说法不一，且 fire 与 cedere 的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds stop-fighting terms that overlap with ceasefire; group two holds the wider diplomatic and military ideas around it.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ceasefire 重叠的停止战斗类词；第二组是围绕它的更广的外交与军事概念。

entries.definition: Simply to stop or bring to an end; it needs an object, as in cease firing, and carries no agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指停止或终止；需要宾语，如停止射击，且不含约定之意。

entries.definition: The act of stopping, often used in phrases such as cessation of hostilities; it is more formal and less specific than ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指停止的行为，常用于「停止敌对行动」等短语；比 ceasefire 更正式、更宽泛。

entries.definition: Agreements limiting weapons types or numbers; they shape the future of a conflict rather than stop present firing.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制武器种类或数量的协定；它塑造冲突的未来，而非停止当下的射击。

entries.definition: A short agreed stop in fighting; it is older and plainer, and often briefer than a ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指约定短时停止战斗；更古老、更口语，通常比停火更短暂。

entries.definition: A formal suspension of hostilities, usually while peace is negotiated; it is generally more binding than a ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式休战，通常在谈判和平期间；一般比停火更具约束力。

entries.definition: A settlement that ends a war and fixes the postwar order; a ceasefire only stops the shooting.
entries.definitionCN: 指结束战争、确定战后秩序的解决方案；停火只停止射击。

entries.definition: A deliberate lowering of tension or force; it may occur without any formal halt in firing.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意降低紧张或武力强度；不一定伴随正式停火。

entries.definition: An area where fighting is excluded by agreement; it is a spatial arrangement that a ceasefire may protect.
entries.definitionCN: 指经约定排除战斗的区域；这是空间安排，停火可用于保护它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real words, the Latin chain behind cease and the compound's modern military setting.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词、cease 背后的拉丁链条，以及这个复合词的近代军事背景。

normal.en: cease 'stop' + fire 'shooting': the name says exactly what stops.
normal.cn: cease「停止」+ fire「射击」：这个名字直接说出停的是什么。

normal.en: Cease goes back through French to Latin cessare, a repeated cedere, 'to withdraw'.
normal.cn: cease 经法语上溯拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「退去」的反复形式。

normal.en: The family runs cease, cessation, ceasefire, fire, gunfire, firepower.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cease、cessation、ceasefire、fire、gunfire、firepower。

normal.en: A ceasefire is a pause, not a settlement: the war is still legally alive.
normal.cn: 停火是暂停而非解决：战争在法律上仍然存在。

normal.en: Typical partners are declare, broker, violate and collapse.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「宣布」「斡旋」「违反」「崩溃」。

abstract.en: Picture a loud machine switched to silent mode without being unplugged.
abstract.cn: 想象一台吵闹的机器被调到静音，却并未拔掉电源。

abstract.en: Picture a fever brought down by medicine: the disease is still in the body.
abstract.cn: 想象用药物把高烧退下：病还在体内。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted in a game: play stops, but the score is unchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象比赛中举起一只手：比赛停了，比分未变。

examples.en: Both sides accused each other of breaking the ceasefire.
examples.cn: 双方都指责对方破坏停火。

examples.en: The ceasefire allowed aid trucks to reach the valley.
examples.cn: 停火让援助卡车得以抵达山谷。

examples.en: A ceasefire without monitoring rarely lasts.
examples.cn: 没有监督的停火很少能持久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cease（停止）+ fire（开火）」——停止开火 → 停火

root: cease 经古法语 cesser 来自拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「退去、让出」的反复动词；fire 来自古英语 fȳr，属日耳曼语本族词。复合为「停止射击」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from the literal order to stop shooting, through the state and the document, to unilateral and humanitarian versions, to a broken halt, a metaphor for any campaign and finally a general cooling of conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的停止射击命令出发，经过停火状态与文书，再到单方面与人道主义变体，再到被破坏的停火，再到任何行动的比喻，最后落到冲突的普遍降温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of rifles lowered at once while smoke still rises from the barrels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排步枪同时放下，枪管仍在冒烟。

branches.en: ORDER AND CONDITION: the command creates the quiet it names.
branches.cn: 命令与状态：命令造出它所命名的安静。

branches.en: PAPER OR ONE VOICE: a deal can be signed by two or offered by one.
branches.cn: 纸面或单方：协议可由两方签署，也可由一方提出。

branches.en: MERCY AND FAILURE: a pause to save lives can still break under one shell.
branches.cn: 仁慈与失败：为救命的暂停仍可能被一发炮弹打破。

branches.en: BORROWED GUNFIRE: any distant exchange of blows can be paused this way.
branches.cn: 借来的枪火：任何远程交火都能这样暂停。

branches.en: COOLING, NOT CURE: intensity falls while the structure of the dispute remains.
branches.cn: 降温而非治愈：强度下降，争端结构仍在。

intro.en: Ceasefire is a transparent English compound of a Latin-derived verb and a native noun, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: ceasefire 是透明的英语复合词，由拉丁来源动词与本族名词构成，两部分都可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin cessare and cedere build cease, cessation, cession and concede; fire has no Latin root and is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cessare 与 cedere 构成 cease、cessation、cession 与 concede；fire 无拉丁词根，属日耳曼语。

items.meaningCN: 一支部队能投送的火力

items.exampleCN: 枪声在广场上回荡。

definition_zh: 电磁波谱；电磁辐射按波长（或频率）排列形成的完整谱段
definition_en: the full range of electromagnetic radiation, ordered by wavelength or frequency from radio waves to gamma rays
core_image: 一条从左到右由长波到短波渐变的彩色谱带，左端标着射电，右端标着伽马
scene: 夜里，射电望远镜的抛物面朝向天空，机房里一排屏幕显示着不同波段的信号曲线。 Radio telescopes read the long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.
sceneCN: 这里指电磁波谱中波长最长的那一段（第 4 个义项：射电与微波部分）；句意为射电望远镜读取的是电磁波谱的长波端。图中可辨识物件：抛物面天线、控制屏、信号曲线、夜空。
