senses.title: The whole range of radiation
senses.definition: all electromagnetic radiation taken together, from the longest radio waves to the shortest gamma rays
senses.definitionCN: 从最长射电波到最短伽马射线的全部电磁辐射的总和
senses.example: The electromagnetic spectrum runs from radio waves to gamma rays without a gap.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁波谱从射电波延伸到伽马射线，中间没有空隙。
senses.why: A single ordering by wavelength turns many apparently separate phenomena into one family.
senses.whyCN: 按波长排成一条序列，就把许多看似分离的现象归为同一族。

senses.title: Named bands
senses.definition: the conventional divisions of the spectrum into radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma bands
senses.definitionCN: 把波谱按惯例分为射电、微波、红外、可见光、紫外、伦琴射线与伽马等波段
senses.example: Astronomers divide the electromagnetic spectrum into bands named after their wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家按波长把电磁波谱分成若干波段。
senses.why: The bands are administrative and historical rather than sharply physical, but they let people talk about regions.
senses.whyCN: 这些分段更多是管理与历史形成的，而非物理上截然分明，但它们让人能谈论某些区域。

senses.title: The visible portion
senses.definition: the narrow band that the human eye can detect, roughly between violet and red
senses.definitionCN: 人眼能够感知的狭窄波段，大致介于紫光与红光之间
senses.example: The human eye samples only a narrow slice of the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 人眼只取用电磁波谱中很窄的一段。
senses.why: Sight is a narrow window, and the phrase makes that narrowness visible by contrast.
senses.whyCN: 视觉只是一扇窄窗，这个说法通过对比让这种狭窄变得可见。

senses.title: Radio and microwave portion
senses.definition: the long-wavelength end used by radio telescopes, radar and communication links
senses.definitionCN: 射电望远镜、雷达与通信链路所使用的长波段
senses.example: Radio telescopes read the long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 射电望远镜读取的是电磁波谱的长波端。
senses.why: Long waves pass through dust and clouds, so this end of the spectrum reveals what optics cannot.
senses.whyCN: 长波能穿过尘埃与云层，因此波谱的这一端能揭示光学观测看不到的东西。

senses.title: Astronomical survey use
senses.definition: the practice of observing the same object in several bands to recover its full physical picture
senses.definitionCN: 在同一目标上观测多个波段，以还原其完整物理图景的做法
senses.example: Surveying the electromagnetic spectrum in many bands gives a fuller picture of a galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 在多个波段普查电磁波谱能给出更完整的星系图景。
senses.why: No single band tells the whole story, so astronomers stack observations across the spectrum.
senses.whyCN: 没有任何单一波段能讲完整个故事，因此天文学家把各波段观测叠在一起。

senses.title: Communication allocation
senses.definition: the regulated assignment of frequency ranges to operators and services
senses.definitionCN: 把频率范围按规定分配给运营商与业务的做法
senses.example: Regulators auction blocks of the electromagnetic spectrum to mobile operators.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构把电磁波谱中的若干频段拍卖给移动运营商。
senses.why: The spectrum is a finite public resource, so its use has to be divided by rules.
senses.whyCN: 波谱是有限的公共资源，其使用必须按规则划分。

senses.title: A plotted spectrum
senses.definition: a graph showing how much energy arrives at each wavelength or frequency
senses.definitionCN: 显示各波长或频率上到达多少能量的图
senses.example: A plot of the electromagnetic spectrum shows intensity against frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁波谱的图示以频率为横轴显示强度。
senses.why: Once the range is drawn as a graph, peaks and gaps become readable at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把范围画成图，峰与空隙就能一眼读出。

senses.title: Spectral fingerprints
senses.definition: the pattern of absorption or emission lines by which a substance can be identified
senses.definitionCN: 可用来识别物质的吸收线或发射线图案
senses.example: Each element leaves a unique pattern in the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 每种元素都在电磁波谱上留下独特的图案。
senses.why: Lines are element-specific, which turned the spectrum into a chemical fingerprint.
senses.whyCN: 谱线因元素而异，这就把波谱变成了化学指纹。

senses.title: The spectrum as a domain
senses.definition: the electromagnetic environment treated as a space to be controlled in communications and conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在通信与冲突中被视为需要掌控的电磁环境
senses.example: Modern forces plan to control the electromagnetic spectrum during a conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 现代军队计划在冲突中掌控电磁波谱。
senses.why: Military planners redefined a physical range as territory, which is a strategic rather than a scientific move.
senses.whyCN: 军事规划者把一段物理范围重新定义为「领土」，这是战略而非科学的操作。

intro.en: The phrase combines a nineteenth-century adjective for electricity and magnetism with a Latin word that Newton had already used for the band of prismatic colours. The pieces are well documented; the exact date of the full phrase is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把十九世纪表示电与磁的形容词，与一个已被牛顿用来指棱镜色带的拉丁词组合起来。各部分来源有据，整个短语的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, because rubbing amber produces static charge.
items.cn: 这个词指琥珀，因为摩擦琥珀会产生静电。

items.en: Magnes named the lodestone of Magnesia, the original natural magnet.
items.cn: 这个词指马格尼西亚的磁石，即最早被认识的天然磁体。

items.en: Spectrum meant an appearance or image, from the verb meaning to look.
items.cn: 这个词表示外观或影像，来自表示「看」的动词。

items.en: Newton used spectrum for the coloured band thrown by a prism, fixing the word in optics.
items.cn: 牛顿用这个词指棱镜投出的彩色带，使其在光学中定型。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics showed that electricity, magnetism and light are one phenomenon.
items.cn: 十九世纪的物理学证明电、磁与光是同一种现象。

items.en: The full phrase appears once the whole range of radiation was understood as a single ordered set, late in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 当全部辐射被理解为一条有序序列后，完整短语才出现，时在十九世纪晚期。

note.en: The first group shares the adjective or the noun spectrum; the second group names particular bands and kinds of range.
note.cn: 第一组共享形容词「电磁的」或名词「谱」；第二组指特定波段与范围类型。

entries.definition: Energy carried by oscillating electric and magnetic fields.
entries.definitionCN: 由振荡电场与磁场携带的能量。

entries.definition: A wave of coupled electric and magnetic fields.
entries.definitionCN: 电场与磁场相互耦合形成的波。

entries.definition: The field produced by charges and currents.
entries.definitionCN: 由电荷与电流产生的场。

entries.definition: A range of wavelengths or frequencies.
entries.definitionCN: 一段波长或频率范围。

entries.definition: Relating to a spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 与谱相关的。

entries.definition: The band of light the eye can see.
entries.definitionCN: 人眼能看见的那段光。

entries.definition: The frequencies used for radio communication.
entries.definitionCN: 用于无线电通信的频率范围。

entries.definition: A continuous range of frequencies set aside for a use.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种用途划出的一段连续频率。

entries.definition: The span between the shortest and longest waves observed.
entries.definitionCN: 所观测最短波与最长波之间的跨度。

entries.definition: The extent of wavelengths an instrument can record.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器能记录的波长范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the rainbow strip outward in both directions; abstract ones treat the spectrum as a single ordered map of one phenomenon.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着彩虹色带向两端延伸；抽象联想把波谱看作同一现象的一张有序地图。

normal.en: Prism in, rainbow out: that band is the visible part.
normal.cn: 棱镜进去，彩虹出来，那条色带就是可见部分。

normal.en: Stretch the rainbow far left and you reach radio waves.
normal.cn: 把彩虹向左拉得很远，就到了射电波。

normal.en: Stretch it far right and you reach gamma rays.
normal.cn: 向右拉得很远，就到了伽马射线。

normal.en: Radio telescopes work at the long-wave end where dust cannot block them.
normal.cn: 射电望远镜工作在尘埃挡不住的长波端。

normal.en: Every element writes its own lines on the strip.
normal.cn: 每种元素都在这条带上写下自己的谱线。

abstract.en: The spectrum is one axis: everything electromagnetic is a position on it.
abstract.cn: 波谱就是一根轴：一切电磁现象都是它上面的一个位置。

abstract.en: Bands are habits of speech, not walls in nature.
abstract.cn: 波段是说话的习惯，不是自然界的墙。

abstract.en: A resource becomes territory the moment someone writes rules for it.
abstract.cn: 资源一旦被人写下规则，就变成了领土。

examples.en: Visible light occupies only a small part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 可见光只占电磁波谱的一小部分。

examples.en: The satellite monitors several bands of the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星监测电磁波谱的若干波段。

examples.en: Engineers test how the material responds across the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 工程师测试该材料在整个电磁波谱上的响应。

dict_mnemonic.text: electromagnetic（电磁的）+ spectrum（谱）——电磁的谱，即电磁波谱

root: 由 electromagnetic 与 spectrum 组合。前者由希腊语 elektron「琥珀」与拉丁语 magnes「磁石」经 magnet 构成；后者来自拉丁语 spectrum「外观、影像」，出自表示「看」的动词。牛顿先以该词指棱镜色带，十九世纪晚期辐射被理解为一条有序序列后，完整短语才定型，确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses unroll one ordered strip: its whole length, its bands, its visible slice, its long-wave end, its uses, its regulation, its graphs, its lines and its strategic reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项展开同一条有序谱带：全长、分段、可见的一小段、长波端、用途、管理、图示、谱线与其战略解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip that shifts from long red waves to short violet ones, then keeps going both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条由长波红端过渡到短波紫端的谱带，并向两端继续延伸。

branches.en: THE CORE TWO: one continuous range and the conventional bands cut into it.
branches.cn: 核心两项：一条连续范围，以及在其上划分的惯用波段。

branches.en: THE TWO ENDS PEOPLE USE: the narrow visible slice and the long-wave end.
branches.cn: 人常用的两端：狭窄的可见段与长波段。

branches.en: THE USES: multi-band astronomy and regulated communication blocks.
branches.cn: 用途：多波段天文观测与受管制的通信频段。

branches.en: THE READINGS: intensity plotted against frequency, and lines that identify elements.
branches.cn: 读法：以频率为横轴画强度，以及可识别元素的谱线。

branches.en: THE STRATEGIC SHIFT: the same strip treated as a domain to control.
branches.cn: 战略转向：同一条谱带被当作需要掌控的领域。

intro.en: Two Greek and Latin roots plus a Latin noun of appearance make up the phrase, and its second element has generated a large family.
intro.cn: 两个希腊与拉丁词根加一个表示外观的拉丁名词构成了这个短语，其第二成分还衍生出一大族词。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies the word for amber, Latin supplies the lodestone and the noun for appearance; modern science combined them.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「琥珀」一词，拉丁语提供了「磁石」与表示外观的名词；近代科学把它们组合起来。

items.example: The word gave its name to electricity because amber holds charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词因琥珀能带电荷而成为「电」的名称来源。

items.example: It named the natural magnet found in one district.
items.exampleCN: 它指在某一地区发现的天然磁体。

items.example: Newton fixed its optical sense as the band of colours.
items.exampleCN: 牛顿把它的光学含义固定为彩色带。

items.example: The noun is built on the act of looking.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词建立在「看」这一动作上。

items.example: It marks the electrical half of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它标记形容词中「电」的那一半。

items.example: It turns the noun magnet into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词「磁体」变成形容词。

items.example: The ending appears in the Latin noun for a means of seeing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾出现在拉丁语中表示「观看手段」的名词里。

items.example: The adjective describes anything belonging to a spectrum.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述属于谱的事物。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「电的」与「磁的」两个成分构成，义为「电磁的」
本词第二成分的复数形式，义为「多个谱」
由本词第二成分加形容词词尾构成，义为「光谱的；谱的」
由本词第二成分加表示「观测、研究」的成分构成，义为「光谱学」
由本词第二成分加表示「观察仪器」的成分构成，义为「分光镜」
由本词第二成分加表示「测量仪器」的成分构成，义为「光谱仪」

definition_zh: 适应；使适应；改编；调整以适合；改装
definition_en: to change or be changed so as to fit new conditions, a new medium or a new purpose
core_image: 苗圃里一排幼苗从温室搬到露天，头几天盖着遮阳网，叶片慢慢转向新的光照
scene: 苗圃把温室里的幼苗搬到露天，头几天盖着遮阳网，叶片慢慢转向新的光照。 Young plants can adapt to stronger light within a week.
sceneCN: 这里指生物对新光照条件逐渐适应（第 1 个义项：适应环境气候）；句意为幼苗能在一周内适应更强的光照。图中可辨识物件：幼苗、遮阳网、温室门。

pos.zh: 适应；使适应；改编；调整

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加名词尾构成，义为「适应；改编作品」
由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「能适应的；可改编的」
由该形容词加名词尾构成，义为「适应性；可改编性」
由该动词加表示器具或施动者的名词尾构成，义为「适配器；改编者」
由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「适应的；有适应性的」

senses.title: To suit a climate or habitat
senses.definition: to become suited to the temperature, light, water or other conditions of a place
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐适合某地的温度、光照、水分或其他条件
senses.example: Polar plants can adapt to extreme cold.
senses.exampleCN: 极地植物能够适应极度寒冷。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fit, and the first thing a living thing must fit is the place it lives in.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为使合适，而生物首先要合适的就是它所居住的地方。

senses.title: To adjust to a new situation
senses.definition: to change one's habits or expectations so as to work within new circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 改变习惯或预期，以便在新环境中运转
senses.example: The staff will adapt to the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 员工将会适应新的时间表。
senses.why: Once fitting is applied to human arrangements, it covers shifts in work, rules and daily rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「使合适」用于人的安排，就涵盖了工作、规则与日常节奏的变化。

senses.title: To make something fit
senses.definition: to alter a person or thing so that it fits a requirement or a group
senses.definitionCN: 改变人或事物，使其符合某项要求或某一群体
senses.example: A good teacher can adapt to mixed abilities in one class.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师能够适应一个班里参差不齐的能力。
senses.why: The verb is transitive in Latin, so English can put the thing being fitted either as its object or behind the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在拉丁语里是及物的，因此英语既可把被调整之物放在宾语位置，也可放在短语之后。

senses.title: To adapt a work for another medium
senses.titleCN: 把作品改编成另一形式
senses.definition: to change a story, play or piece of music so that it can be presented in a different medium or for a different audience
senses.definitionCN: 改动故事、戏剧或音乐，使其能以另一种媒介呈现或面向另一批受众
senses.example: The studio can adapt to television by splitting the novel into six parts.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方可以把这部小说拆成六集，以改编成电视作品。
senses.why: A work must fit a new stage, screen or page, and the word for fitting became the word for rewriting.
senses.whyCN: 作品必须适合新的舞台、银幕或版面，于是「使适合」这个词变成了「改编」。

senses.title: To adjust a plan so that it fits
senses.definition: to change a plan, budget or design so that it meets a limit or a need
senses.definitionCN: 改动计划、预算或设计，使其符合某项限制或需求
senses.example: We can adapt to a smaller budget by cutting travel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以削减差旅，以调整方案适应更小的预算。
senses.why: Planning repeats the same fit: means are trimmed until they match the available resources.
senses.whyCN: 规划重复着同一个「合适」：手段被削减，直到与可用资源相配。

senses.title: To adjust bodily to a stimulus
senses.definition: to undergo a bodily change that reduces the response to a repeated stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 身体发生变化，使对重复刺激的反应减弱
senses.example: Eyes can adapt to dim light after a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛几分钟后就能适应昏暗的光线。
senses.why: The body fits itself to its surroundings without conscious design, and physiology kept the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 身体无需有意的设计就能使自己适合环境，生理学沿用了同一个动词。

senses.title: To conform to customs and rules
senses.definition: to change one's behaviour so that it agrees with the customs or expectations of a group
senses.definitionCN: 改变自身行为，使其与某群体的习俗或期待相符
senses.example: Newcomers may adapt to local customs within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新来者可能一年之内就顺应了当地习俗。
senses.why: Social life asks people to fit a pattern, and the verb covers that quiet conformity as well as physical change.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活要求人符合某种模式，这个动词既指身体变化，也指这种不声张的顺应。

senses.title: To modify equipment for a new use
senses.titleCN: 改装设备以适应新用途
senses.definition: to change a device or machine so that it works with new parts, fuel or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改动装置或机器，使其能配合新的零件、燃料或条件
senses.example: The workshop can adapt to metric parts by machining new fittings.
senses.exampleCN: 车间可以加工新的接头，使设备适应公制零件。
senses.why: Tools are fitted to tasks, and a machine altered for a new task is literally made suitable.
senses.whyCN: 工具要被适合任务，为新技术任务而改动的机器正是字面意义上的「被使合适」。

intro.en: Adapt comes from Latin adaptare, to fit something to something, from ad-, to or towards, and aptare, to make fit, from aptus, fit or fastened. English took the verb in the seventeenth century, and the phrase adapt to followed the verb's own construction.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「adaptare」「使某物适合某物」，由「ad-」「朝向」和「aptare」「使合适」构成，而「aptare」又出自「aptus」「合适的、系紧的」。英语在十七世纪引入这个动词，短语「adapt to」沿用了动词本身的搭配。

items.en: The adjective meant fit, suitable and also fastened, so fitness and attachment were one idea.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为合适的、适宜的，也有系紧之意，因此「合适」与「连接」是同一个概念。

items.en: The verb meant to make fit or to fasten, and it gave the action of putting a thing into its proper place.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使合适或系紧，给出了把事物放到恰当位置的动作。

items.en: The prefix meant towards, and it turned the fitting into a movement towards a particular condition.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为朝向，把「使合适」变成了朝某一特定条件靠拢的动作。

items.en: The compound meant to fit one thing to another, and it is the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为使一事物适合另一事物，是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the seventeenth century for fitting, and soon for rewriting a work for a new medium.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词表示使适合，很快又用于把作品改写以适合新媒介。

items.en: The preposition to marks the condition or purpose that is being fitted, and the phrase became fixed in ordinary and technical English.
items.cn: 介词「to」标出所适合的条件或目的，这个短语在普通英语与技术英语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that look or sound like adapt; the second group gathers verbs of fitting and changing.
note.cn: 第一组收录在形音上与「adapt」相近的形式；第二组收录表示使适合与改变的说法。

entries.definition: To fit or be fitted to new conditions; the base verb of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指使适合或被适合新条件；是该短语的基础动词。

entries.definition: The process or result of fitting, including a work rewritten for a new medium.
entries.definitionCN: 指适合的过程或结果，也包括为新媒介改写的作品。

entries.definition: Able to be changed so as to fit different conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够被改变以适合不同条件的。

entries.definition: To take a child or an idea as one's own; it looks close but its Latin verb means to choose.
entries.definitionCN: 指收养孩子或采纳想法；形近但其拉丁动词意为选择。

entries.definition: Highly skilled at something; it looks close but comes from a Latin word for having attained.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某事上非常熟练；形近但出自拉丁语表示「已达到」的词。

entries.definition: To change something slightly so that it works or fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 指稍作改动使某物运作更好或更合适。

entries.definition: To change in order to meet the needs of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为满足某人或某物的需要而作出改变。

entries.definition: To become used to a new climate or environment over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指随着时间逐渐习惯新的气候或环境。

entries.definition: To change something, often to improve it or give it a new purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指改动某物，常为改进或赋予新用途。

entries.definition: To make or change something so that it suits a particular person or purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指制作或改动某物，使其适合特定的人或目的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin sense of fitting, the real family of the verb, and the real phrases of climate, work and equipment.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「使合适」之义、这个动词的真实词族，以及气候、工作与设备的真实搭配。

normal.en: Aptus meant fit and fastened, so adapt began as the act of putting a thing where it belongs.
normal.cn: 「aptus」意为合适的、系紧的，因此「adapt」最初就是把事物放到它该在的位置。

normal.en: Adapt, adapter, adaptation and adaptable all carry the same idea of fitting.
normal.cn: 「adapt」「adapter」「adaptation」与「adaptable」都带着同一个「使合适」的意思。

normal.en: The phrase adapt to always needs a target: a climate, a timetable, a budget or a medium.
normal.cn: 短语「adapt to」总需要一个目标：气候、时间表、预算或媒介。

normal.en: An adapter is a small piece that makes one plug fit another socket, the word's meaning made visible.
normal.cn: 适配器是一个让小插头适合另一插座的小物件，正是这个词的意思变得可见。

normal.en: Eyes adapt to dim light, workers adapt to new rules, and both are the same quiet fitting.
normal.cn: 眼睛适应暗光，员工适应新规，两者都是同一种不声张的适合。

abstract.en: To adapt is to keep one's aim while changing one's shape, like water taking the shape of its cup.
abstract.cn: 适应就是保持目的而改变形状，像水取杯子的形状。

abstract.en: A species and a story survive by the same move: the form bends so that the core may continue.
abstract.cn: 物种与故事靠同一个动作存活：外形弯一弯，核心才能继续。

abstract.en: The deepest adaptation is invisible: the change has finished before anyone notices that it was needed.
abstract.cn: 最深的适应是看不见的：变化在别人察觉需要之前就已经完成。

examples.en: Desert animals can adapt to heat by resting in shade.
examples.cn: 沙漠动物可以通过在阴凉处休息来适应炎热。

examples.en: The director will adapt to a smaller stage by cutting two scenes.
examples.cn: 导演会删去两场戏，以适应更小的舞台。

examples.en: Older workers may adapt to the software after a short course.
examples.cn: 年长员工上完短期课程后可能就适应这款软件了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿达普特·图」——把自己调到合适的位置：适应、改编、改装

root: 拉丁语「adaptare」「使适合」=「ad-」「朝向」+「aptare」「使合适」←「aptus」「合适的、系紧的」；英语十七世纪引入，短语沿用动词自身搭配。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses extend the idea of fitting: fitting a climate, fitting a new situation, fitting another person, fitting a work to a medium, fitting a plan to a limit, fitting the body to a stimulus, fitting behaviour to custom, and fitting a machine to new parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项延伸「使合适」这一观念：适合气候、适合新情况、使他人适合、把作品改为另一媒介、让计划适合限制、身体适应刺激、行为顺应习俗、设备配合新零件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seedling is moved into stronger light, and its leaves turn until they face the new source.
core.cn: 核心意象：幼苗被移到更强的光下，叶片转动，直到朝向新的光源。

branches.en: THE LIVING FIT: a plant or a person settles into a climate and a new daily arrangement.
branches.cn: 生命的适合：植物或人安顿进一种气候与新的日常安排。

branches.en: THE DELIBERATE FIT: a teacher or a planner alters means until a requirement is met.
branches.cn: 有意的适合：教师或规划者调整手段，直到满足要求。

branches.en: THE WORK IN A NEW MEDIUM: a story is reshaped for stage, screen or page.
branches.cn: 新媒介中的作品：故事为舞台、银幕或版面重新塑形。

branches.en: THE BODY'S QUIET FIT: the senses dull their response to a repeated stimulus.
branches.cn: 身体的静默适合：感官对重复刺激的反应逐渐减弱。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AND MECHANICAL FIT: behaviour follows custom, and a machine takes new parts.
branches.cn: 社会与机械的适合：行为随习俗调整，机器换上新的零件。

intro.en: Adapt is a Latin verb of fitting, and its family covers both the living and the mechanical sides of the idea.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「使合适」的拉丁动词，其词族涵盖这一观念的生物与机械两面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies aptus, aptare and adaptare; the adjective aptus is the seed of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「aptus」、「aptare」与「adaptare」；形容词「aptus」是整个词族的种子。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「使合适」指向一个目标。

items.example: The adjective joins fitness with attachment.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把合适与连接合在一起。

items.example: The verb turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把形容词变成动作。

items.structure: Latin verb from ad- and aptare
items.meaning: to fit one thing to another
items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: English kept the adjective beside the longer verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语在较长的动词旁保留了这一形容词。

items.example: English shortened the Latin compound.
items.exampleCN: 英语缩短了这个拉丁复合词。

items.example: It forms the noun for the process and the rewritten work.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示过程与改写作品的名词。

items.example: It forms the word for being able to fit.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「能够适合」的词。

items.example: It forms the word for the fitting tendency.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「有适应倾向」的词。

definition_zh: 贸易协定；贸易协议；两国或多国就贸易条件达成的正式约定
definition_en: a formal arrangement between countries setting the terms on which they will trade
core_image: 一张长桌两端各坐一方代表，桌中央摊开一份文件，两枝笔同时落在签名栏上
scene: 部长级会谈结束后，双方代表在同一份文件上签字，约定削减关税并开放部分服务市场。 The two governments signed a trade agreement after three years of talks.
sceneCN: 这里指「国家间达成的贸易约定」，对应第 1 个义项：就关税、市场准入等条件形成的正式协议；句意为两国政府经过三年谈判签署了一份贸易协定。画面要点：长桌、双方代表、摊开的文件、签名栏。

pos.zh: 贸易协定；贸易协议（可数，复数 trade agreements）

derivatives.zh: 协议；同意（agree 加名词后缀，语义从「达成一致」转为「一致的结果」）
同意；达成一致（agreement 的基础动词，源自法语表示「使合意」）
令人愉快的；可接受的（agree 加形容词后缀，语义偏向合人心意）
分歧（dis- 加 agreement，指一致状态被取消）
贸易；交易（短语的前半，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）

senses.title: A formal pact on trade terms
senses.titleCN: 就贸易条件达成的正式约定
senses.definition: a formal arrangement in which countries set the rules and terms of trade between them
senses.definitionCN: 国家之间就贸易规则与条件形成的正式安排
senses.example: The two governments signed a trade agreement after three years of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府经过三年谈判签署了一份贸易协定。
senses.why: Agreement comes from a French verb meaning to bring two minds into one pleasure, so a trade agreement is two parties brought to one will about exchange.
senses.whyCN: agreement 出自法语动词，意为使两方心意合一；因此贸易协定就是把两方在交易上的意愿合成一个。

senses.title: A bilateral agreement between two countries
senses.definition: an agreement concluded between exactly two countries
senses.definitionCN: 恰好由两个国家缔结的协定
senses.example: The bilateral trade agreement cut tariffs on farm goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这份双边贸易协定削减了农产品关税。
senses.why: Counting the parties is the simplest way to classify agreements, so bilateral names the two-party case.
senses.whyCN: 按缔约方数量分类最为简单，因此双边专指两方的情形。

senses.title: A regional or multilateral agreement
senses.definition: an agreement among several countries, often forming a bloc or a common market
senses.definitionCN: 由若干国家缔结、常形成集团或共同市场的协定
senses.example: The regional trade agreement created a single tariff schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 这份区域贸易协定形成了统一关税表。
senses.why: When more parties join, the agreement becomes a framework that governs a whole region rather than a pair.
senses.whyCN: 当更多方加入，协定就成为治理整个区域而不是一对国家的框架。

senses.title: The legal text itself
senses.definition: the written instrument containing the agreed terms
senses.definitionCN: 载有约定条款的书面文书
senses.example: The trade agreement runs to four hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定长达四百页。
senses.why: An agreement can be both the understanding and the paper that records it, so the phrase names the document too.
senses.whyCN: 协定既可是共识，也可是记录共识的纸张，因此这个短语也指文件。

senses.title: The scope of the agreed terms
senses.definition: the subject areas covered, such as tariffs, services, rules of origin or investment
senses.definitionCN: 所覆盖的议题，如关税、服务、原产地规则或投资
senses.example: The trade agreement covers services as well as goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定既涵盖货物，也涵盖服务。
senses.why: Modern agreements are bundles of chapters, so the phrase often appears with covers, includes or excludes.
senses.whyCN: 现代协定是一捆章节，因此这个短语常与「涵盖」「包括」「不包括」搭配。

senses.title: A preferential agreement
senses.definition: an agreement granting lower tariffs or wider access than the general rules allow
senses.definitionCN: 给予比一般规则更低的关税或更宽的准入
senses.example: The preferential trade agreement spared small exporters the full duty.
senses.exampleCN: 这份优惠贸易协定使小出口商免缴全额关税。
senses.why: Preference is the point of most agreements: some partners get better terms than the default.
senses.whyCN: 多数协定的要点就是优惠：某些伙伴得到比默认更好的条件。

senses.title: The stage of ratification
senses.definition: the process by which the agreed text is approved and brought into force
senses.definitionCN: 使议定文本获得批准并开始生效的过程
senses.example: The trade agreement awaits ratification by both parliaments.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定有待两国议会批准。
senses.why: Signing is only a promise; the phrase also names the instrument during the period before it binds.
senses.whyCN: 签署只是承诺；这个短语也指在生效之前的那份文书。

senses.title: The framework for settling disputes
senses.titleCN: 作为争端解决框架的协定
senses.definition: the agreement viewed as the set of rules and procedures for resolving trade conflicts
senses.definitionCN: 被视为解决贸易冲突的规则与程序集合的协定
senses.example: The trade agreement provides for arbitration when talks fail.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定规定谈判失败时进行仲裁。
senses.why: A durable agreement outlives its signatories' goodwill, so it must contain a way to settle quarrels.
senses.whyCN: 一份持久的协定要超越签署方的善意，因此必须含有解决争执的办法。

intro.en: Trade agreement joins trade, a Germanic word of path and exchange, with agreement, from French agree, 'to bring to one will'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trade agreement 把源自日耳曼语、表示「路径与往来」的 trade，与出自法语 agree「使心意合一」的 agreement 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or welcome, and it built words about favour and thankfulness.
items.cn: gratus 意为令人愉快的、受欢迎的，构成一批关于恩惠与感谢的词。

items.en: French agreer, from a phrase meaning 'at pleasure', came to mean to consent or to suit.
items.cn: 法语 agreer 出自表示「随其所愿」的说法，后来意为同意或相合。

items.en: English agree appeared in the fourteenth century with the sense of coming to one mind.
items.cn: 英语 agree 在 14 世纪出现，意为达成一致。

items.en: The noun agreement named both the state of consent and the document recording it.
items.cn: 名词 agreement 既指同意的状态，也指记录同意的文件。

items.en: As states began to negotiate tariffs systematically, trade agreement became the standard name for the resulting instrument.
items.cn: 随着各国开始系统性地谈判关税，trade agreement 成为这类文书的标准名称。

note.en: The first group shares the pleasing root but has moved into other senses; the second group names other written understandings between states.
note.cn: 第一组共享「合意」词根但语义已转移；第二组是国家间其他形式的书面约定。

entries.definition: Any state of consent or any contract; a trade agreement is the specific case about commerce.
entries.definitionCN: 任何同意状态或任何契约；贸易协定是关于商业的具体情形。

entries.definition: To come to one mind; the noun adds the result and, in this phrase, the trade subject matter.
entries.definitionCN: 达成一致；名词加上结果，在这个短语中再加上贸易主题。

entries.definition: Pleasing or acceptable; it describes a quality, not a negotiated instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的或可接受的；它描述性质，不是谈判达成的文书。

entries.definition: Favour or elegance, from Latin gratia; it shares the pleasing root but has no commercial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 恩惠或优雅，出自拉丁 gratia；共享「合意」词根，却没有商业含义。

entries.definition: A formally concluded and ratified agreement between states; a trade agreement is one kind of treaty or treaty-like instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 国家间正式缔结并批准的协定；贸易协定是条约或类条约文书的一种。

entries.definition: A formal settlement between parties; it often covers a single dispute, while a trade agreement covers continuing trade.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式和解；它常针对单一争端，而贸易协定覆盖持续的贸易。

entries.definition: A short word for any agreement, often used in headlines; it lacks the legal precision of a trade agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 任何协定的简短说法，常见于标题；它没有贸易协定那样的法律精度。

entries.definition: A statement of intent that may not be legally enforceable; a trade agreement is normally binding.
entries.definitionCN: 意向声明，未必具有法律约束力；贸易协定通常是约束性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real consent root, the real trade word and real diplomatic phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「合意」词根、真实的贸易词与真实外交搭配。

normal.en: Agreement is two minds made one; adding trade says what they came to one mind about.
normal.cn: agreement 是两个心意合成一个；加上 trade 说明他们在什么上达成一致。

normal.en: The verb is agree and the noun is agreement, so the pair is transparent.
normal.cn: 动词是 agree，名词是 agreement，两者关系清楚。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: sign a trade agreement, negotiate a trade agreement, a bilateral trade agreement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：签署贸易协定、谈判贸易协定、双边贸易协定。

normal.en: Classify by parties: bilateral for two, regional or multilateral for several.
normal.cn: 按缔约方分类：两国为双边，多国为区域或多边。

normal.en: Signing is not the end: ratification brings the text into force.
normal.cn: 签字不是终点：批准才使文本生效。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching across a table to sign the same sheet at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手越过桌面，在同一刻签下同一张纸。

abstract.en: Picture two markets joined by a bridge whose planks are numbered clauses.
abstract.cn: 想象两个市场被一座桥连起，桥板就是一条条编号的条款。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook kept on the table even after the signatories stop liking each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则书一直放在桌上，即使签字方后来互不友好。

examples.en: The two countries are negotiating a trade agreement on services.
examples.cn: 两国正在就服务贸易谈判一份贸易协定。

examples.en: The trade agreement lowered tariffs on machinery.
examples.cn: 这份贸易协定降低了机械关税。

examples.en: Farm groups opposed the trade agreement's import rules.
examples.cn: 农业团体反对这份贸易协定的进口规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「把贸易条件谈成一致」——agree 是达成一致，加 trade 就是关于贸易的一致约定 → 贸易协定

root: trade 源自古英语与中古低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词；agreement 出自法语 agreer「使合意」，源自拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」。合指就贸易条件达成的正式约定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the pact itself, its two-party and multi-party forms, the document, its scope, its preferential terms, its ratification and its dispute rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一份文书展开：约定本身、双边与多边形式、文件、覆盖范围、优惠条款、批准程序，以及争端规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two delegations signing one sheet at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个代表团在同一刻签下同一张纸。

branches.en: BASE CONSENT: two parties are brought to one will about trade.
branches.cn: 基础合意：两方在贸易上被合成一个意愿。

branches.en: COUNTING PARTIES: two countries, or several forming a region.
branches.cn: 缔约方计数：两个国家，或若干国家组成区域。

branches.en: DOCUMENT AND SCOPE: the text records what the chapters cover.
branches.cn: 文件与范围：文本记录了各章覆盖的内容。

branches.en: TERMS AND VALIDITY: preferences are granted, then ratification makes them bind.
branches.cn: 条款与效力：先给优惠，再经批准使其生效。

branches.en: DURABLE RULES: the agreement must outlast goodwill and settle quarrels.
branches.cn: 持久规则：协定必须超越善意，并能解决争执。

intro.en: Trade agreement is a phrase of two free words, one Germanic and one built on a Latin root of favour.
intro.cn: trade agreement 由两个自由词构成，一个源自日耳曼语，一个建立在拉丁「合意」词根上。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus 'pleasing' gives grace, grateful, gratify and, through French, agree and agreement; trade gives trading, trader and trademark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」衍生 grace、grateful、gratify，并经由法语衍生 agree 与 agreement；trade 衍生 trading、trader 与 trademark。

items.example: The root builds words of favour.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根构成一批表示恩惠的词。

items.example: Both sides agreed on the terms.
items.exampleCN: 双方就条款达成一致。

items.example: They reached an agreement.
items.exampleCN: 他们达成了协议。

items.example: The terms are agreeable to both.
items.exampleCN: 这些条款双方都能接受。

items.example: A disagreement over quotas delayed the talks.
items.exampleCN: 配额上的分歧拖延了谈判。

items.example: The clause was kept as a grace period.
items.exampleCN: 该条款被保留为宽限期。

items.example: Trade between them doubled.
items.exampleCN: 他们之间的贸易翻了一番。

items.example: Trading resumed after the vote.
items.exampleCN: 投票后交易恢复。

items.example: They signed a border treaty.
items.exampleCN: 他们签署了边界条约。

items.example: A trade agreement was signed.
items.exampleCN: 一份贸易协定被签署。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 令人愉快的；受欢迎的；感激的

definition_zh: 页边的；微小的；边缘化的；边际的；以微弱差距的；贫瘠边缘的；生态边缘的；次要的
definition_en: situated at or near an edge, or so small and slight that it barely matters
core_image: 书页正文之外那条窄窄的空白，写满了小字，正文反倒显得像主体
scene: 两种涂料刷在墙上，屋里的人来回看了半天，几乎分不出哪一种更浅。 The difference between the two paints is marginal at best.
sceneCN: 这里指差别小到几乎可以忽略（第 2 个义项：数量上的差异极微小）；句意为这两种涂料的差别充其量也只是微乎其微。

pos.zh: 边缘的；微小的；边际的
边缘席位；边缘事物

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 margo「边缘」，是该形容词的词基，义为「页边；边缘；差额」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「略微；以微弱差距」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「边缘性；边缘地位」
由该形容词加表示「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使边缘化」
由「使边缘化」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「边缘化」

senses.title: Written in the page margin
senses.definition: placed in the blank border of a page rather than in the main body of text
senses.definitionCN: 放在页面的空白边栏里，而不是正文之中
senses.example: A marginal note in pencil corrected the date.
senses.exampleCN: 一条铅笔写的页边注改正了日期。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant edge or border, and a page's border is its most literal margin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为边缘或边界，书页的边栏就是最字面的「边缘」。

senses.title: So small it barely counts
senses.definition: very slight in amount or degree, close to the point of being unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上极小，接近无关紧要的地步
senses.example: The second product was only marginally cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 第二件商品只是略微便宜一点。
senses.why: A difference at the edge of measurement sits just inside or outside the line, so it is barely worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 处于测量边缘的差异，正好贴着界线内外，因此几乎不值得计数。

senses.title: Pushed to the edge of society
senses.definition: having little power, representation or acceptance within a larger society
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的社会中缺少权力、代表性或接纳度
senses.example: The report focuses on marginal groups in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注城市里的边缘群体。
senses.why: People placed outside the main body of a society are located at its border, exactly where the word points.
senses.whyCN: 被置于社会主体之外的人，就处在它的边界上，正是这个词所指的位置。

senses.title: The next unit in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学中再增加一单位
senses.definition: relating to the extra cost, benefit or utility of one additional unit
senses.definitionCN: 与再增加一个单位所带来的额外成本、收益或效用有关
senses.example: Marginal cost rises once the factory nears capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂接近产能上限时，边际成本会上升。
senses.why: Economics looks at the change at the edge of existing output, and that edge is the margin.
senses.whyCN: 经济学看的是现有产出边缘处的变化，而那个边就是「边际」。

senses.title: Decided by a tiny gap
senses.definition: won or lost by a very small number of votes or points, so the result could easily change
senses.definitionCN: 以极少的票数或分数取胜或落败，结果很容易翻转
senses.example: The party holds a marginal seat by two hundred votes.
senses.exampleCN: 该党以两百票的优势握有一个边缘选区。
senses.why: A result sitting on the boundary between win and loss is marginal in the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 停在胜负边界上的结果，在政治意义上就是「边缘的」。

senses.title: Land at the limit of farming
senses.definition: land whose soil or position makes farming only barely profitable
senses.definitionCN: 土壤或位置使耕作只能勉强获利的土地
senses.example: Marginal land is often left to grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 边缘土地常被留作放牧。
senses.why: Such land lies at the edge of what can be cultivated, so it carries the edge word by position.
senses.whyCN: 这类土地处在可耕种的边缘，因此按位置得到「边缘」之名。

senses.title: A habitat at the edge of a range
senses.definition: a habitat where a species survives at the limit of its tolerated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某物种在可忍受条件的极限处勉强存活的生境
senses.example: Marginal habitats hold fewer species but rare ones.
senses.exampleCN: 边缘生境物种较少，却常有珍稀种类。
senses.why: Ecology maps a range with a centre and a rim, and life at the rim lives on the margin.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把一个分布范围画成有中心有外围，住在外围的生命就处在边缘。

senses.title: Of secondary importance
senses.definition: playing a small or non-central part in a larger matter
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的事务中只起很小的、非核心的作用
senses.example: His role in the negotiation was marginal.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这场谈判中的作用很次要。
senses.why: Anything not in the main body of an affair is pushed to its edge, and the edge is where marginal things sit.
senses.whyCN: 不在事务主体之内的一切都被推到边上，而「边缘」正是这类事物所在之处。

intro.en: Marginal comes from Latin margo, marginis 'edge, border', through the adjective marginalis. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and economics and politics later gave it precise uses. The Latin source is certain; the earlier origin of margo is reconstructed rather than attested.
intro.cn: marginal 来自拉丁 margo、marginis「边缘、边界」，经形容词 marginalis 进入英语，十六世纪被采用，后来经济学与政治学又赋予它精确用法。拉丁来源确定；margo 更早的来源属于重构，并未留下实证。

items.en: Margo meant edge, border or brink, and it named the rim of a page, a field or a sea.
items.cn: margo 意为边缘、边界或崖沿，可指书页、田地或海的边沿。

items.en: The pre-Latin source of margo is not settled, and proposals for its deeper root remain reconstructions rather than recorded forms.
items.cn: margo 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，对其更深词根的种种设想仍属重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Medieval Latin marginalis meant 'of the margin', first for writing placed at the edge of a page.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 marginalis 意为「页边的」，最初指写在页边上的文字。

items.en: English marginal began with page notes, then widened to anything at an edge or limit.
items.cn: 英语的这个词从页边注开始，随后扩展到任何处于边缘或极限的事物。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economics used marginal for the extra cost or benefit of one more unit, giving marginal cost and marginal utility.
items.cn: 十九世纪经济学用这个词指再加一单位的额外成本或收益，产生「边际成本」与「边际效用」。

items.en: A marginal seat is won by a small gap, and a marginal group sits outside the centre of a society.
items.cn: 边缘选区以极小差距决出；边缘群体处在社会中心之外。

note.en: The first group shares the edge stem; the second group holds words for smallness or secondary position, each with a different reason.
note.cn: 第一组共享「边缘」词干；第二组是表示微小或次要的词，各自的理由不同。

entries.definition: The blank edge of a page, or the amount by which one value exceeds another.
entries.definitionCN: 页面的空白边，或一个数值超出另一个的差额。

entries.definition: Slightly, or by a very small amount; it modifies comparisons.
entries.definitionCN: 略微，或以极小数量；修饰比较。

entries.definition: The condition of being at the edge of a group or system; a sociological noun.
entries.definitionCN: 处于群体或系统边缘的状况；是社会学的名词。

entries.definition: To push a person or group to the edge of influence; it names the act, not the state.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或群体推到影响力的边缘；命名动作，而非状态。

entries.definition: Small in degree; it measures amount only and says nothing about position at an edge.
entries.definitionCN: 程度上很小；只量数量，不涉及是否处于边缘。

entries.definition: Low in importance; it ranks things, while the target word places them at a border.
entries.definitionCN: 重要性低；对事物排序，而目标词把它们放到边界上。

entries.definition: On the outer edge of a system, often beside the main concern; close, but more spatial and less numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 处于系统的外缘，常在主关注点旁边；意思接近，但更偏空间而非数量。

entries.definition: So small that it can be disregarded; stronger than the target word, which still allows the difference to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以不理会；比目标词更强，因为目标词仍承认这点差别有意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'edge': marginal things live at the edge of a page, a market or a society.
normal.cn: 词根意为「边缘」：边缘之物活在书页、市场或社会的边上。

normal.en: The family runs margin, marginally, marginality and marginalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括页边、略微、边缘性、使边缘化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark economics: marginal cost, marginal utility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出经济学：边际成本、边际效用。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark politics and society: marginal seat, marginal group.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政治与社会：边缘选区、边缘群体。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: slight is only small, negligible is almost nothing.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：slight 只是小，negligible 几乎是零。

abstract.en: Picture a page whose margin is filled while the centre stays blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸边栏写满，正文却空着。

abstract.en: Picture a runner finishing one stride behind the winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者比冠军差一步冲线。

abstract.en: Picture a town so close to the border that the sign is on its main street.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇贴着边界，界牌就立在主街上。

examples.en: The effect on test scores was marginal.
examples.cn: 对考试成绩的影响微乎其微。

examples.en: Marginal notes in the old book show how it was read.
examples.cn: 这本旧书上的页边注显示了它曾被怎样阅读。

examples.en: The policy did little for marginal communities.
examples.cn: 这项政策对边缘群体帮助甚微。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马挤脑」——马挤在栅栏最边上，只占一线之地，就是边缘的

root: 拉丁 margo、marginis「边缘、边界」→ 中世纪拉丁 marginalis「页边的」→ 英语 marginal；margo 更早的来源属重构，尚未确证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something at an edge: the rim of a page, the limit of significance, the border of society, the next unit of output, the line between win and loss, land or habitat at a limit, and a secondary role.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在边缘上：书页的边、意义的临界、社会的边界、产出的下一单位、胜负的分界、处于极限的土地或生境，以及次要的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip at the border, where a thing sits just inside the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：边界上一条窄带，事物正贴着界线内侧。

branches.en: THE PAGE SENSE: writing placed in the blank border.
branches.cn: 书页义：写在空白边栏里的文字。

branches.en: THE NUMERICAL EDGE: a difference barely worth counting, and a result decided by a tiny gap.
branches.cn: 数量边缘：几乎不值得计数的差别，以及以极小差距决出的结果。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL EDGE: people outside the centre of a society.
branches.cn: 社会边缘：处在社会中心之外的人。

branches.en: THE ECONOMIC EDGE: the extra cost or benefit of one more unit.
branches.cn: 经济边缘：再加一单位的额外成本或收益。

branches.en: THE LIMITS OF USE: land barely worth farming, habitat barely survivable, and a role barely central.
branches.cn: 使用极限：勉强可耕的地、勉强能活的生境，以及勉强算核心的角色。

intro.en: Marginal is built on Latin margo 'edge' with the adjective ending -al; English adds endings for manner, state and the act of pushing to the edge.
intro.cn: marginal 建立在拉丁 margo「边缘」与形容词词尾 -al 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与「推至边缘」动作的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Margo, marginis 'edge' gives the stem margin-, and Medieval Latin marginalis gives the adjective; English margin also comes from the same noun.
latinIntro.cn: margo、marginis「边缘」给出词干 margin-，中世纪拉丁 marginalis 给出形容词；英语的 margin 也出自同一名词。

items.example: The noun is the origin of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The stem appears in margin and marginal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 margin 与 marginal 中。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成形容词。

items.example: It first described writing in a page margin.
items.exampleCN: 它最初描述写在页边的文字。

items.example: English widened it to economics and society.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到经济学与社会。

items.example: The noun kept both the page and the arithmetic senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留书页与算术两义。

items.example: The suffix makes the comparison adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成比较副词。

items.example: The suffix names the condition of being at the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「处于边缘」的状况。

items.example: The suffix names the act of pushing to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「推到边缘」的动作。

items.example: The suffix names the process as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名整个过程。

senses.title: Of the body as a body
senses.definition: relating to an organization as a whole, rather than to one member, one department, or one activity
senses.definitionCN: 指某个组织整体，而不是其中某个成员、某个部门或某项活动
senses.example: The merger changed the organizational name but left the staff in place.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并改掉了组织名称，却把人员原样留了下来。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun organization into a describing word. It points at the body as a body, the way a label on a pen points at the pen rather than at the animals inside it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 organization 变成形容词。它指的是作为一个整体的机构，就像圈栏上的牌子指的是圈栏本身，而不是里面的牲畜。

senses.title: How the parts are arranged
senses.titleCN: 指内部层级与分工排列的
senses.definition: relating to the structure of an organization, especially the way roles, units, and levels are arranged under one another
senses.definitionCN: 指机构的内部结构，尤其是角色、单元与层级之间上下排列的方式
senses.example: A flat organizational structure puts few layers between the intern and the director.
senses.exampleCN: 扁平的组织结构让实习生和总监之间只隔很少的层级。
senses.why: The Greek source organon was a tool whose parts work together. Once the tool becomes a body of people, the adjective can describe the arrangement of those parts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源 organon 是一件各部分协同工作的工具。当这件工具变成一个由人组成的机构后，这个形容词就可以描述各部分如何排列。

senses.title: Of management and administration
senses.definition: relating to management, decision-making, and the daily running of an organization rather than to its technical work
senses.definitionCN: 指管理、决策与机构日常运转，而不是指机构所做的技术性工作
senses.example: The audit blamed organizational failures rather than individual dishonesty.
senses.exampleCN: 审计把问题归因于管理层面的失误，而不是个人的不诚实。
senses.why: Management is the hand that holds the tool. This sense marks whatever belongs to that hand — budgets, chains of approval, reporting lines — as opposed to the work the tool is meant to do.
senses.whyCN: 管理是握着这件工具的手。这个义项标记的是属于这只手的东西——预算、审批链、汇报线——而不是工具本身要完成的工作。

senses.title: Of arranging an event or task
senses.definition: relating to the work of planning and arranging people or things so that an activity can take place
senses.definitionCN: 指为了让某项活动得以举行而规划、安排人与物的那部分工作
senses.example: The festival's organizational work began nine months before the first ticket was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的筹备工作在第一张票卖出前九个月就开始了。
senses.why: Here the adjective points back to the verb organize. It names the labour of drawing the chart, not the body that appears once the chart is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词回指的是动词 organize。它命名的是画这张架构图的劳作，而不是图画好之后出现的那个机构。

senses.title: Of organized labour
senses.definition: relating to a trade union, or to workers acting together as one body in negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 指工会，或指工人在谈判中以一个整体共同行动的
senses.example: Organizational membership in the union rose sharply after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工之后，工会的组织成员人数大幅上升。
senses.why: A union is an organization in the plainest sense: workers gathered into one body. The adjective keeps that collective meaning and attaches it to labour rather than to management.
senses.whyCN: 工会是最字面意义上的组织：工人聚合成一个整体。这个形容词保留了这层集体含义，并把它挂到劳工一方，而不是管理层。

senses.title: Of organizational studies
senses.definition: relating to the academic study of how organizations behave, as in organizational psychology, organizational behaviour, and organizational theory
senses.definitionCN: 指对机构如何运作的学术研究，如组织心理学、组织行为学与组织理论
senses.example: She teaches organizational behaviour to first-year management students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给管理专业一年级学生讲授组织行为学。
senses.why: When a field takes the body itself as its object, the adjective enters the field's name. The subject is no longer how to run the tool but the regular patterns the tool shows.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科把机构本身当作研究对象时，这个形容词就进入了学科名称。研究对象不再是怎样使用这件工具，而是这件工具呈现出的规律。

senses.title: Of levels of biological organization
senses.definition: relating to the nested levels at which living matter is arranged, from molecules and cells up to organs and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 指生命物质由分子、细胞一直嵌套到器官与生态系统的各个层次
senses.example: Ecologists work at organizational levels above the single organism.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家研究的是单个生物体以上的组织层次。
senses.why: Biology kept the literal sense of organon: organs are the body's tools. The adjective then names the ladder of parts nested inside larger parts, which is the chart drawn by nature.
senses.whyCN: 生物学保留了 organon 的字面义：器官是身体的工具。这个形容词于是命名部分嵌套在更大整体里的阶梯，也就是大自然自己画出的那张架构图。

senses.title: Of a unit inside a system
senses.definition: relating to a named subdivision inside a computer directory or an administrative filing system
senses.definitionCN: 指计算机目录或行政档案体系中被命名的下级单元
senses.example: Create one organizational unit for each regional office in the directory.
senses.exampleCN: 在目录里为每个地区办事处建立一个组织单元。
senses.why: Software imitates the chart literally: an organizational unit is a box drawn inside a larger box. Here the word names a container in a hierarchy rather than a group of people.
senses.whyCN: 软件把架构图照字面模仿了一遍：组织单元就是画在更大方框里的一个方框。这里这个词命名的是层级中的一个容器，而不是一群真实的人。

senses.title: Good at putting things in order
senses.definition: of a person, able to plan and arrange work so that many parts move in order without confusion
senses.definitionCN: 指人能够规划并安排工作，使许多部分有序推进而不混乱
senses.example: Her organizational ability kept the archive from collapsing into piles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的统筹能力让档案室没有塌成一堆堆纸山。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the thing to the person who makes the thing. A skill is called organizational when it produces the chart in real life, with boxes that actually report to the boxes above them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从事物转到了制造事物的人身上。当一种本领能在现实里画出那张图、并且方框真的向它上面的方框汇报时，它就被称为组织能力。

intro.en: Organizational is the adjective of organization, built with the Latin suffix -alis (English -al). Organization comes from Medieval Latin organizatio, an action noun from organizare 'to organize', which rests on Latin organum 'instrument, implement, organ of the body'. Organum itself was borrowed from Greek organon 'tool, implement, organ', a derivative of ergon 'work'. The path is therefore 'tool' → 'body part that works like a tool' → 'parts arranged to work together' → 'an institution' → the English adjective.
intro.cn: organizational 是 organization 的形容词，由拉丁后缀 -alis（英语 -al）构成。organization 来自中世纪拉丁语 organizatio，是 organizare“组织”的动作名词，而 organizare 的基础是拉丁语 organum“工具、器具、身体器官”。organum 本身借自希腊语 organon“工具、器具、器官”，由 ergon“工作”派生。因此整条路径是“工具”→“像工具一样工作的身体部件”→“被安排协同工作的各部分”→“机构”→英语形容词。

items.en: Organon means 'tool, instrument, implement' and also 'organ of the body'. It derives from ergon 'work, deed', the same root that gives English energy and ergonomic.
items.cn: organon 意为“工具、器具、器械”，也指“身体器官”。它由 ergon“工作、行为”派生，同一词根还产生英语的 energy 与 ergonomic。

items.en: Latin borrowed organon as organum, widened it to 'musical instrument', and formed the verb organizare in medieval use, 'to furnish with organs, to arrange into a working body'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 organon 借作 organum，词义扩大到“乐器”，并在中世纪用法中造出动词 organizare，意为“装备器官、安排成一个能运转的整体”。

items.en: English organization first names the act of organizing and the state of being organized; the sense 'an organized body of persons, an institution' is established in the 17th century.
items.cn: 英语 organization 最初指“组织的行为”和“被组织起来的状态”；“由人组成的组织、机构”这一义项在 17 世纪确立。

items.en: The adjective organizational appears in the 19th century, at first in the language of institutions and administration, then spreading to psychology, biology, and computing in the 20th.
items.cn: 形容词 organizational 出现在 19 世纪，最初用于机构与行政语言，20 世纪又扩展到心理学、生物学与计算机领域。

items.en: The family is regular: organ + -ize (from Greek -izein through Latin -izare) makes the verb, -ation makes the action noun, -al makes the adjective, and -ally the adverb. Reorganization adds re- 'again'.
items.cn: 这个词族的构词很规则：organ 加 -ize（经拉丁 -izare 上溯希腊 -izein）构成动词，加 -ation 构成动作名词，加 -al 构成形容词，加 -ally 构成副词。reorganization 则再加 re-“再次”。

items.en: Organic and organism share the same organon root but took the 'living body' branch. By contrast, ornament comes from Latin ornare 'to adorn', and its orn- has nothing to do with organ-; the two only share a few letters at the front.
items.cn: organic 与 organism 共享同一个 organon 词根，只是走了“活体”这一支。相反，ornament 来自拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，其中的 orn- 与 organ- 毫无关系，两者只是词头碰巧相似。

note.en: The first group follows the organon root from tool to body part to institution, and separates one word that only looks similar. The second group compares the adjectives learners use when they mean 'about an institution' or 'about running it'.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 organon 词根，从工具走到身体部件再到机构，并区分一个只是形近的词。第二组比较学习者在表示“关于机构”或“关于管理”时最常替换的几个形容词。

entries.definition: a part of the body that performs a special function, or a musical instrument. It is the literal organon, the tool of the body, from which the institution sense grew.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中执行特定功能的部件，或指乐器。它就是字面的 organon——身体的工具，机构义正是从这里长出来的。

entries.definition: relating to living things or to food grown without chemicals. It follows the 'organ of the body' branch of organon rather than the 'arranged institution' branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关，或指不用化学物质种植的食物。它走的是 organon 中“身体器官”那一支，而不是“被安排好的机构”那一支。

entries.definition: the act of arranging parts into a working whole, or the body so formed. The adjective adds -al to this noun and simply means 'of such a body'.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分安排成一个能运转的整体的行为，或由此形成的机构。形容词只是在名词后加 -al，表示“属于这种机构的”。

entries.definition: a decorative object. Its root is Latin ornare 'to adorn', so the orn- resembles organ- only in spelling and shares no meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰品。它的词根是拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，所以 orn- 只在拼写上像 organ-，意义上毫无关联。

entries.definition: relating to a long-established body such as a university, bank, or hospital, often stressing its formal, slow-moving character. Organizational is neutral and can describe any body, including a new one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大学、银行、医院这类长期存在的机构，常强调其正式、迟缓的特征。organizational 是中性的，可以描述任何机构，包括刚成立的。

entries.definition: relating to the work of managing records, rules, and procedures. Organizational can cover culture, structure, and psychology as well as administration.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理记录、规则与程序的工作。organizational 除行政外，还可以涵盖文化、结构与心理层面。

entries.definition: relating to managers and their duties. It names one rank inside the body, while organizational can describe the whole body or its arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理者及其职责。它命名机构内部的一个层级，而 organizational 可以描述整个机构或其排列方式。

entries.definition: relating to a business corporation, often with a tone of large-scale commercial identity. Organizational is wider and applies to schools, charities, and unions too.
entries.definitionCN: 指商业公司，常带大型商业主体的语气。organizational 范围更广，也适用于学校、慈善机构与工会。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: organon 'tool', ergon 'work', the -ize/-ation/-al chain, the organ that gives the family its name, and the ornare trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：organon“工具”、ergon“工作”、-ize/-ation/-al 词缀链、给整个词族命名的 organ，以及 ornare 陷阱。

normal.en: Organon is Greek for 'tool'; an organization is a tool made of people, and organizational describes whatever belongs to that tool.
normal.cn: organon 是希腊语“工具”；organization 是一件由人做成的工具，organizational 则描述属于这件工具的一切。

normal.en: Organon comes from ergon 'work', the root behind energy: a tool is what does work, and an institution is a tool that does work through people.
normal.cn: organon 出自 ergon“工作”，也就是 energy 的词根：工具就是干活的东西，而机构是通过人来干活的工具。

normal.en: The suffixes stack in order: organ → organize (verb) → organization (noun) → organizational (adjective) → organizationally (adverb).
normal.cn: 后缀按顺序叠加：organ → organize（动词）→ organization（名词）→ organizational（形容词）→ organizationally（副词）。

normal.en: An organ is a body part that works like a tool; the same word moved from the body to the body of people, which is why 'organizational structure' sounds anatomical.
normal.cn: organ 是像工具一样工作的身体部件；同一个词从身体挪到了人的集合体，所以 organizational structure 听起来像在讲解剖。

normal.en: Ornament looks close but comes from ornare 'to adorn'; a decoration adds beauty, while an organization adds order.
normal.cn: ornament 看起来相近，但出自 ornare“装饰”；装饰增添美，而组织增添秩序。

abstract.en: A chart on a wall is only ink, yet people arrive at nine and leave at six because the boxes on it agree with one another.
abstract.cn: 墙上的架构图只是墨水，可人们九点来、六点走，只因图上的方框彼此对得上。

abstract.en: An orchestra needs a score, chairs, and a conductor; none of them makes music, but together they let the players do it.
abstract.cn: 管弦乐团需要总谱、座椅和指挥；这些东西都不演奏音乐，但合在一起才让乐手奏出音乐。

abstract.en: A library's shelf numbers do not read the books, but without them no reader finds a book; structure is invisible work.
abstract.cn: 图书馆的架号不读任何一本书，但没有它读者就找不到书；结构是一种看不见的劳动。

examples.en: The study found that organizational culture mattered more than pay.
examples.cn: 研究发现，组织文化比薪酬更重要。

examples.en: She was praised for her organizational skills during the conference.
examples.cn: 会议期间，她的统筹安排能力受到了称赞。

examples.en: The software stores each department as a separate organizational unit.
examples.cn: 该软件把每个部门存成一个独立的组织单元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥格耐贼」——奥格把散乱的人“摁”进一张格子图，一人一格，谁向谁汇报都写清楚 → organizational 组织结构的；有组织能力的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 organizare「组织」，基础是 organum「工具、器官」，再上溯希腊语 organon「工具、器官」，由 ergon「工作」派生；后缀为 -ation 与 -al。核心是「把散开的部件装成一件能干活的工具」。同族的 organic、organism 走“活体”一支，ornament（ornare「装饰」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of organizational all point at one drawing: scattered people and tasks fitted into a chart. What shifts is where the eye lands — on the body itself, on the lines between its boxes, on the hand that draws them, or on the skill of drawing.
sensesIntro.cn: organizational 的九个义项都指向同一张图：散乱的人与任务被装进一张架构图。变化的是视线落点——落在机构本身、落在方框之间的连线、落在画图的那只手上，还是落在画图的本领上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered people and tasks fitted into a drawn chart, each box marked with the box it reports to.
core.cn: 核心意象：散乱的人与任务被装进一张画好的架构图，每个方框都标明它向哪个方框汇报。

branches.en: THE BODY AND ITS LINES: the institution as a whole, and the hierarchy of roles and units inside it.
branches.cn: 机构与连线：作为整体的机构，以及其内部角色与单元的层级。

branches.en: THE HAND: management and administration, and the planning labour that arranges an event before it happens.
branches.cn: 那只手：管理与行政，以及活动发生之前的筹备劳作。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE BRANCH: workers gathered into a union, the body as a bargaining unit.
branches.cn: 集体分支：工人聚成工会，机构成为谈判单位。

branches.en: THE STUDY OF THE BODY: organizational psychology, behaviour, and theory take the chart itself as the object.
branches.cn: 对机构的研究：组织心理学、组织行为学与组织理论把这张图本身当作研究对象。

branches.en: NESTED AND PERSONAL: levels of biological organization, a unit inside a directory, and the personal skill that produces order.
branches.cn: 嵌套与个人：生物组织层次、目录中的组织单元，以及产生秩序的个人能力。

intro.en: Organizational is not a Latin word: it is English organization plus the Latin adjective ending -alis. The Latin core sits underneath, organum < Greek organon 'tool'. The family is built by regular suffix stacking rather than by new prefixes.
intro.cn: organizational 不是拉丁词：它是英语 organization 加拉丁形容词词尾 -alis。拉丁内核在其下方，即 organum < 希腊语 organon“工具”。这个词族靠规则的后缀叠加而建成，没有另加新前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer contains organum 'instrument', organizare 'to arrange into a working body', and organizatio 'arrangement'. Behind organum is Greek organon 'tool', from ergon 'work'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层包含 organum“工具”、organizare“安排成能运转的整体”、organizatio“安排”。organum 背后是希腊语 organon“工具”，再上溯 ergon“工作”。

items.meaningCN: 属于某个被组织起来的机构的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The organizational chart lists every reporting line.
items.exampleCN: 组织架构图列出了每一条汇报线。

items.meaning: the act of arranging parts, or the body so arranged
items.meaningCN: 安排各部分的行为，或由此形成的机构（-ation 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The organization has three regional offices.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构有三个地区办事处。

items.meaning: to furnish with parts and set them working together
items.meaningCN: 给事物配备部件并使其协同运转；组织（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: They organized the files by year and by author.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年份和作者整理文件。

items.meaning: a person who arranges an event, or a container that keeps things in order
items.meaningCN: 安排活动的人，或使物品有条理的收纳盒（-er 施动者）
items.example: The conference organizer sent the schedule by email.
items.exampleCN: 会议组织者通过邮件发来了日程。

items.meaning: a body part with a special function, or a musical instrument
items.meaningCN: 有特定功能的器官，或乐器
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: of living bodies, or grown without chemical inputs
items.meaningCN: 与生物体有关的，或不用化学投入物种植的（-ic 形容词）
items.example: The farm sells organic vegetables.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场出售有机蔬菜。

items.meaning: in terms of the way an institution is arranged
items.meaningCN: 从机构安排的角度来说（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: The two units are organizationally separate.
items.exampleCN: 这两个单位在组织上是分开的。

items.meaning: a fresh arranging of an existing body

items.example: The reorganization merged two departments.
items.exampleCN: 这次改组把两个部门合并了。

items.meaning: lacking order, with parts not fitted together

items.example: His desk was disorganized but his notes were exact.

intro.en: Efficacy is Latin efficacia, the power of accomplishing, built on efficax, able to accomplish, which rests on efficere, to work out.
intro.cn: efficacy 就是拉丁语 efficacia（办成事情的能力），建立在 efficax（能办成的）之上，而 efficax 又来自 efficere（做出、促成）。

items.en: Latin efficere means to work out or bring about.
items.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 意为做出、促成。

items.en: Latin efficax means able to accomplish, with the stem efficac-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 efficax 意为能办成的，词干为 efficac-。

items.en: The noun efficacia names the power of accomplishing.
items.cn: 名词 efficacia 指办成事情的能力。

items.en: English borrowed efficacy in the 14C for the power to produce an effect.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 efficacy，指产生效果的能力。

items.en: Doctors used efficacy for the strength of a remedy.
items.cn: 医生用 efficacy 指药方的效力。

items.en: Clinical trials turned vaccine efficacy into a measurable percentage.
items.cn: 临床试验使疫苗效力成为可测量的百分比。

note.en: Efficacy and efficiency share the Latin root facere, to do, but efficacy asks whether the result comes while efficiency asks how little effort it costs.
note.cn: efficacy 与 efficiency 共用拉丁词根 facere（做），但 efficacy 问结果有没有出来，efficiency 问花了多少力气。

dict_mnemonic.text: efficacy ＝ ef-（向外）＋ fic（做，拉丁 facere）＋ -acy（名词后缀，表性质）＝「能做出来的性质」。同一词根换词尾：-acious → efficacious 灵验的（形容词，常修饰药物、疗法）；-acy → efficacy 功效（名词，不可数为主）；-iency → efficiency 效率。记住这条分工：efficacy 只问「有没有用」，efficiency 还问「省不省」，effectiveness 是日常口语里最常用的「有效性」。医学语境里 efficacy 特指理想试验条件下的效力，落到真实人群则常说 effectiveness。搭配记 clinical efficacy 临床疗效、vaccine efficacy 疫苗效力、prove the efficacy 证明功效。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ facere（做）→ efficax（能办成的）→ efficacia（功效）→ efficacy

senses.title: The ability to read and write
senses.definition: the basic ability to read and write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 读懂并写出简短浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Literacy opens the first door that poverty had shut.
senses.exampleCN: 读写能力打开了贫困关上的第一道门。
senses.why: the noun was built on the Latin word for a letter of the alphabet, so its oldest content is simply knowing one's letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建在拉丁语「字母」一词上，因此它最古老的内容就是「认识字母」。

senses.title: The measured level in a population
senses.titleCN: 一个人群中被统计的识字程度
senses.definition: the share of a population that can read and write, treated as a figure to be counted
senses.definitionCN: 能够读写者在人口中所占的比例，被当作可统计的数字
senses.example: Literacy in the province rose from half to four fifths in one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个省的识字水平在一代人之内从一半升至五分之四。
senses.why: once states began to measure the skill, the word also named the number rather than the ability.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家开始测量这项技能，这个词也就指数字而非能力。

senses.title: Functional literacy for daily tasks
senses.titleCN: 应付日常事务的实用读写能力
senses.definition: the reading and writing needed to fill in forms, follow instructions and manage a household
senses.definitionCN: 填写表格、看懂指示、料理家务所需的读写能力
senses.example: The course targets functional literacy rather than exam skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课针对的是日常实用读写能力，而不是应试技巧。
senses.why: policy shifted focus from letters to use, so the old word acquired a practical measure.
senses.whyCN: 政策重心从「认字」转向「会用」，这个旧词由此带上实用尺度。

senses.title: Digital literacy
senses.titleCN: 使用数字工具与判断网络信息的能力
senses.definition: the ability to use computers and networks and to judge what one finds there
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机与网络，并判断所见信息的能力
senses.example: Students need digital literacy before they can research online.
senses.exampleCN: 学生要先具备数字素养，才能在网络上做研究。
senses.why: the pattern of basic competence in a domain was extended from print to screens.
senses.whyCN: 「某领域的基本能力」这一模式从纸面扩展到了屏幕。

senses.title: Financial literacy
senses.titleCN: 看懂收支、利率与风险的能力
senses.definition: the ability to understand money, interest, debt and risk well enough to decide wisely
senses.definitionCN: 理解金钱、利率、债务与风险并据以明智决策的能力
senses.example: Schools now teach financial literacy alongside mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 学校如今把金融素养与数学一起教。
senses.why: the same frame applies wherever a field has codes that outsiders cannot read.
senses.whyCN: 只要某领域有一套外人读不懂的规则，这个框架就适用。

senses.title: Media literacy
senses.titleCN: 识别媒体信息意图与可信度的能力
senses.definition: the ability to read how news and advertising are built, and to judge their reliability
senses.definitionCN: 看懂新闻与广告如何被构造，并判断其可信度的能力
senses.example: Media literacy helps readers notice what a headline leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体素养帮助读者察觉标题省略了什么。
senses.why: news and advertising are constructed texts, so reading them needs the same skill as reading print.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与广告都是被构造的文本，读懂它们需要与读印刷品相同的功夫。

senses.title: Cultural literacy
senses.titleCN: 共享文化常识的通晓程度
senses.definition: the shared background knowledge that lets people understand references and jokes
senses.definitionCN: 使人能理解典故与玩笑的共同背景知识
senses.example: Cultural literacy includes knowing why a certain date matters.
senses.exampleCN: 文化素养包括知道某个日期为何重要。
senses.why: the word widened from letters to the common stock of references a society assumes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「字母」扩展到社会默认人人共有的典故储备。

senses.title: Literacy in a specialized field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业领域的基本通晓
senses.definition: working knowledge of the basic ideas and vocabulary of a subject such as science or law
senses.definitionCN: 对科学、法律等学科的基本概念与术语具备可用知识
senses.example: Scientific literacy is now treated as part of general education.
senses.exampleCN: 科学素养如今被视为通识教育的一部分。
senses.why: a subject's basic vocabulary works like an alphabet, so the same word fits it.
senses.whyCN: 某学科的基本词汇就像一套字母，因此同一个词也适用于它。

intro.en: Literacy is English literate plus the noun ending -cy, and literate goes back to Latin litteratus 'lettered', built on littera 'letter of the alphabet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语形容词「识字的」上加名词后缀构成，而该形容词上溯拉丁 litteratus「识字的」，后者建于 littera「字母」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet; in the plural it also meant a written message or writings in general. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母；复数时也指书信或一般著作。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus meant 'marked with letters, lettered, learned', an adjective formed from the noun.
items.cn: litteratus 意为「写有字母的、识字的、有学问的」，是由该名词构成的形容词。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fifteenth century, using it first for learned people and later for anyone able to read.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，先用于有学问的人，后用于任何能读书的人。

items.en: The noun is a nineteenth-century formation, made as the positive counterpart of illiteracy when mass schooling made the skill a public question.
items.cn: 这个名词是十九世纪的构词，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法而造，当时大众教育使识字成为公共议题。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word was attached to new fields, giving digital, financial, media and scientific literacy.
items.cn: 从二十世纪后期起，这个词被挂到新的领域上，形成数字、金融、媒体与科学素养等说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the word for a letter is unknown, and the exact first printed use of the modern noun is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个现代名词最早的确切印刷书证亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same letter-root that are easily swapped; group two holds neighbours naming competence.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「字母」词根、容易用错的词；第二组是表示能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a person or society that can read; the noun names the ability itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能读写的个人或社会；名词则指能力本身。

entries.definition: The body of written works, or the published material on a subject; it is the product, not the ability.
entries.definitionCN: 指成体系的著作，或某主题的已发表文献；是产物而非能力。

entries.definition: Meaning 'following the exact words'; it shares the letter-root but has nothing to do with reading skill.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，虽共享「字母」词根，却与读写能力无关。

entries.definition: The lack of the ability; it is the negative noun built with a prefix of negation.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏这种能力，是用否定前缀构成的反面名词。

entries.definition: Basic competence with numbers, coined on the model of literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数字的基本能力，仿照「读写能力」造出。

entries.definition: The broad process of schooling; literacy is one measurable part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛的学校教育过程；读写能力是其中可测量的一部分。

entries.definition: A general word for a high level of skill in something; it carries no link to letters.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某项技能的高水平，不含与「字母」的联系。

entries.definition: The sufficiency to perform a task; it is broader and less measurable than literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以完成任务的能力，范围更广，且不如读写能力那样可测量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'letter', so the core of the word is literally knowing one's letters.
normal.cn: 词根意为「字母」，因此这个词的核心字面上就是「认识字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the newer fields: digital, financial and media literacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出较新的领域：数字素养、金融素养与媒体素养。

normal.en: The noun pairs with its negative twin, one built with a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 这个名词与它的否定孪生词配对，后者由否定前缀构成。

normal.en: The family runs literate, illiterate, literature, literal, literacy.
normal.cn: 同族包括「识字的」「不识字的」「文学」「字面的」「读写能力」。

normal.en: The phrase 'literacy campaign' keeps the public-policy sense visible.
normal.cn: 「扫盲运动」这一说法让公共政策义保持可见。

abstract.en: Picture a key that fits many doors but was cut for one lock first.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能开许多门的钥匙，最初却只为一把锁而削。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lets a reader walk through a dark room without falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，让读者走过暗室而不摔倒。

abstract.en: Picture a currency accepted in every shop, learned one letter at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一种每个店铺都收的货币，是一个字母一个字母学来的。

examples.en: Literacy among women rose fastest where evening classes were free.
examples.cn: 在夜校免费的地方，女性识字率上升最快。

examples.en: Digital literacy is now as basic as reading a timetable.
examples.cn: 数字素养如今已和看懂时刻表一样基础。

examples.en: The campaign cut adult illiteracy by half in six years.
examples.cn: 这场运动在六年内把成人文盲率降低了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特乐西」——里里外外认得那些特小的字母，心里就乐，这就是读写能力。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」构成形容词 litteratus「识字的」；英语先借入形容词，十九世纪再加名词后缀构成 literacy，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one seed: knowing letters becomes the ability to read, then a number to count, then a set of practical competences that spread to screens, money, news and finally to any field with its own codes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一粒种子长出：认识字母变成读写能力，再变成可统计的数字，随后成为一套实用能力，扩展到屏幕、金钱、新闻，最后延伸到任何有自身规则的专业领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short pencil pressed on a page beside a signed form.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支削短的铅笔压在纸页上，旁边是一份签过名的表格。

branches.en: THE SEED: knowing letters is the oldest and simplest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 种子：认识字母是这个词最古老也最简单的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED: a state can turn the ability into a percentage, and the word follows.
branches.cn: 被计数：国家能把能力换算成百分比，词义也随之跟进。

branches.en: USING IT: forms and instructions on one side, a discipline's vocabulary on the other.
branches.cn: 会用：一边是表格与说明，另一边是某学科的专业词汇。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: screens and headlines each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新媒介：屏幕与标题各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: CODES OF THE WORLD: money and shared culture are also systems one must learn to read.
branches.cn: 世界的密码：金钱与共同文化同样是必须学会读懂的体系。

intro.en: The word is a short English noun built on a Latin root for a letter, with a suffix of state or quality.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的英语名词，建在拉丁语表「字母」的词根上，并带一个表状态或性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, letters and literature in English, while litteratus gives literate and, with a negating prefix, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 在英语里衍生出「字母」「书信」与「文学」，litteratus 则衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀又有「不识字的」。

items.meaning: a letter; writings in the plural
items.meaningCN: 字母；复数指书信或著作
items.example: The root names the smallest unit of written language.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指书面语言的最小单位。

items.meaning: a written sign for a speech sound
items.example: A single letter can change a whole meaning.
items.exampleCN: 一个字母就能改变整个意思。

items.example: The village is almost wholly literate now.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子如今几乎人人识字。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy was made a national target.
items.exampleCN: 识字被定为国家目标。

items.example: The forms were useless to illiterate tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些表格对不识字的租户毫无用处。

items.example: She read the literature on soil erosion.
items.exampleCN: 她读了关于土壤侵蚀的文献。

items.example: A literal translation missed the joke.
items.exampleCN: 直译丢掉了那个玩笑。

items.example: He was a man of letters in the old sense.
items.exampleCN: 在旧时的意义上，他是个文人。
